Job Description - Postdoctoral Research Associate (26001358)
Job Description
 
Postdoctoral Research Associate (Job Number: 26001358)
Department of Physics
Grade 7: - £39,560 - £41,885 per annum
Fixed Term - Full Time
Contract Duration: 24 months
Contracted Hours per Week: 35
Working Arrangements: TBC
Closing Date: 15-Nov-2026, 11:59:00 PM
Disclosure and Barring Service Requirement: Not Applicable.
 

Working at Durham University  

A globally outstanding centre of teaching and research excellence, a warm and friendly place to work, a unique and historic setting – Durham is a university like no other.

As one of the UK’s leading universities, Durham is an incredible place to define your career. The University is located within a beautiful historic city, home to a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and surrounded by stunning countryside. Our talented scholars and researchers from around the world are tackling global issues and making a difference to people's lives.  

We believe that inspiring our people to do outstanding things at Durham enables Durham people to do outstanding things in the world. Being a part of Durham is about more than just the success of the University, it’s also about contributing to the success of the city, county and community.

Our University Strategy is built on three pillars of research, education and wider student experience, but also on our keen sense of community and of inspiring others to achieve their potential. 

Our Purpose and Values

We want our University to be a place where people can be free to be themselves, no matter what their identity or background. Together, we celebrate difference, value one another and are each responsible for creating an inclusive community that is respectful and fair for all.

Find out more about the benefits of working at the University and what it is like to live and work in the Durham area on our Why Join Us? - Information Page

The Role and Department
A World Top 100 department in the 2025 QS subject rankings, our research spans advanced instrumentation, astronomy and astrophysics, condensed matter physics, cosmology, particle physics and quantum physics. It has real‑world impact, informing developments in energy storage, improved cancer imaging, quantum computing, nuclear fusion, pandemic modelling and faster digital technologies. We pride ourselves on closely aligning our teaching with the University’s research‑intensive ethos. Research‑led learning is embedded at every stage of our undergraduate programmes—from first‑year laboratory reports to our flagship final‑year MPhys individual research projects—ensuring our students develop the skills and insight needed for future roles in STEM.

The successful candidate will join the Quantum Light and Matter (QLM) research section, a vibrant community working on the forefront of quantum science and technology, with experimental activities spanning cold atoms and molecules, thermal vapours and solid-state systems. Complementary theory activities and excellent technical support, together with an strong national and international network provide the ideal environment for cutting-edge experimental quantum science and technology.   

The Role

We are recruiting a Postdoctoral Research Associate on the project ‘Quantum networking at telecom wavelengths with Yb qubits’. The research project is funded by the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC) and led by EPSRC Quantum Technology fellow Dr Tobias Franzen. The project aims to develop a key technology for future quantum networks by combining arrays of single Yb atoms as a leading qubit platform with long-distance quantum networking over existing telecom fibre infrastructure. Possible applications include the scaling of neutral-atom quantum computing through distributed computing, as well as new tests of fundamental physics, such as exploring the interplay of general relativity and quantum mechanics through experiments with entangled clocks separated in space.

To realise this vision, we are working on a modular ytterbium tweezer-array platform, compact laser setups, and cavity-enhanced atom-photon interfaces for efficient remote entanglement generation over telecom-wavelength optical fibre links.

We are seeking an ambitious and highly motivated researcher with a background in AMO physics, quantum optics, or related fields. The successful applicant will work closely with Dr Tobias Franzen to realise the projects goals. They will be expected to take an active role in all aspects of the project, contributing directly to the experiment and working with national and international collaborators, undergraduate and graduate students, other members of the research group and technical staff.

The post holder will be expected to display the initiative, creativity, skills and knowledge required to advance the project. They need to work effectively both independently and as part of a small research team to solve technical and scientific challenges. It is expected that the successful applicant will enhance the international contacts of the group through the presentation of work at international conferences. The post holder will also be expected to aid in the supervision of graduate students within the group as well as contributing to the undergraduate teaching within the Department.

The postdoctoral researcher will have opportunities to develop scientific leadership, build international collaborations, contribute to grant proposals and supervise students.

Key responsibilities:

To understand and convey material of a specialist or highly technical nature to the team or group of people through presentations and discussions that leads to the presentation of research papers in conferences and publications.

To prepare and deliver presentations on research outputs/activities to audiences which may include: research sponsors, academic and non-academic audiences.
To publish high quality outputs, including papers for submission to peer reviewed journals and papers for presentation at conferences and workshops under the direction of the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder.
To assist with the development of research objectives and proposals.
To conduct individual and collaborative research projects under the direction of the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder.
To work with the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder and other colleagues in the research group, as appropriate, to identify areas for research, develop new research methods and extend the research portfolio.
To deal with problems that may affect the achievement of research objectives and deadlines by discussing with the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder and offering creative or innovative solutions.
To liaise with research colleagues and make internal and external contacts to develop knowledge and understanding to form relationships for future research collaboration.
To plan and manage own research activity, research resources in collaboration with others and contribute to the planning of research projects.
To deliver training in research techniques/approaches to peers, visitors and students as appropriate.
To be involved in student supervision, as appropriate, and assist with the assessment of the knowledge of students.
To contribute to fostering a collegial and respectful working environment which is inclusive and welcoming and where everyone is treated fairly with dignity and respect.
To engage in wider citizenship to support the department and wider discipline.

To engage in continuing professional development by participation in the undergraduate or postgraduate teaching programmes or by membership of departmental committees, etc. and by attending relevant training and development courses.   

 

The appointment will initially be made for 24 months, with the possibility for extension subject to performance and funding availability.

The post-holder is employed to work on research/a research project which will be led by another colleague. Whilst this means that the post-holder will not be carrying out independent research in his/her own right, the expectation is that they will contribute to the advancement of the project, through the development of their own research ideas/adaptation and development of research protocols.

The starting date is flexible, with the successful candidate ideally being in post by April 2027.

Working at Durham 

A competitive salary is only one part of the many fantastic benefits you will receive if you join the University:

You’ll receive 30 days annual leave per year in addition to 8 public holidays and 4 customary days per year – a total of 42 days per year. The University closes between Christmas and New Year.

We offer a generous pension scheme, and as a new member of staff you will be automatically enrolled into the University Superannuation Scheme (USS).

No matter how you travel to work, we have you covered.  We have ample parking across campus, a cycle to work scheme which helps you to buy a bike and discount with local bus and train companies. You can also take advantage of our cost-effective and environmentally friendly Tusker Car Benefit Scheme, allowing you to lease a brand-new electric or hybrid vehicle with savings on tax and National Insurance.

We have a genuine commitment to developing our colleagues professionally and personally.  There is a comprehensive range of development courses, apprenticeships and access to qualifications and routes to develop your career in the University.  All staff have dedicated annual time to concentrate on their personal development opportunities.

We provide wide-ranging health and wellbeing support including discounted membership for our state-of-the-art sport and gym facilities and access to a 24-7 Employee Assistance Programme.

Our on-site nursery is rated Outstanding by Ofsted, and you can access holiday camps for children aged 5-16.

Our family-friendly policies, including maternity and adoption leave, are among the most generous in the higher education sector (and likely above and beyond many employers).

We offer all staff the opportunity to take part in volunteering activities to make a difference in the local community.

You can access exclusive discounts via our benefits portal including money off at supermarkets, high street retailers, IT products such as Apple, eating out and days out at various attractions.

Various salary sacrifice schemes are also available to help you take advantage of tax savings on benefits.

If you are moving to Durham, you may be eligible for help with removal costs, and we have a dedicated team who can help you with the practicalities such as house hunting and schools.  If you need a visa, we cover most visa costs and offer an interest-free loan scheme to pay for dependant visas.

Discover more about our total rewards and benefits package here.

Durham University is committed to equality, diversity and inclusion

Equality, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) are a key component of the University’s Strategy and a central part of everything we do.  We also live by our Purpose and Values and our Staff Code of Conduct.  At Durham we actively work towards providing an environment where our staff and students can study, work and live in a community which is supportive and inclusive.

We welcome and encourage applications from those who are currently under-represented in our work force, including people with disabilities and from racially minoritised ethnic groups.

If you have taken a career break or periods of leave that may have impacted on the volume and recency of your research outputs and other activities, such as maternity, adoption or parental leave, you may wish to disclose this in your application. The selection committee will take this into account when evaluating your application.

The University has been awarded the Disability Confident Leader status. If you are a candidate with a disability, we are committed to ensuring fair treatment throughout the recruitment process. We will make adjustments to support the interview process wherever it is reasonable to do so and, where successful, reasonable adjustments will be made to support people within their role. 

Contact Information 

Department contact for academic-related enquiries 

Dr Tobias Franzen, Assistant Professor (Research), tobias.franzen@durham.ac.uk

Contact information for technical difficulties when submitting your application 

If you encounter technical difficulties when using the online application form, we prefer you send enquiries by email.  Please send your name along with a brief description of the problem you’re experiencing to e.recruitment@durham.ac.uk 

Alternatively, you may call 0191 334 6801 from the UK, or +44 191 334 6801 from outside the UK. This number operates during the hours of 09.00 and 17.00 Monday to Friday, UK time.  We will normally respond within one working day (Monday to Friday, excluding UK public holidays).  

How to Apply  

To progress to the assessment stage, candidates must evidence each of the essential criteria required for the role in the person specification below. It will be at the discretion of the recruiting panel as to whether they will also consider any desirable criteria, but we would urge candidates to provide evidence for all criteria.  

While some criteria will be considered at the shortlisting stage, other criteria may be considered later in the assessment process, such as questions at interview.  

Submitting your application 

We prefer to receive applications online.   We will update you about your application at various points throughout the selection process, via automated emails from our e-recruitment system. Please check your spam/junk folder periodically to make sure you have not missed any of our updates.

What to Submit 

All applicants are asked to submit: 

a CV and cover letter which details your experience, skills, and achievements in meeting (or the potential to meet) the criteria set out below.

Next Steps 

Short-listed candidates will be invited to the University, either virtually or in-person and will have the opportunity to meet key members of the Department.  The assessment for the post will normally include a short presentation followed by an interview and we anticipate that the interviews will take place in or around November 2026. 

In the event that you are unable to attend in person on the date offered, it may not be possible to offer you an interview on an alternative date. 

Please note that in submitting your application Durham University will be processing your data. We would ask you to consider the relevant University Privacy Statement Job Applicants/Potential Job Applicants - Durham University which provides information on the collation, storing and use of data.   

Durham University is a UKVI sponsor. Applicants who require sponsorship to work in the UK should note that not all roles are eligible. Further information on visa requirements and eligibility can be found on the UKVI website.

Person Specification 

Essential Criteria:

Qualifications

A good first degree in physics or a related subject.
A PhD (or be close to submission) in AMO physics or a related subject.

Experience

Experience in conducting high quality academic research.
Demonstrable ability to write material of a quality commensurate with publication in highly-ranked journals.
Demonstrable ability to present research papers at conferences and communicate complex information to specialists and within the wider academic community.
Experience in experimental AMO physics. 

Skills

Demonstrable ability to work cooperatively as part of a team, including participating in research meetings.
Ability to work independently on own initiative and to strict deadlines.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
Experimental experience with with single atoms or ions, quantum optics, cavity QED or a related area.
Experience with optical systems (especially frequency stabilisation, spectroscopy, photonic interfaces, or optical cavities) and related experimental techniques.

Desirable Criteria

Experience

12. Strong publication record in peer-reviewed journals, commensurate with stage of career.

13. A track record of presenting research at conferences, symposia, or meetings, commensurate with stage of career.

14. Demonstrable ability to develop research proposals and designs in collaboration with other academics.

15. Experience of overseeing students with respect to the development of their practical/research skills e.g. acting as a demonstrator; supervising student projects/practicals.

16. Experience designing, building, operating and troubleshooting complex experimental apparatus.

17. Experience with one or more of the following: micro-cavities, cavity-QED, light-matter interfaces, laser cooling of atoms, molecules or ions, optical tweezers.

Skills

18. Demonstrable ability to plan and manage independent research. 

19. Design, setup and alignment and operation of scientific laser setups.

20. Basic knowledge of lab electronics.

21. Programming for experiment control and data analysis.

	
 

 

We welcome applications from candidates with disabilities, neurodiversity and long-term health conditions, and we are committed to ensuring fair treatment throughout the recruitment process.

About the role

Build the Next Generation of Health Policy Simulation Models

Do you want your research to influence how governments design policies to prevent chronic disease? Are you excited by the challenge of combining data, simulation, and policy to tackle the world’s biggest health problems?

The Centre for Health Economics & Policy Innovation (CHEPI) at Imperial Business School is seeking a Research Associate / Research Fellow in Computational Health Policy Modelling to play a central role in developing Health-GPS — our state-of-the-art microsimulation model for non-communicable disease (NCD) policy analysis. Appointment will be made at Research Associate or Research Fellow level, depending on experience.

Why This Role Matters

Chronic diseases such as diabetes and cardiovascular disease remain leading causes of illness and premature death worldwide. Yet, the tools available to evaluate and design effective prevention policies are still evolving. Health-GPS provides a framework to explore how changes in diet, physical activity, and related risk factors affect long-term population health and economic outcomes.

Health-GPS represents the gradual accumulation and interaction of individual-level risk factors — such as BMI, diet, and income — offering insights into the potential impact of different policy interventions over time.

You will help develop and apply this model across major international projects including:

GOLDFINCH – estimating the effects of fiscal policies on ultra-processed food consumption.
JA Prevent NCD – a European Joint Action on integrated strategies for NCD prevention.
JACARDI – a European initiative to reduce cardiovascular and diabetes risk.

Working with economists, epidemiologists, and data scientists, you’ll push the boundaries of policy simulation and shape real-world decision-making.

This is a hands-on computational role. Alongside using Health-GPS for policy analysis, you will write, test and review code in its C++ codebase, working within the team’s collaborative development workflow (version control, pull requests and code review). C++ experience is highly desirable, but we also welcome strong programmers in other relevant languages who are willing to work in C++.

What you would be doing

Contribute to the architecture, development, optimisation, and maintenance of Health-GPS, writing and reviewing code in its C++ codebase and ensuring its continued scientific and policy relevance.
Work with colleagues to plan and deliver modelling work across multiple projects, producing high-quality outputs on time.
Help integrate new methodologies, including AI and machine-learning approaches, into simulation design.
Conduct quantitative analyses to estimate the health and economic impact of proposed policies.
Identify and manage relevant datasets in collaboration with internal and external partners.
Communicate findings through academic papers, policy briefs, and stakeholder workshops.
Contribute to funding proposals and the expansion of CHEPI’s modelling activities.

What we are looking for

We’re seeking a creative and technically strong individual with:

A PhD (or equivalent, or near completion) in health economics, epidemiology, computer science, or a related field.
Experience building or using microsimulation models or other quantitative policy tools.
Strong programming skills in at least one language (e.g. Python, R, or C++), and experience contributing to a shared codebase using version control (e.g. git).
Experience working with large or longitudinal datasets.
The ability to translate complex model outputs into actionable policy insights.
Curiosity, independence, and enthusiasm for multidisciplinary collaboration.

Experience with C++ is highly desirable. Experience applying AI or ML methods to health or policy modelling is also desirable.

Candidates for appointment as Research Fellow should also demonstrate a strong publication record, experience contributing to funding proposals, and the ability to design and lead original research.

What we can offer you

The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to use science for humanity.
Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression.
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes).
Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

Further information

Interested? Apply online with:

A cover letter explaining your motivation and relevant experience, and indicating the level (Research Associate or Research Fellow) for which you are applying.
Your CV.
Contact details for two referees.

This position is full-time and fixed-term for 24 months, with potential for extension depending on funding. Start date: as soon as possible.

For queries about the post, contact Prof. Franco Sassi (f.sassi@imperial.ac.uk).

About the role

Could your expertise in computational modelling, neutronics or AI methods help design and manage the nuclear reactors of tomorrow as a Research Associate in Applied Nuclear Computation? Working within Imperial College London's world-leading Applied Modelling & Computation Group (AMCG), you will apply advanced numerical, physics-based and data-driven methods to one or two exciting and complementary projects: an industry-funded digital engineering platform focused on the design and optimisation of a novel thorium reactor, and a UKRI-backed agentic digital ecosystem supporting the full lifecycle of next-generation High-Temperature Gas-Cooled Reactors (HTGRs).

What you would be doing

As a Research Associate in the AMCG, you will contribute to internationally leading research, taking the initiative in planning and executing your own scientific work to contribute to the broader goals of two cutting-edge nuclear projects.

You will develop and apply advanced computational, numerical and physics-based methods, ensuring the validity and reliability of your data and maintaining meticulous records of your findings throughout. Your work will span the full research cycle — from identifying and developing appropriate techniques for data collection and analysis, to writing reports for research sponsors, submitting publications to high-quality refereed journals, and presenting your findings at national and international conferences.

You will also have the opportunity to lead and mentor, directing small research teams and providing guidance to PhD students and research assistants, helping to shape the next generation of computational scientists.

Collaboration will be at the heart of your role, as you build and maintain relationships with allied researchers both within Imperial College and across the wider international community, contributing to grant bids and actively participating in group meetings and seminars. In everything you do, you will be expected to uphold the highest standards of research integrity, safety and professionalism, promoting the reputation of the AMCG, the Department and Imperial College London as a whole.

What we are looking for

With up to three posts available, we welcome applicants from a broad range of disciplines — including applied mathematical modelling, computational mathematics, reactor physics and AI — who are eager to bring their technical expertise to one of the most important clean energy challenges of our time. In particular, you will have:

 

A strong computational and numerical foundation — you hold a PhD (or have equivalent experience) in Applied Mathematics, Physics, Nuclear Engineering or a closely related computational discipline, and have hands-on experience developing software implementing discretisation methods such as Finite Element or Finite Volume approaches. (Note: Candidates who have not yet been officially awarded their PhD will be appointed as Research Assistant.)
Scientific programming proficiency — you are confident writing and deploying scientific code in one or more of Fortran, C/C++ or Python, ideally with experience developing and running codes in High Performance Computing (HPC) environments.
Familiarity with reactor physics methods and tools — experience with neutronics, fuel cycle or burnup/depletion modelling — whether through codes such as OpenMC, Serpent, MCNP, WIMS or SCALE, or through knowledge of advanced reactor concepts such as HTGRs or thorium systems — is highly advantageous, though not essential.
An interest in or exposure to AI and data-driven modelling — experience applying machine learning or reduced-order modelling techniques to physics problems, such as training neural networks on simulation data, would be a valuable addition to our multidisciplinary team.
A track record of research delivery and communication — you can demonstrate experience working in a research environment, with the ability to write clearly for publication, present confidently at conferences, and engage effectively with both academic collaborators and industry partners.
A proactive, collaborative and organised approach to work — you are able to manage your own research programme with appropriate supervision, prioritise effectively against deadlines, and contribute positively to a team environment, including supporting and motivating junior researchers and students.

What we can offer you

The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity.
Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression.
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 41 days off a year and generous pension schemes).
Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

Further information

This is a fixed term post for up to 33 months.

If you require any further details about the role, please contact Chris Pain - c.pain@imperial.ac.uk

About the role

Are you a robot learning researcher eager to push the boundaries of dexterous manipulation? Join DexLab at Imperial College London, led by Dr. Rolandos Potamias and Stefanos Zafeiriou, in a postdoctoral research role to lead transformative projects spanning robot foundation models and real-world dexterous manipulation. 

DexLab at Imperial is seeking a highly motivated and talented Postdoctoral Research Associate (PDRA / PostDoc) who has demonstrated competence in conducting cutting-edge robot learning research. The position focuses on building dexterous, high-degree-of-freedom (high-DoF) manipulation policies and robot foundation models, such as vision-language-action models (VLAs), learned from human demonstrations, but is not limited to this. The successful candidate will work on a state-of-the-art robotic platform comprising Sharpa Wave dexterous hands and UR7e arms, contributing both to methodological advances and to the deployment of learned policies on real robots. To this end, the role integrates knowledge from robot learning, computer vision, generative modelling and control. 

What you would be doing

The post will focus on research topics in probabilistic programming. The specific details of the project are flexible and will be determined based on the interests and strengths of the successful candidate.  

You will conduct original research at the intersection of dexterous manipulation, robot learning and foundation models, exploring how large-scale human demonstration data (e.g., video, motion capture and teleoperation) can be turned into capable, general-purpose robot behaviour. In particular, you will develop novel algorithms and policies for high-DoF hands and validate them on real hardware. In doing so, you will collaborate with a team of expert researchers in robotics, computer vision and machine learning. We strive to publish in top-tier conferences such as CVPR, NeurIPS, ICLR, ECCV, ICCV, ICRA and RSS.  

What we are looking for

 

A strong track record in top conferences and journals in robot learning, machine learning or computer vision such as CVPR, NeurIPS, ICLR, ECCV, ICCV, ICRA and RSS.
Demonstrated robot learning experience (e.g., imitation learning, learning from demonstrations, VLAs / robot foundation models, or reinforcement learning) is a must.
Strong PyTorch programming skills and working knowledge of ROS are a must. 
Hands-on experience deploying learned policies on real robots is a must; experience with dexterous hands, teleoperation or motion capture for demonstration collection is a plus. 
Applicants must hold a PhD in computer science, robotics, engineering or equivalent. 

You should have proven research record and publications in the relevant areas.  

Please see job description for a full list of requirements. 

What we can offer you

The chance to work in an exciting and rapidly developing area, with access to state-of-the-art hardware including Sharpa Wave hands and UR7e arms. This is a chance to grow and establish yourself as a leader in this field.
Dedicated mentorship as well as the freedom to explore your own ideas. 
Working closely with a team of PhD students and postdocs from different backgrounds. 
The Department of Computing is the top-1 ranked computer science department in the UK, according to REF 2021.
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year). 
Disseminating your research in major robotics, machine learning and computer vision conferences is supported and travel costs will be covered. 

Further information

Full-time, fixed term position for 12 months to start as soon as possible

*Candidates who have not yet been officially awarded their PhD will be appointed as Research Assistant within the salary range £45,399 - £48,876 per annum. 

In addition to completing the online application candidates should attach:

A full CV with a list of all publications
A research statement indicating what you see are interesting research issues relating to the above post and why your expertise is relevant

Informal enquiries related to the position should be directed to Dr Rolandos Potamias r.potamias19@imperial.ac.uk

For queries regarding the application process contact Jamie Perrins: j.perrins@imperial.ac.uk

Research Associate in AI and Evidence Synthesis

Job id: 161425. Salary: £45,031 - £52,514 per annum inclusive of London Weighting Allowance.

Posted: 23 October 2026. Closing date: 06 November 2026.

Business unit: Faculty of Life Sciences & Medicine. Department: Primary Care & Data Science.

Contact details: Iain Marshall. iain.marshall@kcl.ac.uk

Location: Guy's Campus. Category: No category added.

Back to job search

About us

King’s College London is one of the world's leading universities, ranked 31st globally and 5th in the UK in the QS World University Rankings 2026. Founded in 1829, King’s is a Russell Group university with a world-renowned reputation for excellence in education, research and innovation, particularly across medicine, health and the life sciences.

This post will be based within the newly established Department of Primary Care & Data Science, an interdisciplinary department that brings together expertise in primary care, population health, health informatics, artificial intelligence, epidemiology, biostatistics and health services research. The Department aims to develop innovative data-driven approaches to improve health and healthcare, working closely with patients, communities, policy-makers, healthcare providers and international partners.

The Department sits within the  School of Life Course & Population Health Sciences , one of six Schools that make up the Faculty of Life Sciences & Medicine at King’s College London. The School unites over 500 experts in a wide range of population health sciences including women and children’s health, life course sciences, nutritional sciences, Health AI, preventive medicine and the molecular genetics of human disease. Our research links the causes of common health problems to life’s landmark stages, treating life, disease and healthcare as a continuum. We are interdisciplinary by nature and this innovative approach works: 91 per cent of our research submitted to the Subjects Allied to Medicine (Pharmacy, Nutritional Sciences and Women's Health cluster) for REF was rated as world-leading or internationally excellent. We use this expertise to teach the next generation of health professionals and research scientists. Based across King’s Denmark Hill, Guy’s, St Thomas’ and Waterloo campuses, our academic programme of teaching, research and clinical practice is embedded across seven Departments.

About the role

We are seeking a post-doctoral health data scientist with a strong mix of Python scientific coding skills and applied health research expertise, to work on the METIUS AI work package (metiusevidence.org), which is co-led by King’s and UCL. The successful candidate will design, build and adapt AI-enabled evidence synthesis tools, help METIUS consortium partner organisations onboard and use them, and contribute to methodological and evaluation research.

METIUS (Mobilising Evidence Through Artificial Intelligence and User-Informed Synthesis) is an £11.5m UKRI-funded programme, led by Queen’s University Belfast, building breakthrough AI and open data infrastructure for rapid, living evidence synthesis. The consortium brings together 19 organisations, including King’s, to deliver exemplar syntheses across education, crime & justice, climate, and sustainable development, and to engage directly with policymakers.

You will design, build, and evaluate AI-enabled evidence synthesis tools and pipelines, writing well-documented, production-quality code, and will work directly with partner organisations across the consortium to configure and onboard these tools to their needs. You will design and run methodological and evaluation studies assessing the performance, reliability and usability of AI-assisted evidence synthesis methods, and write these up for publication.

You will work in a team with software developers, data scientists, and evidence synthesis specialists. Alongside METIUS, you will contribute to the related Solace-AI project (solaceai.org), applying AI-driven evidence synthesis methods to climate-health emergencies, and will develop new methods for making sure AI systems are trustworthy.

This is a full time post (35 hours per week), and you will be offered a fixed term contract for 2 years from your start date.

Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. This entitlement, from the  Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers, applies to Postdocs, Research Assistants, Research and Teaching Technicians, Teaching Fellows and AEP equivalent up to and including grade 7. Visit the  Centre for Research Staff Development for more information.

About you

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria:

PhD awarded in Health Data Science, Computer Science, Epidemiology, Public Health, or a related quantitative field; or PhD in one of these subjects near completion.
Experience conducting high-quality evidence synthesis (including systematic reviews, and scoping, rapid, umbrella reviews, and guidelines) using formal methodological approaches (e.g. narrative synthesis, evidence mapping).
Strong software development skills; experienced in version control/GitHub; expertise in using Python scientific stack (jupyter/numpy/scipy/sci-kit learn/pandas etc).
Strong publication track record as demonstrated through first-author publications in peer-reviewed journals.
Demonstrated ability to design and conduct applied health or policy research studies, including study design, quantitative analysis, and interpretation of findings.
Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.

Desirable criteria:

Experience in stakeholder engagement: working with policy makers, humanitarian organisations, international partners, and/or the public.
Experience contributing to multi-partner or consortium research projects, e.g. adapting tools or methods for different partner organisations.
Experience working with global and interdisciplinary teams to conduct and publish research.

Downloading a copy of our Job Description

Full details of the role and the skills, knowledge and experience required can be found in the Job Description document, provided at the bottom of the page. This document will provide information of what criteria will be assessed at each stage of the recruitment process.

HR Use Only (Research G6 Clause):

* Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have submitted their thesis and are awaiting award of their PhDs will be considered. In these circumstances the appointment will be made at Grade 5, spine point 30 with the title of Research Assistant. Upon confirmation of the award of the PhD, the job title will become Research Associate and the salary will increase to Grade 6.

Further Information

At King’s, we believe that the diversity of our community and a culture that is welcoming, open, inclusive and collaborative, are great strengths of the university.

The Equality Act of 2010 protects the rights of our students and staff and provides a framework to fulfil our duties to eliminate unlawful discrimination, harassment and victimisation and in addition, to advance equality of opportunity and foster good relations between those who share a protected characteristic and those who do not. When engaging in the robust exchange of ideas, we ask that our community is mindful of our Dignity at King’s guidance.

We ask all candidates to submit a copy of their CV, and a supporting statement, detailing how they meet the essential criteria listed in the person specification section of the job description. If we receive a strong field of candidates, we may use the desirable criteria to choose our final shortlist, so please include your evidence against these where possible.

We reserve the right to close adverts early due to the volume of applications we receive. While the closing date may change, all adverts will close at 23:59 to allow sufficient time for applications to be submitted on that day.

KTP Associate - Digital Manufacturing Engineer for AI based Quality Inspection
Knowledge Transfer Partnerships
Location:  Off Campus
Please note, this post is fixed-term until 31/10/2028 and full-time at 37 hours per week.
Closing Date:   Friday 30 October 2026
Interview Date:   To be confirmed
Reference:  EL1284

Are you passionate about applying artificial intelligence and computer vision to solve real-world manufacturing challenges? Do you want to take cutting-edge AI technologies beyond the laboratory and deploy them within a live industrial environment? Are you excited by the opportunity to lead an innovation project at the intersection of AI, digital manufacturing, and industrial automation?

We are seeking a KTP Associate - Digital Manufacturing Engineer for AI-Based Quality Inspection for an exciting 24-month Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP) between the University of Lincoln and Eminox Ltd.

Eminox is a global leader in the design and manufacture of advanced exhaust after-treatment systems for heavy-duty on-road and off-road vehicles, rail, marine and power-generation applications. This KTP brings together Eminox's industrial expertise with research expertise from the University of Lincoln's Creative Automation Lab for Industrial X-factors (CALIX) in intelligent manufacturing, industrial automation, artificial intelligence, computer vision and Industry 4.0 technologies. 

What You'll Be Doing

Based primarily at Eminox Ltd in Gainsborough, Lincolnshire, you will take a leading technical role in developing and implementing an AI-enabled vision pre-inspection system for industrial manufacturing.

You will work to first capture complex, multi-modal industrial datasets to and then develop intelligent methods capable of identifying manufacturing defects and predicting downstream performance outcomes of Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) units. Combining computer vision, machine learning, deep learning, and industrial automation, you will translate advanced AI research into a robust system capable of operating within a real manufacturing environment. 

You will lead activities including developing machine-vision methods for defect detection and classification; designing and training AI models; establishing industrial data pipelines; integrating AI algorithms with manufacturing processes; and validating and optimising the resulting system under industrial operating conditions. The aim is to improve inspection accuracy and consistency while reducing unnecessary downstream processing, manufacturing costs and waste. 

This is much more than a desk-based AI role. You will work at the interface between advanced research and industrial implementation, developing prototypes, conducting system-integrated testing, and translating theoretical approaches into commercially viable solutions. 

As the KTP Associate, you will have considerable autonomy and responsibility for delivering the project, managing technical milestones, and communicating results. You will also contribute to research outputs, technical reports, publications, and conference presentations, while developing documentation and training materials that enable the new knowledge and capability to remain embedded within Eminox beyond the project. 

What We're Looking For

We are looking for an ambitious interdisciplinary engineer who wants to apply advanced digital technologies to real industrial challenges.

A strong academic foundation: A master’s degree in mechanical engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Robotics, Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science/Data Science, or a closely related discipline is essential. A PhD in a relevant discipline is desirable. 
AI and data expertise: Experience in machine learning, computer vision and/or data analytics, with an ability to develop and evaluate intelligent models for engineering applications. 
Strong programming capability: Programming experience in Python or similar is particularly important, with MATLAB or similar environments also relevant. Experience with deep-learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow and computer-vision tools such as OpenCV would be advantageous. 
Engineering and experimental capability: Experience of experimental work, quality-inspection techniques, and systems, and researching and developing new or improved engineering systems or methods. 
Analytical problem-solving: Strong mathematical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to analyse complex data and translate technical concepts into practical industrial solutions. 
Industrial and digital manufacturing experience: Familiarity with industrial datasets, manufacturing environments, process automation and control systems such as PLCs, Industry 4.0 technologies or automated quality-inspection systems would be advantageous. 
Project leadership: The ability to manage a complex project involving multiple stakeholders, organise your own work effectively and deliver against demanding KTP and business milestones. 
A collaborative and innovative mindset: You should be proactive, adaptable, and enthusiastic about R&D, with the ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with multidisciplinary academic and industrial teams. 

Why Join Us?

This KTP offers a unique opportunity to lead the development of an industrial AI system from research concept through to implementation in a live manufacturing environment.

You will benefit from:

Direct mentorship and joint supervision from experienced engineers and senior management at Eminox and academic experts from the University of Lincoln. 
Access to a dedicated KTP personal development and training budget. 
Nationally recognised management and leadership development through the Innovate UK KTP programme. 
Experience spanning AI, computer vision, digital manufacturing, industrial automation, and real-world technology deployment. 
Opportunities to produce research outputs and engage with the wider academic and industrial research community. 
The opportunity to develop project-management, leadership, and stakeholder-engagement capabilities alongside your technical expertise. 
Strong potential for continued career development within Eminox following successful completion of the KTP. 

The project provides an unusual opportunity for an ambitious engineer or AI specialist to become the technical lead for a strategically important industrial innovation project, developing expertise that bridges advanced AI research and manufacturing practice.

The role is based primarily at Eminox Ltd in Gainsborough, Lincolnshire, with regular interaction with the University of Lincoln and CALIX. The Associate will work closely with both industrial and academic teams throughout the 24-month project. 

If you would like further information or an informal discussion about this exciting opportunity, please contact Dr Faiz Iqbal (fiqbal@linoln.ac.uk), School of Engineering and Physical Sciences, University of Lincoln.

Senior Research Associate in Computer Vision and 3D Reconstruction for Wildlife Conservation - (9503)

About the Faculty 

Manchester Metropolitan University is one of the UK's largest universities, with a strong commitment to interdisciplinary research addressing real-world challenges. Our newly established School of Biological and Chemical Sciences, within the Faculty of Science and Engineering, brings together expertise spanning biodiversity, zoology, ecology, physiology and the biomedical sciences. The University has growing strengths in artificial intelligence, data science and computational research, supported by its new Centre for Digital Data Research (CDDR). Together, these strengths provide an exciting environment for research at the intersection of AI, biological sciences and conservation. 

About the School 

You will join the School's Biodiversity and Environmental Resilience research group, where researchers investigate animal biology, evolution, behaviour and conservation, and develop innovative approaches to understanding and protecting the natural world. Our research combines traditional biological expertise with emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, advanced 3D imaging and computational modelling. You will benefit from access to specialist research facilities, including imaging equipment in the University's new £1m Centre for Digital Modelling and Analysis for Cultural Heritage (D-MACH), and opportunities to engage with the wider Species Biology and Conservation (SBAC) research community through seminars, collaborative activities and knowledge exchange.  

About the Project  

This position is funded by the Natural Environment Research Council (NERC) through Phase 1 of its Artificial Intelligence for Environmental Science (AI4ES) programme. The project, Using Camera Trap Images to Reconstruct Wildlife 3D Body Size and Condition, aims to develop innovative AI-based methods for measuring animal size, shape and body condition from standard camera-trap photographs.  

By combining monocular depth estimation with single-image 3D reconstruction, the project will develop new approaches to recovering quantitative, real-world measurements of wild animals without the need for physical handling. Working with Chester Zoo and the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology, we will develop and validate these methods using advanced 3D imaging techniques, including LiDAR and photogrammetry, with the longer-term aim of supporting non-invasive wildlife health monitoring and conservation.  

The project is led by Dr Charlotte Brassey (Principal Investigator), alongside Manchester Met colleagues Dr Selvino de Kort and Dr Bradley Cain, and external collaborators Dr Peng Wang (University of Sussex), Dr Lisa Holmes (Chester Zoo) and Dr Adam van Casteren (Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology).  

About the Role & Team 

You will play a central role in the day-to-day technical development and delivery of the project, with responsibility for developing, testing and validating AI-based approaches to reconstructing animal body size and shape from camera-trap imagery. Your work will primarily involve computational research, including model development, dataset curation and quantitative analysis, alongside opportunities for practical data collection and validation at Chester Zoo.  

You will be encouraged to take ownership of your research, contribute to peer-reviewed publications and conference presentations, and help shape future research directions, including the development of a larger Phase 2 funding application. You will also become part of the wider Biodiversity and Ecosystem Resilience research community, with opportunities to participate in the Species Biology and Conservation (SBAC) seminar series and professional development activities.  

Key Responsibilities 

Benchmark and fine-tune state-of-the-art monocular depth-estimation models using camera-trap imagery. 
Develop and evaluate AI-based methods for single-image 3D reconstruction of animals, integrating metric depth information to recover body dimensions and shape in real-world units. 
Curate and manage colour, LiDAR, photogrammetry and 3D datasets. 
Develop robust, reproducible computational pipelines using Python and relevant deep-learning frameworks. 
Undertake quantitative validation, statistical analysis and evaluation of model performance, accuracy and uncertainty. 
Collaborate with project partners to undertake data collection and validation at Chester Zoo. 
Contribute to the development and release of open-source software, datasets and trained models. 
Prepare research findings for publication in peer-reviewed journals and presentation at national and international conferences. 
Contribute to project management, dissemination, stakeholder engagement and the development of follow-on funding applications, including Phase 2 of the NERC AI4ES programme. 

Key Skills & Experiences  

We are looking for a highly motivated researcher with strong computational skills and experience in computer vision, machine learning, AI-based image analysis and/or 3D reconstruction. We welcome applicants from a broad range of disciplinary backgrounds; previous experience in ecology or zoology is not required. This is an interdisciplinary project, and we recognise that relevant expertise can be developed through a variety of research backgrounds and career pathways. We therefore encourage applications from candidates who bring transferable skills and enthusiasm for the project, even if they do not meet every criterion listed below.  

Essential criteria:

About the Role's

Listening to Nature: Monitoring Biodiversity Through Sound

Join an exciting government funded research project developing next-generation biodiversity monitoring technologies

Nottingham Trent University is seeking two enthusiastic researchers to join the newly funded Eco-SEv project, which aims to optimise autonomous acoustic technologies for assessing biodiversity and ecosystem health across agricultural, forestry and natural environments.

Working in collaboration with an innovative technology company and a consortium of industry and international partners, you will contribute to the development and validation of next-generation ecoacoustic tools for assessing biodiversity and ecosystem health across diverse environments in the UK and internationally.

By combining autonomous acoustic sensors, ecological expertise and advanced analytical approaches, Eco-SEv aims to deliver scalable solutions that support environmental monitoring, natural capital assessment and sustainability across a range of agricultural, forestry and conservation settings.

Available positions:

Research Fellow

You will lead NTU's research contribution to the project, designing and delivering acoustic monitoring studies, analysing ecological and acoustic datasets, reporting outputs and coordinating validation activities undertaken by partners in the UK and Kenya.

You will work closely with leading researchers in ecoacoustics, ecology and biodiversity assessment, alongside commercial partners developing cutting-edge environmental sensing technologies.

Research Associate

You will support field and analytical aspects of the project, including deployment of acoustic monitoring equipment, ecological surveys, biodiversity ground-truthing, data processing and stakeholder engagement activities.

This role offers an excellent opportunity for an early-career researcher wishing to develop expertise in ecoacoustics, biodiversity monitoring and environmental data science.

What we are looking for

Ecology

Geography
Bioacoustics
Ecoacoustics

Related environmental disciplines

Candidates should ideally have experience in ecological field research and biodiversity monitoring, together with skills in data analysis, statistical modelling, GIS, and programming in R and/or Python. Familiarity with ecoacoustic methods, including the processing and analysis of acoustic datasets, use of ecoacoustic software and platforms, and management of large biodiversity databases, would be highly desirable. Experience with environmental sensors, remote sensing technologies and machine learning approaches would also be advantageous.

While this role will work with Brighton and Sussex Medical School, the substantive contract will be held by the NHS and as such all applicants must apply via Oriel. Any applications received here are not able to be considered.

About the role

For this ACF we are seeking an enthusiastic candidate interested in the analysis of routinely collected primary and secondary care data. They will be training (or applying to train) in general practice and will undertake academic training alongside this, particularly in their last 2 years of training. They will receive supervision from academics in both General Practice and Data Science. ACFs in GP have a four year training programme meaning that they spend 25% of their time in ST3 & 4 undertaking research. This post has entry points at ST1,2 and 3. 

This program will utilise linked NHS hospital and primary care data to investigate the clinical consequences of medication changes initiated during hospital admissions. The successful ACF will develop a program of work exploring the critical transition point of hospital discharge to community care where there are medication changes initiated during a hospital admission (including new prescriptions, dose adjustments, and discontinuations). These medication changes have significant implications for post-discharge outcomes, which then need to be managed in primary care. A cohort of patients vulnerable to such harms will be chosen such as those with a) polypharmacy (≥5 medications prescribed), b) Multiple Long-Term Conditions (≥2 long term conditions), or c) trans people (chosen due to evidence that they may be less likely to interact with standard primary care).

Further Key Information 

Interested candidates are advised to contact Dr Liz Ford (Informatics) E.M.Ford@bsms.ac.uk, Prof Richard McManus (GP) deansoffice@bsms.ac.uk and Prof Dunx Shrewsbury (GP) d.shrewsbury@bsms.ac.uk for an early discussion.

The Role

We are seeking to appoint a highly motivated and enthusiastic Post-Graduate Research Associate on a new project ‘Expansion of cultivated meat research at Aberystwyth University: encompassing texture and accelerating research for economic benefit in Wales’ funded by the Welsh Government. The project seeks to explore the expansion of current cultivated meat research at Aberystwyth through the use of edible scaffolds, 3D bioprinting and AI-Machine Learning (AI-ML) driven methods to create high-throughput research pipelines.

To make an informal enquiry, please contact Dr Ruth Wonfor at rec21@aber.ac.uk.  

Successful applicants may be subject to a satisfactory Disclosure and Barring Service Check (DBS) check.

Appointments are normally made within 4 - 8 weeks of the closing date.

What you’ll do

The role will largely be desk based to complete a review of the current literature and industry needs to identify gaps in current knowledge, leading to the production of an Innovation plan and target areas for follow on funding or commercialisation. This part time post will focus on the AI-ML aspects of the project.

The PGRA post will be based in the Department of Life Sciences in Dr Ruth Wonfor’s research group, but will also require collaboration with Prof Tossapon Boongoen in the Department of Computer Science. The project includes collaboration with a Welsh based biotech company, Copner Biotech, who the post-holder will be expected to develop a good working relationship with. There will also be opportunities to connect with other companies in the cultivated meat space to network with experts in the field whilst gaining an overview of current industry needs.

The project will be completed over 5 months and this post will work alongside another part-time post that will focus on cell culture/scaffolds. The two PGRAs will be expected to work closely together to complete the Innovation Plan.

Main duties and responsibilities:

Complete a literature review of the academic and wider industry literature around AI-ML for cultivated meat
Support development of a professional network with industry collaborators and academic experts to foster future collaborations.
Partake in site visits to external companies or academic institutes to assess technologies used and discuss data requirements.

Other duties and responsibilities:

To support the university strategy and underlining plans, engage in continuous personal and professional development in line with the demands of the role, including undertaking relevant training and development activities to develop yourself and support the development of others.
Fulfil health and safety responsibilities appropriate to the role, while actively promoting the personal health, safety, and wellbeing of staff and students as a member of the Aberystwyth community. Additionally, support the University’s commitment to environmental sustainability through responsible practices and engagement. 
Promote equality of opportunity, and to support and uphold the University's commitment to diversity and inclusion in all aspects of your work.
Undertake other duties as assigned by your line manager, commensurate with the role's grade.

This job description is subject to review and amendment in the light of the changing needs of the University, to provide appropriate development opportunities and/or the addition of any other reasonable duties.

Essential

Masters or post-graduate qualification in a relevant subject area e.g. computer science (applicants who have submitted a Masters dissertation and are awaiting a result will be considered).
Experience of working with and/or in-depth knowledge of AI-ML models.
Attention to detail to ensure accurate and reliable literature synthesis.

Organisational skills, with an ability to multitask and work independently on defined tasks.

This position offers a unique opportunity for a highly motivated individual to work at the interface of academia and industry in a Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP) Associate role that will deliver transformational impact. You will lead and deliver a service innovation programme within a fast-growing British SME manufacturer, helping to drive innovation and business growth in a company with strong values centred on teamwork, innovation, and excellence.

The project is fundamentally focused on servitization; supporting an engineering company transition from providing equipment through traditional capital expenditure (CapEx) systems towards a service-led, lifecycle-oriented business model. You will lead the co-design and implementation of a product-service system within the company, developing service-led concepts and offerings that create value for customers over the lifecycle of their operations.

This role is designed to enable the transition of a company towards a service-led business model, developing new forms of value creation and strengthening long-term customer relationships. You will play a key role in establishing the foundations for ongoing servitization, embedding new capabilities, and supporting the sustainable growth of the business beyond the duration of the KTP.

Candidate Profile: 

A minimum of a 2:1 BSc degree in Engineering or Management, or a related discipline.  

 Essential skills, experience and attributes required include:

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
Ability to work across technical and commercial domains
Experience of adapting theories and/or tools to commercial practice
Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills with the ability to engage across multiple levels of an organisation
Strong project management capability, able to manage complex projects, coordinate roles, and work independently, as well as part of the team.

Knowledge or experience of servitization, product-service systems, or business model innovation.
Experience of working in manufacturing or industrial settings.
Experience in customer research, data analysis, or development of commercially informed strategies.

Key responsibilities of this role include: 

Service design and product-service system development
Servitization strategy development

Aston University: You will work in a project team consisting of Dr Reza Marvi, Dr Geoff Parkes, Dr Daniel Andrews from Aston University and the Senior Management Team of the Company, with the support of a Knowledge Transfer Adviser from Innovate UK.

Research Associate in QET LABS /Senior Research Associate

The role

We have a number of exciting research opportunities in the Quantum Engineering Technology Labs (QET Labs) at the University of Bristol. As a member of QET Labs, you will conduct research at the interface of quantum technologies, photonics, and experimental science. You will be part of a dynamic team and have the opportunity to interact with all members of QET Labs and the wider Bristol Quantum Information Institute.

QET Labs has a mission to take quantum science discoveries out of the lab and engineer them into technologies for the benefit of society.  This includes novel routes to quantum computing hardware, quantum communications, enhanced sensing & imaging and new platforms to investigate fundamental quantum physics. The Research Centre consists of over 100 academics, researchers, staff and students and sits within both the School of Physics and the School of Electrical, Electronic and Mechanical Engineering.

Multiple Research Associate positions are available of different durations. The duration of the post to be offered will be discussed following a successful interview.

What will you be doing?

Your responsibilities will include working with others to formulate project plans, developing new techniques for classical and quantum optics characterisation and delivery of research outputs.

Specifically, you will be working in one of these key areas of research:

Quantum Computing
Quantum Communications
Quantum Sensing/Imaging
Solid State quantum systems
Integrated Quantum Photonics
Pure or applied quantum information theory
Cold and ultra cold atomic Physics

You should apply if

You have a strong track record in the design, implementation, and analysis of photonic devices or quantum information processing with photons
You have expertise in optical engineering or quantum optics and a demonstratable understanding of its major platforms, e.g. integrated photonics, emitters
You have postgraduate (or equivalent) laboratory experience in one of experimental physics, optics, photonics, electronics, or a related discipline
You have a PhD (or equivalent qualification) and first degree in Physics, Electrical/ Electronic Engineering, or other relevant discipline (or equivalent relevant research experience)

This position is presented as full-time. Flexible working options are considered. QET Labs is committed to helping researchers become independent academics and have extensive experience in aiding PDRAs with fellowship applications.

 

Please note this is NOT a direct application for a live vacancy. Instead, you will be entered into a candidate pool for a RESEARCH ASSOCIATE IN QET LABS /SENIOR RESEARCH ASSOCIATE position.

We have a policy in place to regularly review our candidate pool to ensure its relevance and efficiency therefore you may be invited to interview or occasionally receive notifications regarding new job openings. We encourage you to stay connected with us and to keep your contact information up to date to ensure that you don't miss out on any potential opportunities.

If you have any questions or need further assistance, please don't hesitate to reach out to us at recruitment@bristol.ac.uk.

 

Our strategy and mission

We recently launched our strategy to 2030 tying together our mission, vision and values.

 

The University of Bristol aims to be a place where everyone feels able to be themselves and do their best in an inclusive working environment where all colleagues can thrive and reach their full potential. We want to attract, develop, and retain individuals with different experiences, backgrounds and perspectives – particularly people of colour, LGBT+ and disabled people - because diversity of people and ideas remains integral to our excellence as a global civic institution.

BCAST is well equipped with state-of-the-art facilities for both metal processing and materials characterisation. See https://www.brunel.ac.uk/research/Centres/BCAST for more information. 

This position is funded by an Innovate UK project entitled TURBOCOOLING: Energy-Efficient and Frost-Resistant Heat Exchangers Enabled by Advanced Aluminium Brazing, for a period of nine months. It focuses on brazing aluminium alloy components using an induction heating system with integrated temperature monitoring and control to ensure high-integrity, high-quality brazed joints. 

The position involves both experimental and modelling aspects of aluminium brazing. The successful candidate will focus on optimising aluminium brazing process, simulating temperature distributions within aluminium workpieces during brazing, and characterising the microstructure and mechanical properties of brazed joints. Responsibilities include developing apparatus and methodologies for manufacturing high-integrity, high-quality brazed aluminium joints, with the aim of optimising joint microstructures and maximising mechanical performance.

Our work combines ecological research, quantitative analysis and digital tools to improve the evidence underpinning carbon markets.

We are seeking a technically capable graduate with strong analytical and programming skills and an ability to communicate clearly. This is an opportunity to contribute to applied research at the interface of conservation science, climate change and carbon markets.

Working closely with the Scientific Lead, Dr Tom Swinfield, you will support the development and application of 4C's analytical methods for evaluating nature-based climate and biodiversity benefits. Finally, you will contribute to our external communications, by producing blog posts and other accessible accounts of our research. We are looking for someone who enjoys working with data and can explain scientific findings clearly, including their uncertainties and limitations.

Support the development, testing and application of analytical methods to evaluate the climate and biodiversity benefits of forest conservation.

postings.advert_text:
Applications are invited for a Research Assistant in the Materials Theory Group, Department of Materials Science and Metallurgy. The ERC-funded position is with Prof. Stefano Racioppi (PI) on his "Quantum Theory of the Periodic Tables Under Extreme Conditions (QUANTEX) project. We are looking for motivated and enthusiastic applicants interested in theoretical chemistry, condensed matter physics and computational materials science.

The successful candidate will join Prof. Racioppi's group to investigate how extreme pressure changes the electronic structure, chemical bonding, and properties of elements and compounds, challenging familiar chemical rules. QUANTEX aims to understand these changes and develop a theoretical framework to describe chemical periodicities under compression and guide the prediction of new materials. The appointee will also join a thriving community of computational materials scientists within the Materials Theory Group and the wider Lennard-Jones Centre at Cambridge.

The role will combine first-principles calculations, largely based on density functional theory (DFT) with: crystal structure prediction and machine-learning methods; chemical bonding analysis, including the quantum theory of atoms in molecules (QTAIM); energy decomposition analysis (EDA), and analysis of electronegativities. Potential research directions include pressure-induced changes in electronic structure (e.g. core-valence boundaries),chemical periodicity (e.g. electronegativities and oxidation states), the formation of electride and superconducting states, and machine-learning accelerated materials discovery.

Applicants should have (or expect to be awarded) a good UK Master's degree (or overseas equivalent) in a relevant science subject (Materials Science, Chemistry, Physics) and meet the University's academic and English-language entry requirements for their doctoral programme. A strong interest in theoretical and solid-state chemistry is essential. Previous experience in programming, machine learning, electronic-structure calculations, or atomistic modelling whilst advantageous, is not essential. Applicants should have good analytical and communication skills, intellectual curiosity, and ability to work both independently and collaboratively. They will receive training in computational methods for solid-state chemistry and physics, have access to high-performance computing facilities, and benefit from interactions with local and international theoretical and experimental collaborators. Applicants can be of any nationality and should be enrolled in a doctoral programme at Cambridge during the project.

Informal enquiries should be directed to Prof. Stefano Racioppi, sr2200@cam.ac.uk.

Interviews will be held online: 1 March 2027. Expected start date: 1 October 2027.

Fixed-term: The funds for this post are available for 42 months in the first instance.

Click the 'Apply' button below to register an account with our recruitment system (if you have not already) and apply online.

Additionally, PhD applications should be submitted separately via the University Application Portal: www.postgraduate.study.cam.ac.uk/apply, identifying Prof. Stefano Racioppi as the proposed supervisor with QUANTEX as the project of interest.

Applications must include: (i) A short research statement/cover letter describing the applicant's past research, future goals, and why the applicant is interested and suitable for this position. (ii). A curriculum vitae, including publications. (iii). The contact details of two referees who can provide a letter of recommendation.

Please quote reference LJ51458 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy.

Moss carder bee recovery post-doc opportunity

We are looking for an exceptional, driven postdoctoral researcher to lead a high-impact, 1-year project bridging the gap between machine learning for species identification and real-world insect conservation. You will focus on recovery of the moss carder bee (Bombus muscorum), an iconic bumblebee species classed as 'vulnerable' in the latest European Red List of bees. You will join a Species Recovery Programme project led by the Bumblebee Conservation Trust, funded by Natural England. This is an exciting opportunity to develop tools with direct impact on nature recovery and biodiversity policy.

To drive targeted monitoring programmes and inform targeted field surveys, you will build and evaluate a visual recognition tool for this morphologically cryptic species. To achieve this, you will harness machine learning approaches, combined with DNA barcoded species photos. This will require fieldwork, coordination of scientists and volunteers from our partner, the Bumblebee Conservation Trust, and lab work. This tool will enable real-world conservation interventions.

Joining the vibrant Brown Lab within the Department of Zoology, you will be embedded in a world-leading scientific network as a member of the Cambridge Conservation Research Institute (CCRI) and the Cambridge Conservation Initiative (CCI) - one of the largest clusters of biodiversity researchers and policy experts on Earth.

 The role:

An exciting opportunity has become available to work on a 36-month Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP) between the University of Exeter and Rapid Fusion Ltd. The KTP will develop software for intelligent process control in Large Format Additive Manufacturing (LFAM), focused on improving polymer deposition consistency and interlayer bonding performance. The candidate is expected to have a good understanding of the LFAM process including thermal behaviour of the polymers and knowledge of polymer material science. 

The successful candidate will be employed by the University of Exeter and will spend the majority of their time working at Rapid Fusion Ltd in Exeter, with occasional visits to the University of Exeter. They will be expected to work full-time.

Company Information: Rapid Fusion specialises in large-format additive manufacturing systems, including modular 3D printing platforms, AM modules, and robotic AM cells. Their LFAM technology enables the creation of large components with high production outputs, offering a sustainable alternative to traditional manufacturing. More information about the Rapid Fusion Ltd can be found here: https://rapidfusion.co.uk/pages/about

Previous applicants to this role need not apply.

Educated to first degree level or a good Master’s Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science, or in a related field of study or equivalent experience. A degree in Computer Science will be considered where supported by relevant experience in materials and manufacturing.
Strong academic record demonstrating capability in theoretical analysis and practical application.

Strong analytical and problem‑solving skills, with ability to interpret complex datasets.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to mixed academic and industrial audiences.
Ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary academic–industry team, with commercial awareness.
Experience of managing research projects or contributing significantly to collaborative research.
Well‑organised, self‑motivated, and able to prioritise work independently within a project framework.
Enthusiasm for hands‑on experimental work alongside computational modelling.
Adaptable and able to work effectively in a fast‑paced SME environment.
Understanding of health and safety requirements and good research record‑keeping practices.
Commitment to equality, diversity and inclusive working practices.
Willingness to be primarily based at Rapid Fusion Ltd (Exeter), with visits to the University of Exeter as required, and flexibility to meet project demands.

A £6,000 training budget with 10% of your working time dedicated to personal development.
A unique and challenging career opportunity, working with both industry and academia.

The opportunity to manage and lead on a project early on in your career.
Specific KTP residential training.
The possibility to write academic papers and present at conferences.
