Research Assistant

Job id: 160246. Salary: £39,076 - £41,761 per annum, including London Weighting Allowance.

Posted: 12 October 2026. Closing date: 26 October 2026.

Business unit: IoPPN. Department: Academic Neuroscience.

Contact details: Peter Goadsby/Ivana Rosenzweig. Peter.goadsby@kcl.ac.uk/ivana.1.rosenzweig@kcl.ac.uk

Location: Guy's Campus. Category: Research.

Back to job search

About us:

King’s College London is one of the world’s leading universities, renowned for its excellence in research, education, and clinical innovation. The Sleep and Brain Plasticity Centre, based within the Department of Neuroimaging, Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience (IoPPN), is at the forefront of cutting-edge sleep research, integrating neuroscience, computational modelling, and clinical applications to advance our understanding of sleep-related brain processes. Our work spans multiple disciplines, including memory research, neurology, psychiatry, headaches, and pain, providing a comprehensive framework for investigating the role of sleep in brain function and dysfunction.

A key focus of our centre is the development and refinement of sleep EEG research pipelines, enabling high-resolution analyses of sleep architecture, neural oscillations, and cognitive function. Our projects employ advanced polysomnography (PSG), computational EEG signal analysis, and network-based approaches, bridging fundamental neuroscience with translational applications in neurological and psychiatric disorders.

We are seeking a highly skilled specialist to contribute to the SleepCity EEG project, ensuring the successful execution and optimisation of our bespoke EEG research pipeline. The appointed candidate will play a central role in advancing our research initiatives, enhancing our capabilities in data processing, analysis, and interpretation of sleep EEG, and contributing to novel discoveries in sleep neuroscience.

About the role:

King’s College London invites applications for a highly skilled specialist to join our research team at the Sleep and Brain Plasticity Centre. The successful candidate will play a critical role in executing and finalising the bespoke SleepCity EEG project pipeline, contributing significantly to ongoing research in sleep neurophysiology and ensuring the continued success and advancement of our research initiatives.

This position requires expertise in sleep EEG processing and analysis, with a strong background in non-linear EEG methods, spectral analysis, and network-based approaches to sleep dynamics. The ideal candidate will have extensive experience in Python programming and be proficient in handling large EEG datasets using publicly available polysomnography (PSG) analysis software. A deep understanding of sleep phenotypes, graphoelements, and their functional role in sleep cycling is essential, as is prior experience working with EEG signal processing and computational modelling of sleep dynamics.

The role involves developing and optimising the EEG analysis pipeline, overseeing the successful analysis and management of large-scale sleep EEG datasets, and ensuring seamless coordination with key collaborators. The candidate will be expected to train and support team members in using EEG analysis protocols, deliver weekly progress updates to the line manager, and contribute to manuscript preparation, including methodology sections and data visualisation.

Given the complexity of our current bespoke EEG pipeline—from data acquisition and pre-processing to advanced analyses of sleep architecture and spectral parameters—the candidate’s demonstrated experience in computational physics and dynamical systems modelling will be invaluable. Their strong programming background, including Python, C++, and Java, as well as their ability to work efficiently with shell scripting and remote server-based computational workflows, would be ideal in order to ensure they can fully integrate into the research team with minimal training. Their prior work in state-transition networks, scale-free spectral properties, and sleep EEG fractal dynamics would make them particularly well-suited to our ongoing projects.

This is a unique opportunity to contribute to pioneering research in sleep neurophysiology and EEG signal analysis within a leading academic institution. The position is ideal for a researcher with a strong computational background who is eager to apply their expertise in EEG processing, sleep science, and network-based analysis methods to a highly specialised research setting.

About you:

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential Criteria:

Expertise in sleep EEG analysis, including spectral analysis, non-linear EEG methods, and network-based approaches to sleep dynamics.
Proficiency in Python programming, with experience in EEG signal processing and computational modelling of sleep architecture.
Demonstrated experience working with large-scale EEG datasets, including pre-processing, artefact correction, and statistical analysis.
Familiarity with polysomnography (PSG) data analysis, including publicly available EEG analysis software.
Background in computational physics, neuroscience, or biomedical engineering, with a strong understanding of dynamical systems and neural oscillations.
Ability to work with remote server-based computational workflows, including shell scripting, high-performance computing environments, and cloud-based EEG data processing.
Proven ability to manage research projects independently, ensuring timely completion of analyses and deliverables.
Track record of contributing to scientific publications, particularly in sleep research, neuroimaging, or computational neuroscience.

Desirable Criteria:

Experience with advanced EEG connectivity analyses, including graph theory and state-transition network modelling.
Knowledge of programming languages beyond Python, such as C++, Java, or MATLAB, for EEG and neuroimaging applications.
Familiarity with machine learning approaches for EEG data analysis.

Downloading a copy of our Job Description

Full details of the role and the skills, knowledge and experience required can be found in the Job Description document, provided at the bottom of the page. This document will provide information of what criteria will be assessed at each stage of the recruitment process.

Location: Guy's Campus. Category: Professional & Support Services.

About us

The Sustainability in Research Team works with research and technical communities across King’s to reduce the environmental impact of research. We support laboratories, research facilities and digital research teams to use resources, equipment, energy and data more sustainably.

Our work supports King’s sustainability targets, UKRI Concordat priorities and emerging sustainability requirements for research funding. Following 100% LEAF accreditation in 2025, we’re continuing to help laboratories strengthen their sustainable practices and work towards the highest level of accreditation by 2030.

We also support sustainable computing, waste and resource management, and practical initiatives that help embed sustainability across our research environments.

About the role

We’re looking for a Sustainable Research Officer to help research teams improve the sustainability of their day-to-day work. Reporting to the Sustainable Research & Innovation Lead, you’ll work closely with laboratory sustainability leads, technical staff, researchers and professional services colleagues across King’s.

A key part of the role will be:

Drive Sustainability Accreditations: Guide wet and dry laboratories through sustainable research frameworks, including LEAF, Green Disc, SparkHub, and MyGreenLab.
Deliver Practical Guidance: Empower laboratory teams to adopt sustainable daily practices and co-facilitate interactive workshops.
Advance Sustainable Computing: Collaborate with the e-Research team to help computational researchers optimise data management and computing workflows for lower environmental impact.

You’ll coordinate sustainability projects and be involved in our campaigns, including energy-saving activities, supplier take-back schemes and waste minimisation programmes. You’ll work with laboratory teams to increase participation and support safe, compliant and sustainable waste practices.

The role will also involve coordinating activities, collecting and reporting data and creating clear, engaging communications and guidance.

This is a varied and collaborative role for someone who can turn sustainability goals into practical improvements across laboratory and research environments.

This is a full-time post (35 hours per week) offered on an indefinite contract.

About you

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience: 

Essential criteria 

1.      Experience supporting or implementing laboratory sustainability initiatives and projects that promote sustainable research practices and operational improvements with in a lab environment. 

2.      Knowledge of, and experience supporting accreditation processes for the Laboratory Efficiency Assessment Framework (LEAF).

3.      Understanding of sustainable waste management practices and environmental compliance requirements, including the ability to interpret and apply relevant policies and standards.

4.      Experience organising or delivering training, workshops or engagement activities for diverse audiences.

5.      Strong project coordination and administrative skills, with the ability to manage multiple activities and meet competing deadlines.

6.      Experience collecting, analysing and presenting data to monitor performance, identify improvement opportunities and support decision-making.

7.      Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience producing guidance, training materials, digital content or other engagement resources for students and research lab staff.

8.      Ability to build effective working relationships and engage a wide range of stakeholders, including researchers, technical staff, professional services colleagues and external suppliers.

Desirable criteria

1.      Familiarity with Green DiSC and sustainable data management practices.

2.       Knowledge of best practices in laboratory sustainability.

This is an opportunity for an experienced researcher to make a real contribution both to delivering Lancaster University’s contract with the National Institute of Health Research (NIHR) Research Support Service (RSS) and progressing their own research career, within the field of environmental sustainability in health and care.  

Working with the RSS Sustainability Strategic Theme Lead and a small team of fellow researchers, the appointee will provide expertise in research methodology and topics relevant to priority research areas including sustainability in health and care (focussed on life cycle assessment/environmental footprinting).

The RSS aim is to provide researchers, especially (but not exclusively) those applying for and in receipt of NIHR funding with free access to support and expertise. You will join us on an indefinite contract however the roles remain contingent on external funding which currently is due to end on 30th September 2028.

Postdoctoral Research Associate in Supernova Cosmology

School Of Physics And Astronomy
Location:  Bailrigg, Lancaster, UK
Salary:   £39,906 to £46,049 (Full time, indefinite with end date)
Closing Date:   Friday 06 November 2026
Interview Date:   To be confirmed
Reference:  1077-26

Lancaster University's School of Physics and Astronomy seeks to appoint a Postdoctoral Research Associate in Supernova Cosmology. The successful candidate will work with Dr Mathew Smith on an STFC-funded project to build an independent, homogeneous, low-redshift sample of SNeIa from the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF), and combine it with measurements at high redshift (e.g. from the Dark Energy Survey, the Vera Rubin Observatory’s Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST)) to measure the equation-of-state of dark energy. 

The work will primarily focus on two closely related areas: developing a simulation and cosmological inference framework for the ZTF survey; and measuring and modelling environmental biases, including how these interact with the survey's selection effects. The output of this project will be a low-redshift anchor suitable for use by the Vera Rubin/LSST and 4MOST-TiDES surveys.

Candidates with experience in supernova cosmology are encouraged to apply. The post is available immediately, with an anticipated start date of 1st January 2027 (a later start, up to early Spring 2027, can be accommodated). The appointment is a fixed-term contract until September 2029. 

In addition to joining the ZTF Collaboration, the selected candidate will join the wider Observational Astrophysics group at Lancaster, a friendly and collaborative research environment. The candidate will be welcome to participate in group research activities, which cover diverse topics including transients, high-redshift galaxies, galaxy evolution, gravitational waves and citizen science projects, and will have regular opportunities to exchange ideas across these areas. 

If you have any queries regarding this position, please contact Mathew Smith at mat.smith@lancaster.ac.uk.

Qualifications:
A PhD (or near completion) in astrophysics, physics, cosmology or a related field; strong scientific programming skills (Python); research experience in supernova cosmology, statistical or systematic-uncertainty analysis, or large-scale survey science. Excellent communication and teamwork skills.

Application Requirements: CV, publication list, and a 2-page research statement describing past research experience and its relevance to the project's science goals.

Deadline: Applications received by Friday 6th November 2026, midnight UK time will receive full consideration.

Compensation: Salary commensurate with a standard postdoctoral researcher role at Lancaster.

Application instructions: Applications must be submitted through the Lancaster University online portal. 

Contact info: mat.smith@lancaster.ac.uk

Research Assistants in Biophilic Design and Sleep Quality

About the Role

We are looking for three Research Assistants to support exciting research in biophilic design and sleep quality. To undertake research activities, including questionnaire development, survey administration, data collection and analysis, and the application of quantitative research methods to support project objectives and outputs.

Key Responsibilities

Support research activities focused on biophilic built environments, psychology and user experience evaluation.
Design, administer and analyse questionnaires and surveys to collect user feedback and behavioural data.
Undertake data collection, processing and analysis using statistical and machine learning tools.
Contribute to literature reviews, fieldwork and other research activities in line with project objectives.
Maintain accurate research records, datasets and documentation, ensuring data quality and integrity.
Support the administration and organisation of research projects, including communication with internal and external stakeholders.
Share relevant findings and information with the research team and contribute to project meetings.
Keep knowledge and skills up to date through continuous professional development.

This role offers an opportunity to contribute to innovative research exploring how biophilic design influences occupant wellbeing and experience within the built environment.

About You

You will have a degree (or equivalent experience) in a relevant discipline such as Building Design, Psychology, or a related field, together with an understanding of research methods and techniques within building design and virtual reality modelling.

You will be confident using specialist software and research tools, with experience of data collection, analysis and interpretation. Experience working with platforms such as Revit, Unity, or EEG data collection systems would be advantageous, alongside strong bibliographic research skills and the ability to utilise electronic library resources effectively.

The successful candidate will be able to gather, organise and manage research information from a range of sources, maintain accurate records, and support research projects to agreed objectives and deadlines. You will have good problem-solving skills, including the ability to resolve routine issues independently and escalate more complex challenges when required. Strong organisational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work collaboratively as part of a research team are essential.

We are the School of Architecture, Design and the Built Environment (ADBE) at Nottingham Trent University. We make, create, design and build. We’re planners and problem solvers. We draw lines, and we break boundaries. We are 3,000 students, five departments and one school.

We embrace theoretical rigour and insist on providing hands-on experience for all our students. We celebrate design heritage, and we invite innovation.

We’re a nationally renowned stage for talent in making and design. We investigate the physicality of tools and tech, glass and grass, and bricks and mortar. We also explore the abstract excitement of ideas and creative philosophies.

Research Fellow in Analog Computing for Advanced Communication Systems

The University of Surrey is a global community of ideas and people, dedicated to life-changing education and research. 

We are ambitious and have a bold vision of what we want to achieve - shaping ourselves into one of the best universities in the world, which we are achieving through the talents and endeavour of every employee.  

Our culture empowers people to achieve this aim and to collectively, and individually, make a real difference.  

The role

The Institute for Communication Systems (ICS) home of the 5G and 6G Innovation Centre (5GIC/6GIC) is looking to recruit Research Fellow in Analog Computing for Advanced Communication Systems. The successful candidate will be part of the Wireless Systems Lab group and will have the opportunity to work very close with our industrial partners as well as with academic partners all over the world.

The post holder will undertake research into ultra-low-power analog and mixed-signal computing architectures for future communication systems, with particular emphasis on receiver processing and architectures that reduce or remove reliance on conventional high-resolution analog-to-digital conversion.
 The research will investigate how signal-processing operations traditionally implemented digitally can be reformulated and realised using analog, mixed-signal and in-memory computing technologies. Particular emphasis will be placed on the co-design of algorithms and hardware, circuit- and system-level modelling, and evaluation of the resulting architectures in terms of communication performance, power consumption, latency, precision and implementation complexity. The post holder will be expected to be able to set, define and work towards achieving targets, disseminate results and document work done.
 
About you

ICS is the largest academic research institute in Europe specialising in all aspects of ICT (Information and Communication Technologies). It is home to over 200 researchers with expertise in all communication and broadcasting systems and has developed the best in class large scale testbeds for research and innovation and enjoys the state-of-the-art lab and computing facilities.
 
 Established in 2012, 5GIC is the world’s first dedicated centre in researching end-to-end aspects of 5G and works closely with national and international leading academic institutes and key industrial partners. In November 2020, 6GIC was officially launched with parallel research undertaken in both 5G+ and 6G for 2030+.
 
 The post holder must have expertise in the following:
 •    Strong knowledge and research experience in analogue circuit design, particularly for low-power signal processing, computing or communication applications.
 •    Experience in circuit-level modelling and simulation, including the ability to evaluate power/energy consumption and relevant circuit non-idealities.
 •    Experience or strong knowledge of algorithm–hardware co-design, including the mapping of mathematical or signal-processing operations onto practical hardware subject to noise, precision, dynamic-range, variability and implementation constraints.
 •    Strong analytical, modelling and programming skills, including experience with MATLAB and/or Python, and the ability to communicate research findings effectively in written and oral form.
 
 It would be desirable but not essential for the post holder to also have:
 •    Experience with in-memory computing architectures, including memristive/ReRAM or other emerging-device technologies.
 •    Knowledge of signal processing and communication systems, particularly channel estimation, detection, decoding, optimisation or linear algebra.
 •    A track record of high-quality peer-reviewed publications in analog/mixed-signal circuits, in-memory/neuromorphic computing, signal processing, communications or related areas.

k.nikitopoulos@surrey.ac.uk

About the role

You  will undertake design and computational work on the project “Graphene-Based Programmable Holographic Metasurface Devices for Magnetic Field Beamforming and Beam-Steering at the Nanoscale. The project is funded by a pump-prime grant from the UK Metamaterials Networks, supported by the EPSRC and is a collaboration between the 6G Lab at the University of Sussex and the Graphene Centre at the University of Cambridge. 

The project is led by Prof.  Maziar Nekovee at the University of Sussex.

About you

The successful candidate will hold a PhD, or equivalent research experience, in engineering, physics, electromagnetics, materials science or a related discipline, with strong knowledge of electromagnetic theory, metasurfaces, graphene or related areas. Essential experience includes computational electromagnetic modelling and design using CST, COMSOL, HFSS or equivalent, analysis and design of resonant structures and electromagnetic fields, and scientific programming using Python, MATLAB or similar. Candidates should also be able to interpret experimental data, validate and refine models, and work effectively both independently and collaboratively. 

Desirable experience includes graphene plasmonics, terahertz devices, split-ring resonators, programmable metasurfaces, holographic beamforming or phased arrays, together with an emerging record of high-quality publications and research or knowledge-exchange activity. 

About our School

In the School of Engineering and Informatics we cover the disciplines of computer, electrical and electronic engineering, mechanical, and automotive engineering, product design, digital media, computer science and informatics. Our distinctive characteristics are: creativity, interdisciplinarity, strong links with industries, and an international outlook in both research and teaching. £10m (£4.9m from HEFCE) has been invested in the Future Technologies Laboratory as a result of a 60% surge in applications for the School’s degrees.

Our interdisciplinary approach applies to our research, with current and recent externally funded projects with researchers in a wide range of other subject areas. Innovative research across the School has led to a number of patents which are being commercialised including: novel electric potential sensors (EPS) licensed to Plessey Semiconductors and marketed as the EPIC sensor chip; and University spin-out companies, including InCrowd Sports, and TexRAD.

Please find further information regarding the School of Engineering and Informatics.

The School of Engineering and Informatics is proud to hold a Bronze Athena Swann Award.

Why work here

Our university is situated off the A27, next to the beautiful South Downs where you will enjoy everything that our 150-acre campus has to offer. We are accessible by public transport; Falmer train station is a five-minute walk to campus and several bus stops are located within campus. We also have dedicated cycling paths and encourage our staff to use these with our offering of a cycle to work scheme.  

Sussex is a renowned, multi-accredited, research-led International University and this is only possible because of the people that work here. Whether you are a member of Faculty, part of a Professional Services team or a Student, it’s our people that make us great and we want you to be part of that. 

Find out more about our reward and benefits package. 

Find out about our equality, diversity and inclusion. 

Further Key Information 

Please contact Maziar Nekovee (m.nekovee@sussex.ac.uk) for informal enquiries.

The University of Sussex values the diversity of its staff and students, and we welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

Eligibility

Visa Sponsorship Queries: This role has been assigned an eligible SOC code, however, the role does not meet the eligibility for sponsorship due to its part-time nature. Please consult our Skilled Worker Visa information page for further information about Visa Sponsorship.

The University requires that work undertaken for the University is performed in the UK.

Birkbeck, University of London, is seeking Postdoctoral Researcher to join the Klesch Postdoctoral Fellowship in History of Art and Technology, on a two-year, fixed term contract this Autumn 2026. 

The Klesch Postdoctoral Fellowship supports exceptional early-career researchers whose work is redefining how art history is studied in the age of artificial intelligence and digital technologies.

Applications are invited from researchers working on any aspect of art history from Early Renaissance Europe through to the twentieth century. 

Research Environment

The Fellowship is based within the Vasari Research Centre for Art and Technology and is closely connected to the Birkbeck Centre for Creative AI and the Birkbeck Immersive Learning Centre. Together these centres bring expertise in art history, museum studies, creative AI, immersive technologies, digital humanities and computational methods.

The Fellow will pursue an independent programme of research while participating fully in the intellectual life of the three host centres.

Research Themes

Projects should demonstrate how innovative methodologies can generate new knowledge within art history. Relevant topics may include, but are not limited to:

Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Art History
Museums, Collections and AI
3D Scanning and Digital Heritage
Extended Reality (VR, AR and Mixed Reality) as Art Historical Tool
Network Analysis and Cultural Data
Human–AI Collaboration in Art Historical Interpretation
Digital Provenance Research and Collection Histories
Computer Vision for Art Historical Research
Cultural Analytics and Network Analysis
Geospatial Approaches to Art History

Supervision

The Fellow will also benefit from the wider research community within Birkbeck, with opportunities to collaborate with colleagues in the Centre for Museum Cultures, the History and Theory of Photography Research Centre, and other research centres and institutes across the College.

The Fellow will be supervised by Dr Joel McKim, Reader in Digital Media and Culture and Director of the Vasari Research Centre for Art and Technology.

The successful applicant will receive academic mentoring and career development support while becoming an active member of the Vasari Research Centre, the Birkbeck Centre for Creative AI and the Birkbeck Immersive Learning Centre.

To succeed in this role applicants should:

hold a PhD in Art History or a closely related discipline;
demonstrate an emerging research and publication record;
present an original research project that combines art historical scholarship with methodological innovation;
demonstrate the potential to contribute to Birkbeck’s research environment.

The Fellowship seeks scholars who combine rigorous historical inquiry with methodological innovation. Rather than simply applying new technologies to existing questions, the Fellowship encourages projects that develop new approaches to art historical research through artificial intelligence, immersive technologies, computer vision, computational analysis, digital heritage, or related methods.

Salary and benefits

£44,247 to £50,379, Grade 7 on the College's London Pay Scale which includes a consolidated London Weighting Allowance. 

Benefits of working at Birkbeck: a competitive salary and pension scheme, 31 days paid leave, flexible working arrangements, generous benefits in the HE sector, and being located in the heart of Bloomsbury, Euston, London.

Contract

Fixed-term, full-time contract (35 hours a week), flexible working pattern offered with some remote work but attendance will be expected at Birkbeck regularly.

To apply, please submit a CV and a research project proposal (maximum 2,000 words) and two academic references.

Closing date: Saturday 31 October, interview date: Friday 27 November. 

Enquiries

If you would like to know more about the role, please click on apply below or contact Dr. Joel McKim, Reader in Digital Media and Culture, at j.mckim@bbk.ac.uk

If you have technical issues or difficulties using the recruitment portal, please contact jobs@bbk.ac.uk providing your name and the job reference number of the position. While we are happy to respond to all informal enquiries, only formal applications through the online system will be considered.

We welcome applicants from all sections of the community - www.bbk.ac.uk/jobs. The College is committed to improving the gender and cultural diversity of its workforce, holding a bronze Athena SWAN award and operating Disability Confident & Mindful Employer schemes.

Research Associate / Senior Research Associate in Intelligent Optical Network Architecture
 Apply
The role

Develop the intelligent, resilient optical networks that future AI, cloud and edge systems will depend on.

Join the University of Bristol’s Smart Internet Lab as a Research Associate or Senior Research Associate on HASC Phase 2, the EPSRC Hub for All-Spectrum Connectivity. Working with academic and industrial partners, you will develop programmable optical networks, intelligent automation and rapid recovery from failures, and explore new network solutions using hollow-core fibre.

Our multidisciplinary environment connects optical and wireless communications, networking, cloud technologies and AI, giving you opportunities to turn research ideas into working demonstrations.

What will you be doing?

You will develop architectures for metro, access and data centre connectivity; create automation, orchestration and resource-control algorithms; and investigate fault detection, reconfiguration and recovery. Sensing, telemetry and physical-layer monitoring will inform closed-loop control and resilient operation.

You will prototype and validate hardware or software solutions through laboratory and testbed experiments, using infrastructure including JOINER where appropriate. You will publish and present your findings and contribute to partner collaborations, research proposals, standards and patent applications.

At Senior Research Associate level, you will also take significant research initiative, support early career researchers or students and help coordinate collaborative activities.

You should apply if

You will have a PhD, be nearing completion, or have equivalent research experience in optical communications, telecommunications, networking, electronic engineering, computer science or a related discipline.

You should bring knowledge of optical network architectures; experience in network control, automation, orchestration or resilience; and practical experience of optical communication systems or network testbeds. Programming skills and evidence of research achievement through publications or relevant research and development experience are essential.

We welcome complementary strengths across these disciplines. AI/ML, software-defined networking, automated recovery, fibre sensing or telemetry experience is valuable; expertise in every research theme is not required. Clear communication, teamwork and a willingness to learn are essential.

Research Associate / Senior Research Associate / Research Fellow in Security Assurance for Agentic
 Apply
The role

The Smart Internet Lab at the University of Bristol is seeking an outstanding researcher to join the newly funded AURA (Autonomous Unified RAN Architecture) project. AURA introduces autonomous AI-driven network management across critical network infrastructure, utilising AI agents that sense, decide, orchestrate, and propose configuration changes with minimal human intervention. This role focuses exclusively on addressing the critical security challenges created by the AI-native Future Networks architecture, ensuring the AI management layer remains trustworthy, secure, and resilient to compromise. The aim is to target agentic AI security assurance.  
 
You will be part of a team addressing the security and resilience of private 5G networks deployed across critical infrastructure sectors. The successful candidate will conduct novel academic and high Technology Readiness Level (TRL) Agentic AI security assurance research to characterise threat landscapes, conduct adversarial testing, develop runtime assurance mechanisms, and enforce zero-trust principles on the autonomous AI layer. 

What will you be doing?

Identifying and documenting the threat landscape across the data ingestion, intent interface, and execution layers of the Agentic AI system.
Simulating and demonstrating agent misuse and multi-agent coordination attack scenarios on a live partner platform to establish a concrete attack landscape. 
Designing and implementing intent-to-policy mapping to translate agent intent into verifiable formal policy constraints.
Developing a runtime decision validation engine to evaluate proposed configuration actions against cross-layer security dependency models.
Implementing dynamic trust scoring mechanisms based on historical agent behavior and continuous behavioral monitoring across decision patterns and network-layer security impacts.
Developing automated mitigation strategies without human intervention, including rollback mechanisms and agent isolation protocols for compromised agents.
Publishing research findings in high-impact journals and presenting at leading conferences such as IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy, ACM CCS, or USENIX Security Symposium.
Evaluating research experimentally using the project partner's agentic AI platform and the University's JOINER national open-networks experimentation infrastructure

You should apply if

You hold a PhD or near completion or equivalent R&D experience in computer science, computer engineering, networks, or communications.
You possess an in-depth understanding of fundamental cybersecurity concepts, threats, vulnerabilities, and AI applications in network security.
You have demonstrated experience in Agentic AI security in 5G and Beyond networks.
You have a working knowledge of telecom standards and specifications, such as O-RAN, 3GPP, and ETSI.
You have programming experience, preferably using Python, within a Linux/Unix-based research or development environment.
You have experience conducting experimental research and technical investigations using systematic, evidence-based approaches.
For higher grades (Senior Research Associate/Research Fellow), you should demonstrate substantial postdoctoral or equivalent research experience, independent research leadership, and specialist knowledge in areas like AI/ML security, agentic AI, zero-trust frameworks, and cloud-native observability tools.

The role

The Smart Internet Lab is seeking two highly motivated, enthusiastic researchers of Grade I, J or K to research spectrum access techniques, focusing on automated and intelligent spectrum sharing technologies, looking at both technology enablers and policy consequences for wireless users, vendors, spectrum managers and spectrum regulators using JOINER National Spectrum Facility (JOINER-NSF).

The successful candidates will carry out research for the JOINER (https://joiner.org.uk ) and HASC (https://allspectrumhub.org/) projects.

What will you be doing?

You will work with the JOINER and HASC projects and will focus on spectrum access innovation with particular emphasis on automated, spectrum assignment techniques and the creation of a spectrum digital twin. You will also carry out experimental/proof-of-concept implementation work to demonstrate the applicability of your research. 

 Your main research responsibilities may include:  

Conduct research into spectrum access, sharing and assignment, with a focus on automated and intelligent approaches.
Collect and analyse spectrum data using JOINER’s national monitoring infrastructure, identifying patterns and developing datasets and tools to understand spectrum use.
Develop and test spectrum-sharing techniques using software-defined radio and wireless system emulation across technologies including 5G/6G, Wi-Fi and satellite.
Apply AI/ML and data-driven approaches to spectrum management and contribute to the development of a national spectrum digital twin.
Contribute to the development and support of the JOINER National Spectrum Facility, working with researchers and external partners.

You have a PhD or equivalent research experience in a relevant area, or for Grade K, a relevant postgraduate research degree and substantial research experience.
You have knowledge of spectrum assignment and allocation, spectrum policy and regulatory frameworks.
You have experience with RF systems, wireless technologies and software-defined radio, ideally including USRP/GNU Radio.
You have strong programming and data analysis skills, particularly with Python, C++ or similar, and experience working with large datasets.
You have experience or a strong understanding of AI/ML, particularly its application to spectrum management or time-series data.
You can demonstrate experience conducting research, analysing results and communicating findings through technical reports, scientific papers or presentations.
You are able to work collaboratively across disciplines, learn quickly, take initiative and manage competing priorities and deadlines.
For Grade J/K, you should also be able to demonstrate increasing research independence, publication experience and leadership appropriate to the level.

Research Associate / Senior Research Associate in Evidence Synthesis
 Apply
The role

We have an exciting opportunity for a talented systematic reviewer or a quantitative researcher with an interest in evidence synthesis to join the BEAM (Bristol Evidence Synthesis, Appraisal and Modelling) Centre at the University of Bristol.

BEAM brings together researchers working on evidence synthesis and modelling research across Bristol Medical School.  BEAM is an internationally renowned centre of excellence in evidence synthesis and is the only centre to host all three types of NIHR funded Evidence Synthesis Groups (ESGs), providing access to a wealth of knowledge and expertise in evidence synthesis across a broad range of topics and clinical areas.  

You will work primarily within the NIHR Bristol ESG and NIHR BUcKLES ESG but with some flexibility to contribute to the work of other research groups within BEAM where needed. The Bristol ESG produces evidence reviews on a wide range of topics for the NIHR. The BUcKLES group is the only ESG dedicated to undertaking living systematic reviews.

You will be part of a multidisciplinary team including systematic reviewers, statisticians, information specialists, qualitative researchers, and health economists. You will also work closely with clinical experts and public contributors. 

The post is available full time from the 1st November 2026 until 31/03/2030, but part-time working will be considered at a minimum of 0.6 FTE.

Requests for flexible working patterns will be considered.

Hybrid working is available: we encourage staff to work in the office as face-to-face working and regular contact with colleagues are key to a healthy workplace. The postholder would be expected to attend the office a minimum of 1 to 2 days in a normal working week with no restriction on which days these are.  

What will you be doing?

Projects will include applied evidence syntheses, from evidence maps and rapid reviews to full systematic reviews, and may include methodological work related to evidence synthesis.   You will be required to contribute to:

The day-to-day review processes and research-related administration of conducting systematic reviews and other evidence syntheses.
Developing review protocols, screening studies for inclusion, data collection, risk of bias and GRADE assessments, preparation of datasets, interpretation of data and writing reports.
Narrative and quantitative syntheses (e.g. meta-analyses) for a wide range of projects.
Peer reviewed publications, grant proposals and conference presentations

You should apply if

You have strong training in quantitative research, including knowledge of basic concepts in medical statistics
You have an enthusiasm for evidence synthesis and to contribute to living systematic reviews.
You have some experience of working on systematic reviews, although this is not a requirement and training will be available
You have excellent critical appraisal skills for a range of studies designs
You have a postgraduate degree in a relevant discipline, such as medical statistics, epidemiology or public health: Master’s degree for Research Associate; PhD for Senior Research Associate

Senior Research Associate in Laser Physics for Lithium Isotope Enrichment
 Apply
The role

The University of Bristol is seeking a Senior Research Associate to join an ambitious, industrially funded programme focused on the development of advanced laser-based technologies for lithium isotope enrichment. Based within the Interface Analysis Centre, School of Physics, the role offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to a strategically important research programme that brings together laser physics, spectroscopy, vacuum engineering and process development.

Working within a multidisciplinary team led by Professor Tom Scott, Dr Jacek Wasik and Dr Dave Megson-Smith, you will provide specialist expertise in laser physics and optical systems while helping to establish a new experimental capability. The position offers a unique opportunity to work at the interface between academic research and industrial innovation, contributing to the development of novel technologies with the potential for significant scientific and commercial impact.

What will you be doing?

You will lead the development, commissioning and optimisation of advanced laser and optical systems that underpin the isotope enrichment process. This will include designing and integrating laser sources, spectroscopy tools and optical diagnostics, while ensuring the performance, stability and precision required for experimental success.

A major focus of the role will be planning and conducting spectroscopy and process-development experiments to investigate isotope-selective interactions and evaluate process performance. You will analyse data, interpret results and apply scientific insight to solve complex technical challenges, helping to guide future research activities.

Working closely with engineers, physicists and technical specialists, you will integrate laser systems with vacuum equipment, diagnostics, control systems and wider facility infrastructure. postings.title: Postdoctoral Research Associate (Fixed Term)
postings.listing_context: Postdoctoral Research Associate (Fixed Term) Department of Genetics £37,694-£46,049 Research 30 September 2026 8 November 2026 PC51215
postings.advert_text:
Applications are invited for a Postdoctoral Research Associate position to join the research group of Dr Felipe Karam Teixeira (https://www.gen.cam.ac.uk/research-groups/research-groups/karam-teixeira) in the Department of Genetics at the University of Cambridge.

The Project

We are seeking an outstanding and highly motivated scientist to investigate the molecular mechanisms that drive germline differentiation in vivo. Using the Drosophila female germline as a model, the successful candidate will explore how multiple layers of gene regulation coordinate the developmental switches required for oocyte formation. Our group combines high-throughput molecular and genomic, including short-read and long-read sequencing, with computational analysis, developmental biology, advanced microscopy, and Drosophila genetics. Experimental approaches may include CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing, tissue-specific RNA interference, transgenesis, transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling, immunofluorescence, single-molecule RNA imaging, and quantitative confocal microscopy.

Our recent work generated a systematic roadmap of transcriptional and translational changes that accompany germline stem cell differentiation in vivo (Samuels et al., EMBO Journal 2024; Samuels et al., Development 2025). This work revealed that differentiation does not occur through the simple accumulation of molecular changes. Instead, it is driven by distinct, developmentally ordered waves of gene-expression remodelling that progressively transform a germline stem cell into a terminally differentiated cell.

Building on these findings, the successful candidate will investigate how transcriptional, post-transcriptional, translational, and chromatin-associated mechanisms cooperate to control key developmental switches during oogenesis. The position offers substantial scope for the successful candidate to shape the project's direction, introduce complementary approaches, and develop an independent scientific profile.

Candidate profile

Applicants should hold, or be close to completing, a PhD in molecular biology, genetics, developmental biology, biochemistry, genomics, or a related discipline. We encourage candidates with research experience in germline, stem cell, or developmental biology. Prior expertise in next-generation sequencing-based methods to interrogate gene expression/chromatin (RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, CUT&Tag, Hi-C) and/or confocal microscopy (IF, smFISH, or HCR) would be particularly valuable. Previous experience with Drosophila genetics would be advantageous but is not essential, as appropriate training can be provided. We therefore welcome applications from excellent candidates working in other experimental systems who wish to apply their expertise to an experimentally tractable in vivo model of stem cell differentiation. We are looking for candidates who can demonstrate a solid academic and research record appropriate to their career stage; the ability to design, execute, and troubleshoot complex experiments; rigorous and quantitative approaches to data analysis; evidence of scientific creativity and intellectual independence; excellent written and verbal communication skills; and the ability to work effectively in an interdisciplinary and collaborative research environment.

Click the 'Apply' button below to register an account with our recruitment system (if you have not already) and apply online.

Research environment and development

The successful candidate will join a collaborative and interdisciplinary research environment spanning genetics, developmental biology, genomics, microscopy, and computational biology. The postholder will be encouraged to contribute intellectually to the direction of the research, present findings at international conferences, develop collaborations, participate in manuscript preparation, and pursue appropriate fellowship and career-development opportunities.

Duration

The funds for this post are available for three years in the first instance. The preferred start date is January/February 2027, although some flexibility may be possible.

Informal enquiries are welcomed and should be addressed to Dr Felipe Karam-Teixeira fk319@cam.ac.uk

postings.listing_context: Senior Research Associate in Translational Biophysical Chemistry and Imaging (Fixed Term) Yusuf Hamied Department of Chemistry £42,254-£56,535 Research 15 October 2026 12 November 2026 MA51403
postings.advert_text:
Fixed term: Funds are available for 12 months in the first instance.

Applications are invited for a Senior Research Associate to work with Professor Steven F. Lee in the Yusuf Hamied Department of Chemistry, University of Cambridge.

The post forms part of a translational research programme developing an imaging based drug discovery platform for neurodegenerative disease. Using quantitative single molecule imaging, the programme will characterise small protein assemblies and determine how candidate compounds alter their formation, structure and abundance. The initial focus is alpha synuclein aggregation in Parkinson's disease.

The programme will develop, miniaturise and validate a higher throughput assay, undertake compound screening and generate quantitative datasets linking compound treatment to changes in protein assembly. Working with Cambridge researchers and external academic and translational partners, the successful applicant will help develop the technology into a robust, externally deployable drug discovery platform.

The successful applicant will take substantial independent responsibility for:

Developing and validating quantitative single molecule imaging assays for protein aggregation.
Establishing reproducible workflows for higher throughput compound screening.
Performing screening experiments and developing quantitative approaches to classify and prioritise compound responses.
Building robust analysis pipelines for large imaging datasets and interpreting and presenting results.
Coordinating research across academic collaborators and external partners.
Working with commercial suppliers and technology partners to integrate compound libraries, instrumentation and assay formats.
Contributing to publications, funding applications and scientific leadership.

A central aim is to establish a commercially credible opportunity with a clear route to market. The successful applicant will refine the customer proposition, test the business model and undertake customer discovery with pharmaceutical companies, biotechnology companies and contract research organisations. They will also contribute to intellectual property strategy and commercial positioning, building an evidence base around assay performance, workflow, cost and differentiation.

Applicants should hold a PhD in chemistry, biophysics, biochemistry, neuroscience or a related discipline, with substantial postdoctoral or equivalent research experience and expertise in quantitative biological or biophysical research. Experience in single molecule microscopy, advanced fluorescence microscopy, protein aggregation, neurodegeneration, high throughput screening or quantitative image analysis would be particularly valuable.

Applicants must demonstrate scientific independence, experience of working across disciplinary boundaries and responsibility for complex research projects. Experience involving external organisations, technology translation, innovation, commercialisation, industry engagement or research strategy would be advantageous.

The successful applicant will contribute to the programme's strategic direction and represent the project in discussions with academic, commercial and translational partners. Excellent communication, organisational and project management skills are essential.

The post offers an opportunity to combine advanced physical chemistry, neurodegeneration research and drug discovery, contributing directly to the translation of single molecule technologies towards therapeutic discovery.

Click the 'Apply' button below to register an account with our recruitment system (if you have not already) and apply online.

Please ensure that you upload your Curriculum Vitae (CV), a covering letter and publications list in the upload section of the online application. If you upload any additional documents that have not been requested, we will not be able to consider these as part of your application.

For informal enquiries, please contact Professor Steven Lee at sl591@cam.ac.uk.

Please quote reference MA51403 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy.

The School of Physical Sciences holds an Athena Swan Silver Award which recognises and supports progress in gender equality.

The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society.

The University has a responsibility to ensure that all employees are eligible to live and work in the UK.

Research Assistant

School of Psychology

We are seeking a Research Assistant to contribute towards an extremely exciting 5-year research project, in which we are developing novel treatments for depression and PTSD through the manipulation of memory in sleep.  This role will focus on exploring the use of Targeted Memory Reactivation in sleep to alleviate Depression.  This role requires flexibility to work in a hybrid environment, combining home-based work with onsite laboratory activities. Some laboratory experiments may require overnight attendance.  During the course of this role you may have the opportunity to apply for a PhD.

This project is funded by the Wellcome Trust on a multi center grant lead by Penny Lewis, who specializes in the study of what sleep does to our memories, and is based at the Cardiff University Brain Research Imaging Centre (CUBRIC).

Cardiff University’s Brain Research Imaging Centre (CUBRIC) is one of the best equipped neuroscience institutes in Europe, housing 3 MRI scanners, including a 7T and a Connectom scanner, a MEG, EEG labs, a brain stimulation lab, and of course the state of the art sleep lab.  The Welsh National Center for Mental Health. is situated next door to the building which enables us to work closely with them. The Neuroscience and Psychology of Sleep (NaPS) group is housed within CUBRIC, and conducts world-leading research on the impacts of sleep on cognitive processes. 

For informal enquiries, please contact Penny Lewis: lewisp8@cardiff.ac.uk (please put title Sleep Engineering job in the email subject)

This position is part-time (24.5 hours per week), and is fixed term until 31st May 2029.

Research Associate

 Cardiff Babylab is looking for a full-time Research Associate to join our team which is funded by The James S. McDonnell Foundation (JSMF). Our research examines infants’ and toddlers’ everyday experiences, with a particular focus on how attentional and motor development shapes the ways in which young children engage with, adapt to, shape, and learn from their everyday environments. We combine naturalistic and controlled approaches, using methods such as head-mounted cameras, screen-based and head-mounted eye-tracking, standardised behavioural assessments, observational measures, and computational analyses.

Our team brings together expertise from developmental psychology, computer science, and applied research. We study both typically developing infants and toddlers and young children with developmental conditions, with a particular programme of research focused on Down syndrome.

The postholders will contribute to a range of ongoing projects investigating early development across naturalistic and controlled settings. The precise balance of activities can be tailored to the successful candidates’ backgrounds and interests. There will also be opportunities to work with existing datasets and to take an active role in developing analyses, publications, and conference presentations.

Typical responsibilities may include:

Working with naturalistic audio and video data alongside other developmental measures
Developing and implementing data processing and analysis workflows, including machine learning tools
Using computational modelling to create mechanistic accounts of early development
Supervising and training research assistants and students involved in data collection and annotation
Supporting data collection
Contributing to data management, documentation, and research governance
Participating in lab meetings and wider scientific activities
Leading or contributing to publications, conference presentations, and other research outputs

We are particularly interested in candidates whose expertise complements our work in developmental science, naturalistic measurement, behavioural methods, computational approaches, and multimodal data analysis. These roles offer substantial scope for candidates to develop their own research profile while contributing to the broader scientific programme of the Cardiff Babylab.

These positions offer an opportunity to join an active and collaborative developmental science environment and to gain experience working across complementary methodological approaches and research populations.

Research Environment

The successful candidate will be based at the Cardiff Babylab within the Cardiff University Centre for Human Developmental Science (CUCHDS). CUCHDS provides access to advanced facilities for developmental research, including state-of-the-art eye-tracking, functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), and magnetoencephalography using optically pumped magnetometers (OPM-MEG).

Candidates may also have opportunities to engage with the Cardiff University Brain Research Imaging Centre (CUBRIC), one of the largest and most technologically advanced imaging centres in Europe. Both CUCHDS and CUBRIC are part of Cardiff University’s School of Psychology, which has a strong international reputation for research in psychology, psychiatry, and neuroscience and was ranked 6th in the UK for research power in the 2021 Research Excellence Framework.

The successful candidate will join a supportive, collaborative, and intellectually vibrant community that values curiosity, innovation, and rigorous scientific practice. We strongly encourage applications from researchers from underrepresented backgrounds and are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive environment.

If you are motivated by big theoretical questions, excited by rich multimodal data, and eager to help shape a new, process-based science of development, we would love to hear from you.

For informal enquiries, contact Dr Hana D’Souza (DSouzaH@cardiff.ac.uk).

Job Advert
Research Associate (Qualitative) - 3 Posts
Centre for Trials Research (CTR)
College of Biomedical & Life Sciences

The Centre for Trials Research at Cardiff University is a large, multinational community of researchers, professional services staff and students from a diverse range of backgrounds. 

We tackle the big diseases and health concerns of our time by forming partnerships with researchers and building lasting relationships with the public. Find out more about the Centre and working with us here.

An opportunity has arisen to join CTR as a Research Associate (Qualitative), contributing to the delivery of health and care studies with a qualitative component. The role may involve collecting research data using qualitative methods, e.g. interviews and/or focus groups, and/or participant observation. It may require travel to collect research data. The role will involve carrying out research (e.g. qualitative data collection and qualitative analysis) on a number of different trials and/or studies, undertaking in depth qualitative research with service users, carers and staff. The role will involve working on other studies/trials with a qualitative component too and will typically involve working across multiple studies at one time.

With a culture of continuous professional and career development the Centre has an excellent track record of helping people develop in their areas of interest, with many progressing within the Centre itself, the wider University or further afield.

For informal discussions you are welcome to contact the recruiter Lucy Brookes-Howell (Senior Research Fellow) by email Brookes-HowellLC@cardiff.ac.uk or by phone +44(0)29 20687145

This position is full-time (35 hours per week), fixed-term for a duration of 12 months and available immediately. however this post is subject to a review process and may therefore be extended (or converted to open-ended).

This role is eligible to be offered on a blended working basis, meaning that as well as spending time working on campus you can also choose to spend some time working from another location, e.g. your home. The University is committed to offering this flexibility, wherever the role and business need allows, supporting work-life balance.

Salary: £41,064 - £46,049 per annum (Grade 6)
Appointments to roles at Cardiff University are usually made at bottom of scale unless in exceptional circumstances.

Cardiff University offers many excellent benefits, including  45  days annual leave (incl. bank holidays), local pension scheme, a cycle to work scheme and other travel initiatives, annual increments within the pay scale, and more. It's an exciting and vibrant place to work with many different challenges and is a proud Living Wage supporter. Business needs will require some degree of office-based working but the balance of time can be spent in the office or remotely (subject to agreement with the line manager).
 
Date advert posted: Friday, 9 October 2026
Closing date: Sunday, 25 October 2026

Cardiff University is committed to supporting and promoting equality and diversity and to creating an inclusive working environment. We believe this can be achieved through attracting, developing, and retaining a diverse range of staff from many different backgrounds.  We therefore welcome applicants from all sections of the community regardless of sex, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, trans identity, relationship status, religion or belief, caring responsibilities, or age.  We especially welcome and encourage applications from those from under-represented groups within the University workforce, such as those who identify as LGBT +, Ethnic Minority or those with disabilities. In supporting our employees to achieve a balance between their work and their personal lives, we will also consider proposals for flexible working or job share arrangements.

Applications may be submitted in Welsh, and an application submitted in Welsh will not be treated less favourably than an application submitted in English.

Cardiff University is a signatory to the San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA), which means that in hiring and promotion decisions we will evaluate applicants on the quality of their research, not publication metrics or the identity of the journal in which the research is published. More information is available at:  Responsible research assessment - Research - Cardiff University.

postings.title: Supporting our researchers Find out how we encourage and support research activity at our University
postings.listing_context: Supporting our researchers Find out how we encourage and support research activity at our University
postings.advert_text:
Derby boasts a dynamic research environment and a close-knit community of 400 research students and 300 research-active staff. We are committed to providing exceptional support and encouragement, empowering them to push boundaries, innovate, and succeed in their fields.

Postgraduate Researcher Support

We offer a variety of initiatives and resources to ensure our Postgraduate Research (PGR) students feel supported throughout their journey.

Early-Career Researchers and Academics

If you are a researcher or early-career researcher, we have several initiatives to support you in delivering ground-breaking research with real-world impact.

Researcher Development Programme

Our Researcher Development Programme develops the skills you need for your research and future career. 

Our community

At the University, we are committed to empowering our researchers at every stage of their careers. Whether you are just starting out or leading pioneering projects, we provide the resources, spaces, and opportunities you need to thrive. 

From dedicated research environments and expert training to funding guidance and networking opportunities, our support is designed to help you make an impact. We encourage a collaborative community where ideas flourish, connections are made, and research drives real-world change.

Student and staff wellbeing

Our University is committed to a supportive and inclusive culture where wellbeing, diversity, and opportunity are at the heart of everything we do. We believe that a thriving academic and professional environment is built on respect, inclusivity, and the right support for both staff and students. 

To achieve this, we offer a wide range of initiatives, policies, staff networks, student societies, and events throughout the year, all designed to promote a sense of belonging and ensure that everyone can reach their full potential. 

Explore the support available: 

Wellbeing for staff – Access dedicated resources, initiatives, and support services designed to help staff maintain a healthy work-life balance and overall wellbeing. 
Wellbeing for students – Find guidance, support, and wellbeing initiatives tailored to students, including The Wellbeing Thesis, an online resource specifically designed to support postgraduate research students in managing their wellbeing alongside their studies. 
Equality, diversity, inclusion, and wellbeing for all – Discover how we are creating an inclusive community through policies, networks, and events that celebrate and support the diversity of our University. 

Whether you are a member of staff or a student, we are committed to ensuring you have access to the resources and support needed to succeed and feel valued within our University community. 

Supporting health and wellbeing in the workplace is a key priority for us, which is why we offer the Work Health Hub. This initiative provides tailored training, guidance, and resources to help individuals and businesses create healthier, more productive working environments. And as part of our commitment to fostering an inclusive and supportive research environment, we also champion the Technician Commitment, ensuring that our skilled technical staff receive the recognition, development opportunities, and career support they deserve.  

Events

We value the importance of connecting our research community and sharing the outstanding work taking place across the University. To support this, we organise a variety of events that allow our researchers, students, and the wider community to come together, engage with each other, and showcase the impact of their research. 

Some of the key events include: 

The Annual Research and Innovation Conference – A key event where researchers come together to present their work, share ideas, and discuss new developments. 
The Postgraduate Student Research Conference – An event dedicated to showcasing the research of our postgraduate students, offering them a platform to present their findings and receive valuable feedback. 
Public Lectures – A series of lectures designed to engage the public with important research topics and provide insight into the latest academic developments. 
Professorial Inaugural Lectures – These lectures celebrate the achievements of newly appointed professors and offer them the chance to share their research journey and future plans. 
College-based activities – A range of activities within each College that promote collaboration, knowledge-sharing, and academic growth. 
Annual Images of Research Competition – A creative competition where students and staff are encouraged to represent their research visually, highlighting the diversity and creativity of the work being done. 
Events and festivals, such as the FORMAT – We also take part in larger events like the FORMAT International Photography Festival, which offers a platform to showcase creative research in the arts. 

These events provide valuable opportunities for networking, learning, and celebrating the impact of research across a wide range of disciplines. 

PGR Cafés

Our PGR Cafes provide valuable opportunities for Derby’s research community to connect, share, and learn. The PGR Cafés are specifically designed for Postgraduate Researchers (PGRs) to present their research, network with peers, and engage with fellow students to help build a more cohesive, supportive research environment at the University of Derby.

Library support

The library supports the university research community in realising their ambitions by opening up new areas of knowledge and understanding. Our dedicated Library team supports staff and students at every stage of their research journey, from postgraduate research students to established academics. Inductions, along with training and guidance on publication practice, help researchers develop confidence in research metrics, Open Access publishing, copyright, and how to maximise the visibility and impact of research outputs. Our librarians offer expert guidance on essential topics, including navigating library systems, effective literature searching, and reference management.

The library manages the University of Derby Online Research Archive (UDORA), our institutional repository, which showcases research outputs from the University and ensures compliance with funder mandates and the institutional Publication and Open Access policy. The Civic Collection includes long-form publications authored or edited by University of Derby staff across all disciplines, inspiring students and celebrating the work of our researchers. The Library actively supports Open Research and responsible research assessment, promoting transparency, collaboration, and accessibility in scholarly communication.

Library Services provide access to a vast collection of research materials and content, including over 50,000 journals, more than 450,000 e-books, and an extensive selection of printed resources. Our digital collections and digital-first policy ensure that researchers have access to scholarly content either from our collections or further supplemented through our Interlibrary Loan service, which enables access to a broader network of academic resources. Our Books For You service gives students the option to request books to support personal learning and research, wellbeing and enrichment. The Scan and Deliver service enables staff and students to request a digital copy of any chapter or article that the Library holds in print, facilitating access to printed resources for all.  

The Doctoral College

The Doctoral College is a dedicated space designed to support your research journey, spark collaboration, and create a true home for our postgraduate research community. 

Located on the upper ground floor of the library at Kedleston Road, this space is more than just a place to work – it’s where ideas connect, inspiration grows, and knowledge thrives. Whether you need a quiet corner to focus, a welcoming space to meet with your supervisor, or an environment to exchange ideas with fellow researchers, you’ll find it here. 

Designed with flexibility in mind, the Doctoral College offers a mix of social, networking, and study areas, as well as bookable meeting rooms, a dedicated Viva Voce Examination room, and facilities for both individual and group work. A fully equipped kitchen is also available, ensuring you have everything you need to make the space your own. 

What next?
Find a PhD, MPhil or Professional Doctorate

We are committed to research-led teaching and supporting the professional development of our students and academics at all stages of their career. By joining our active and growing research community,...

Build your research career at Derby

Are you looking for a research career at the University of Derby? Find out more about current vacancies and what it is like to work here.
