Job Description - Postdoctoral Research Associate (26001315)
Job Description
 
Postdoctoral Research Associate (Job Number: 26001315)
School of Education
Grade 7: - £39,560 - £41,885 per annum
Fixed Term - Full Time
Contract Duration: 32 Months
Contracted Hours per Week: 35
Closing Date: 04-Nov-2026, 11:59:00 PM
Disclosure and Barring Service Requirement: Please note that the successful applicant will require DBS disclosure. Further info: https://bit.ly/3DP5K8y
 

Working at Durham University  

A globally outstanding centre of teaching and research excellence, a warm and friendly place to work, a unique and historic setting – Durham is a university like no other.

As one of the UK’s leading universities, Durham is an incredible place to define your career. The University is located within a beautiful historic city, home to a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and surrounded by stunning countryside. Our talented scholars and researchers from around the world are tackling global issues and making a difference to people's lives.  

We believe that inspiring our people to do outstanding things at Durham enables Durham people to do outstanding things in the world. Being a part of Durham is about more than just the success of the University, it’s also about contributing to the success of the city, county and community.

Our University Strategy is built on three pillars of research, education and wider student experience, but also on our keen sense of community and of inspiring others to achieve their potential. 

Our Purpose and Values

We want our University to be a place where people can be free to be themselves, no matter what their identity or background. Together, we celebrate difference, value one another and are each responsible for creating an inclusive community that is respectful and fair for all.

Find out more about the benefits of working at the University and what it is like to live and work in the Durham area on our Why Join Us? - Information Page
W

The Department

We are one of the leading departments for education in the UK, recognised regionally, nationally and internationally for excellence in research, scholarship and teaching. As a large School, with almost 100 staff and over 900 students, we are home to a diverse, inclusive and vibrant community. We are 1st nationally for research impact (REF 2021), 2nd for Education in the Complete University Guide 2026 and 6th for Education in The Times Good University Guide 2026.

The Role

Applications are invited for a Postdoctoral Research Associate, with particular emphasis on young people’s mental health and wellbeing. The research project is an Horizon funded 5 year study developing evidence-based mental health promotion models for young people in education, training, and work across Europe. The project is being led at Durham by Professor Aimee Quickfall, and runs from September 2026 to August 2031. You can find out more about the project on the dedicated website here: https://support-y.eu

The successful applicant will be expected to contribute to the co-creation, piloting and evaluation of mental health interventions for young people, including a web-based tool and face-to-face supportive interventions. Some international travel may be offered but is not compulsory. The successful applicant must be available to attend in person data-collection and meetings in Durham and the wider north of England on a regular basis.

This is a full-time (100% FTE), fixed-term post for 32 months. The successful candidate will ideally be in post by 1 January 2027, with an end date of 31 August 2029.

Key responsibilities:

To undertake data collection with young people and other appropriate individuals and groups.
To assist with intervention activities, such as seminars and workshops and development of the web-based tool.
To prepare and deliver presentations on research outputs/activities to audiences which may include: research sponsors, academic and non-academic audiences.
To publish high quality outputs, including papers for submission to peer reviewed journals and papers for presentation at conferences and workshops under the direction of the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder.
To assist with the development of research objectives and proposals.
To conduct individual and collaborative research projects under the direction of the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder.
To work with the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder and other colleagues in the research group, as appropriate, to identify areas for research, develop new research methods and extend the research portfolio.
To deal with problems that may affect the achievement of research objectives and deadlines by discussing with the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder and offering creative or innovative solutions.
To liaise with research colleagues and make internal and external contacts to develop knowledge and understanding to form relationships for future research collaboration.
To plan and manage own research activity, research resources in collaboration with others and contribute to the planning of research projects.
To contribute to fostering a collegial and respectful working environment which is inclusive and welcoming and where everyone is treated fairly with dignity and respect.
To engage in wider citizenship to support the department and wider discipline.
To engage in continuing professional development by participation in the undergraduate or postgraduate teaching programmes or by membership of departmental committees, etc. and by attending relevant training and development courses.   

The post-holder is employed to work on research/a research project which will be led by another colleague. Whilst this means that the post-holder will not be carrying out independent research in his/her own right, the expectation is that they will contribute to the advancement of the project, through the development of their own research ideas/adaptation and development of research protocols.

Working at Durham 

A competitive salary is only one part of the many fantastic benefits you will receive if you join the University:

•   You’ll receive 30 days annual leave per year in addition to 8 public holidays and 4 customary days per year – a total of 42 days per year. 

•    We offer a generous pension scheme, and as a new member of staff you will be automatically enrolled into the University Superannuation Scheme (USS).

•    No matter how you travel to work, we have you covered.  We have ample parking across campus, a cycle to work scheme which helps you to buy a bike and discount with local bus and train companies. You can also take advantage of our cost-effective and environmentally friendly Tusker Car Benefit Scheme, allowing you to lease a brand-new electric or hybrid vehicle with savings on tax and National Insurance.

•    We have a genuine commitment to developing our colleagues professionally and personally.  There is a comprehensive range of development courses, apprenticeships and access to qualifications and routes to develop your career in the University.  All staff have dedicated annual time to concentrate on their personal development opportunities.

•    We provide wide-ranging health and wellbeing support including discounted membership for our state-of-the-art sport and gym facilities and access to a 24-7 Employee Assistance Programme.

•    Our on-site nursery is rated Outstanding by Ofsted, and you can access holiday camps for children aged 5-16.

•    Our family-friendly policies, including maternity and adoption leave, are among the most generous in the higher education sector (and likely above and beyond many employers).

•    We offer all staff the opportunity to take part in volunteering activities to make a difference in the local community.

•    You can access exclusive discounts via our benefits portal including money off at supermarkets, high street retailers, IT products such as Apple, eating out and days out at various attractions.

•  Various salary sacrifice schemes are also available to help you take advantage of tax savings on benefits.

• If you are moving to Durham, you may be eligible for help with removal costs, and we have a dedicated team who can help you with the practicalities such as house hunting and schools.  If you need a visa, we cover most visa costs and offer an interest-free loan scheme to pay for dependant visas.

Discover more about our total rewards and benefits package here.

Durham University is committed to equality, diversity and inclusion 

Our collective aim is to create an open and inclusive environment where everyone can reach their full potential and we believe our staff should reflect the diversity of the global community in which we work.        

As a University equality, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) are a key part of the University’s Strategy and a central part of everything we do.  We also live by our values and our Staff Code of Conduct, At Durham we actively work towards providing an environment where our staff and students can study, work and live in a community which is supportive and inclusive. 

We welcome and encourage applications from members of groups who are under-represented in our work force including people with disabilities, women and black, Asian and minority ethnic communities.  If you have taken time out of your career, and you feel it relevant, let us know about it in your application.  If you are a candidate with a disability, we are committed to ensuring fair treatment throughout the recruitment process. We will make adjustments to support the interview process wherever it is reasonable to do so and, where successful, reasonable adjustments will be made to support people within their role .    

Contact Information 

Department contact for academic-related enquiries 

Professor Aimee Quickfall, aimee.quickfall@durham.ac.uk

Contact information for technical difficulties when submitting your application 

If you encounter technical difficulties when using the online application form, we prefer you send enquiries by email.  Please send your name along with a brief description of the problem you’re experiencing to e.recruitment@durham.ac.uk 

Alternatively, you may call 0191 334 6801 from the UK, or +44 191 334 6801 from outside the UK. This number operates during the hours of 09.00 and 17.00 Monday to Friday, UK time.  We will normally respond within one working day (Monday to Friday, excluding UK public holidays).  

University contact for general queries about the recruitment process 

e.recruitment@durham.ac.uk

How to Apply  

To progress to the assessment stage, candidates must evidence each of the essential criteria required for the role in the person specification below. It will be at the discretion of the recruiting panel as to whether they will also consider any desirable criteria, but we would urge candidates to provide evidence for all criteria.  

While some criteria will be considered at the shortlisting stage, other criteria may be considered later in the assessment process, such as questions at interview.  

Submitting your application 

We prefer to receive applications online.   We will update you about your application at various points throughout the selection process, via automated emails from our e-recruitment system. Please check your spam/junk folder periodically to make sure you have not missed any of our updates.

What to Submit 

All applicants are asked to submit: 

a CV and cover letter which details your experience, skills, and achievements in meeting (or the potential to meet) the criteria set out below.
A recent example of your academic writing – this could be an academic paper, a chapter of your thesis or other publication.

Next Steps 

Short-listed candidates will be invited to attend an interview, either virtually or in person, and will have the opportunity to meet key members of the Department. Interviews are expected to take place in or around November.

In the event that you are unable to attend in person on the date offered, it may not be possible to offer you an interview on an alternative date. 

Please note that in submitting your application Durham University will be processing your data. We would ask you to consider the relevant University Privacy Statement Job Applicants/Potential Job Applicants - Durham University which provides information on the collation, storing and use of data.   

When appointing to this role the University must ensure that it meets any applicable immigration requirements, including salary thresholds which are applicable to some visas.

Person Specification

Essential Criteria:

Qualifications

A good first degree in education, psychology or other relevant subject.
A PhD (or be close to submission) in a related subject.

Experience

Experience in conducting high quality academic research.
Demonstrable ability to write material of a quality commensurate with publication in highly-ranked journals.
Demonstrable ability to present research papers at national conferences and communicate complex information to specialists and within the wider academic community.
Experience data collection, ideally with children and young people.

Skills

Demonstrable ability to work cooperatively as part of a team, including participating in research meetings.
Ability to work independently on own initiative and to strict deadlines.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, especially with children and young people.

Desirable Criteria -

Experience

Strong publication record in peer-reviewed journals, commensurate with stage of career.
A track record of presenting research at conferences, symposia, or meetings, commensurate with stage of career.
Demonstrable ability to develop research proposals and designs in collaboration with other academics.
Experience of overseeing students with respect to the development of their practical/research skills e.g. acting as a demonstrator; supervising student projects/practicals.
Experience in scaling up research and contextualisation of research findings to other jurisdictions/countries.

Skills

Demonstrable ability to plan and manage independent research. 

Please note that an Enhanced DBS certificate will be a requirement of this post.

 

	
 

 

We welcome applications from candidates with disabilities, neurodiversity and long-term health conditions, and we are committed to ensuring fair treatment throughout the recruitment process.

 

We will make adjustments to support the recruitment and interview process wherever it is reasonable to do so and, where successful, adjustments will be made to support people within their role.

An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Research Fellow to join the Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences. 

This is an academic liaison role funded by the NHS Norfolk and Suffolk Integrated Care Board (NSICB) in collaboration with the Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences, University of East Anglia. NSICB uses Research Capability Funding (RCF) to support system wide research development.

Senior Research Associate
Ref: RA2418

Salary on appointment will be £38,784 per annum with an annual increment up to £46,049 per annum. 

An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Senior Research Associate to join the School of Biological Sciences.

You will contribute to an ambitious research programme focused on developing methods for the site-specific incorporation of non-canonical amino acids (ncAAs) into bacterial S-layer proteins.

S-layer proteins are remarkable self-assembling biomolecules that form highly ordered two-dimensional lattices with tunable pore structures. These materials have significant potential applications in molecular separations, catalysis, and advanced photonic technologies. The project is supported by a prestigious multi-institutional grant funded by the Advanced Research and Invention Agency (ARIA) and involves collaboration with leading researchers across several UK and international institutions.

You will hold a PhD in Biochemistry, Molecular Biology, Chemistry, Biology, or a closely related discipline (or have submitted your PhD thesis by the time of appointment). You should possess previous experience of independent research in molecular biology and biochemistry.

Given the ambitious timescales of the project, demonstrated expertise in expression of proteins in bacterial hosts, protein purification and biochemical characterisation, expression of proteins containing ncAAs, and molecular cloning is essential.

You will have excellent analytical, organisational, and problem-solving skills, together with strong interpersonal and communication abilities. You will be expected to work effectively both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary research team. As the project involves close collaboration with partner institutions, you will participate in weekly online meetings with principal investigators and research staff across the consortium, presenting progress updates and contributing to project discussions.

At UEA, the project will be supervised by Prof. Julea Butt and Dr. Amit Sachdeva. 

This full-time post is available from 23 November 2026 on a fixed term basis for 18 months.

 UEA offers a variety of flexible working options and although this role is advertised on a full-time basis, we encourage applications from individuals who would prefer a flexible working pattern including annualised hours, compressed working hours, part time, job share, term-time only and/or hybrid working. About The Role

Postdoctoral Research Associate

INTERNAL APPLICANTS ONLY

This Natural Environment Research Council (NERC)-funded, full-time post is available from 01/10/2026 on a fixed-term basis for 12 months.

The starting salary will be from £35,302 on grade E, depending on knowledge, skills and experience.

The Role

Faculty of Environment, Science and Economy

The Faculty wishes to recruit a Postdoctoral Research Fellow to support the work of Professor Gabriel Yvon-Durocher on AI4DigiMiC, a collaborative project developing hybrid artificial intelligence models to guide microbiome-driven soil restoration.

Soil microbial communities play a central role in carbon storage and ecosystem recovery. This project will combine experimental measurements of microbial carbon-use efficiency—the proportion of carbon taken up that is retained in biomass—with genomic and environmental data to predict microbiome function and inform future restoration interventions.

The successful applicant will deliver the project’s experimental microbiology programme, working with soil microbiomes and microbial isolates from the UK Crop Microbiome CryoBank. The post will include reviving and culturing microbial communities and isolates; developing and conducting high-throughput measurements of microbial growth, respiration and carbon-use efficiency; and analysing and interpreting the resulting data.

The postholder will contribute specialist expertise to experimental design and method development, maintain reproducible experimental records, and undertake quality control. They will collaborate with project partners to produce datasets suitable for integration with genomic information and predictive models, and contribute to research publications, project meetings and presentations.

About You

Applicants will possess a relevant PhD (or nearing completion) or equivalent qualification or experience in microbial ecology, microbiology or a related field. The successful applicant will possess sufficient specialist knowledge to develop research methodologies and contribute to the project’s research programme.

Applicants will have experience of designing and conducting complex microbial experiments, including microbial cultivation, alongside strong quantitative and data-analysis skills. They will be able to organise experimental workflows, resolve methodological problems and maintain accurate, reproducible records. Experience of microplate-based assays, microbial growth or respiration measurements, and reproducible analysis using R or Python would be advantageous.

The successful applicant will be able to work collaboratively, communicate complex information orally, in writing and electronically, and present research progress and outcomes. They will contribute to proposals and applications to external bodies, manage their work to meet project deadlines, and support the work of colleagues and students as appropriate.

Please ensure you read the Job Description and Person Specification for full details of this role.

Postdoctoral Research Associate/Fellow - Philosophy and Ethics of AI
Posted on 16/10/2026

About The Role

Postdoctoral Research Associate / Postdoctoral Research Fellow (Philosophy and Ethics) 

Salary Details 

The starting salary will be from £34,610 up to £39,906 for PDRA and from £43,482 for PDRF, depending on knowledge, skills and experience.

This full time, ERC funded post is available January 2027 to 31 December 2031. The successful applicant will conduct outstanding, international quality research on the ethics of AI and military decision-making. They will produce outstanding publications in the course of the research and establishing themselves as an expert in the field.

The post

The Faculty is seeking a Postdoctoral Research Associate or Fellow with expertise in with expertise in philosophy, ethics, political philosophy, moral philosophy, philosophy of technology, or a closely related field to work with Professor Anthony King (Principal Investigator) on his ERC Advanced Grant project GENERAL-AI: Artificial Intelligence and Military Decision-Making. 

Applicants must have lived continuously in the UK for at least 5 years and be a national of a NATO member state in order to be eligible to obtain and maintain the required security clearance level for the role. Applications from candidates that do not meet the criteria will not be considered.

Appointment will be conditional upon the successful completion of security vetting.

The Project: GENERAL-AI: Artificial Intelligence and Military Decision-Making

GENERAL-AI is a five-year European Research Council Advanced Grant investigating how artificial intelligence is transforming military decision-making. The project challenges speculative accounts of AI taking over military command by examining what AI can actually do, how military commanders and their staffs use AI in practice, and the ethical implications of its use in war.

 Focusing on AI-enabled high-intensity land warfare, the project combines the sociology of science and technology, ethnographic research, and philosophy and ethics. It investigates the development of military AI by leading technology companies, its use within NATO and European military headquarters, and the legal and ethical frameworks governing its application.

 The project will provide a detailed empirical account of the relationship between AI and human decision-making, while developing new theoretical perspectives on how AI is changing cognition, organisations and military command. Its findings will contribute both to academic debates about AI and to contemporary European security and defence policy.

 GENERAL AI consists of three work packages: Work Package 1 examines the technology itself exploring the development and character of AI Decision Support Systems through engagement with the relevant tech companies. Work Package 2 explores the process of decision-making inside military headquarters. Work Package 3 will examine the ethics of military decision making with AI. This post refers to Work Package 3.

The Role:

The successful candidate will undertake research for Work Package 3 (WP3), AI Ethics, investigating the ethical and legal implications of the use of artificial intelligence in military operations.

The research addresses a central question: to what extent does AI threaten the ethics of military decision-making? Contemporary debates frequently frame this issue in terms of whether humans remain "in", "on" or "off" the decision-making loop. GENERAL-AI develops an alternative approach, examining military decisions as decisions made by human groups in which AI systems, military personnel and civilian technical experts may increasingly be involved.

The postholder will investigate the changing distribution of agency, responsibility and ethical judgement within these emerging human-AI decision environments.

Key responsibilities

The successful candidate will:

undertake philosophical and ethical research into the use of AI in military decision-making;
critically analyse contemporary philosophical and ethical debates concerning AI, autonomy, agency, responsibility and military decision-making;
examine critically the concept of the human "decision loop" and alternative approaches to understanding human-AI decision-making;
investigate whether, and in what sense, AI systems can be regarded as moral or decision-making agents;
analyse the ethical responsibilities of military commanders and other human actors who use AI in potentially lethal operations;
investigate the changing ethical relationships between military personnel and civilian technology specialists involved in the development, operation and application of military AI;
conduct documentary research into national, European and NATO policies and legislation concerning the responsible use of AI in defence;
analyse the application of the Laws of Armed Conflict and associated ethical norms to AI-enabled military operations;
conduct interviews with policymakers, legislators, military professionals, technology executives and AI programmers;
examine how ethical principles are understood and applied in practice by military and technological practitioners;
investigate how ethical reasoning influences decisions concerning the deployment and use of AI in potentially lethal military operations;
contribute to the project's analysis of the human decision team, including questions of collective agency, responsibility, accountability and moral judgement;
contribute to high-quality academic publications and international conference presentations;
work collaboratively with the Principal Investigator and the wider GENERAL-AI research team while developing an independent programme of philosophical and ethical research.

WP3 will combine philosophical analysis, ethical theory, legal and policy analysis, and empirical qualitative research. The successful candidate will therefore have the opportunity to work across the boundary between normative philosophy and empirical research.

The research will examine European, NATO and national frameworks for the responsible use of AI, alongside the Laws of Armed Conflict. It will also investigate how these formal principles are interpreted and applied by the people actually developing and using military AI.

The empirical research will involve interviews with organisations and practitioners across the policy, military and technology sectors. These include relevant EU and NATO bodies, national defence organisations, military headquarters and technology companies involved in the development and deployment of AI.

A particular focus will be the emergence of new human teams within military decision-making, in which civilian technical specialists may work alongside commanders and military staff. The research will ask how responsibility and accountability should be understood when technological experts, military professionals and AI systems are collectively involved in decisions with potentially lethal consequences. The project therefore moves beyond the simple question of whether a human is technically "in the loop" to examine who actually makes decisions, who exercises judgement, and who bears moral responsibility.

Research environment

The successful candidate will be based at the University of Exeter’s Strategy and Security Institute will be integrated into the Defence Data Research Centre, providing access to an interdisciplinary research environment spanning data science, computer science, social science and cyber security. The project also has an international academic and practitioner network spanning the UK, Europe and the United States.

The postdoctoral researcher will also work closely with the wider GENERAL-AI team. The three academic Work Packages are independent but interconnected, allowing the postholder's research on the development of AI technology to inform the project's parallel research into military decision-making and ethics.

About you

The successful applicant will be able to present information on research progress and outcomes, communicate complex information, orally, in writing and electronically and prepare proposals and applications to external bodies.

For PDRA applicants, you will possess a relevant PhD (or nearing completion). For PDRF applicants, you will possess a relevant PhD. Applicants will be able to plan, execute and conduct international level research and publish findings in peer reviewed journals and books.

Please ensure you read the Job Description and Person Specification for full details of this role.

Further information

For further information please contact Professor Anthony King, e-mail a.c.king@exeter.ac.uk or telephone (01392) 723259.

Interviews are expected to take place Late Nov/Early Dec

About the role

The post is funded through a SarcoidosisUK Research Innovation Award and will contribute to a research project using linked UK electronic healthcare records to better understand the diagnostic and treatment pathways experienced by people living with sarcoidosis. You will undertake analyses to characterise symptoms, healthcare interactions and diagnostic delays prior to sarcoidosis diagnosis, as well as investigate patterns of oral corticosteroid prescribing and their association with adverse health outcomes. Working closely with clinical researchers and people with lived experience of sarcoidosis, you will help generate real-world evidence to support earlier diagnosis, safer treatment and improvements in patient care.

What you would be doing

You will utilise large datasets of linked electronic health records and undertake data management and epidemiological analyses to investigate diagnostic and treatment pathways in people with sarcoidosis. You will characterise symptoms, healthcare interactions and diagnostic delays prior to diagnosis, and examine patterns of oral corticosteroid prescribing and their association with adverse health outcomes. You will contribute to developing study protocols, preparing research outputs and manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed journals, and presenting and disseminating findings. You will work closely with epidemiologists, respiratory clinicians and people with lived experience of sarcoidosis and may also contribute to other related projects within the research group. This position would suit an early-career researcher with an interest in epidemiology, health data science and respiratory research who is looking to further develop their research skills and career.

What we are looking for

A first / masters degree (or equivalent) in Statistics, epidemiology or other relevant quantitative discipline.
Knowledge of using electronic healthcare record data to study respiratory disease.
Excellent verbal communication skills and the ability to deal with a wide range of people.

The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity.

You will be embedded in the Respiratory Electronic Health Record group, led by Prof Quint and work with global collaborators.

This is a full-time post (35 hours per week).

This role is for a fixed-term contract for approximately 12 months, expected start date of 4th Jan 2027 until 31 Dec 2027.

About the role

The Department of Chemical Engineering is seeking a researcher to undertake work on the development of a biobased solvent extraction system for recovering biological products. The project will be supervised by Professor Jason Hallett in collaboration with Professor Rodigo Ledesma.

What you would be doing

You will carry out research in experimental design, solvent selection and green solvent extractions for lipid and protein products from fermentation systems. You will be responsible for project management and/or to supervise small multi-disciplinary teams. In addition, you will be submit publications to refereed journals and proposals to attract external research funding.

What we are looking for

You will design, synthesize and test novel solvents to enhance the recovery of fermentation products via solvent extraction.

Some of your key responsibilities will include:

• Working with project partners integrating recovery methods with novel biomanufacturing systems

• Synthesising sustainable solvents (ionic liquids and deep eutectic solvents) based on biocompatible and renewable components

• Designing new extraction processes for recovery of bioproducts such as lipids and proteins

• Performing solvent selection to determine options for further testing

• Performing solvent extractions to optimise product yield and purity

• Assessing product yield and purity through molecular analysis (HPLC, NMR)

The successful candidate will have a first degree (or equivalent) in Chemical Engineering, Chemistry or a related discipline and a PhD (or equivalent) in the field of sustainable solvents, or related to bioprocessing. You will have knowledge of novel solvents and bioproduct recovery and characterisation.

You will be able to perform experiments in solvent synthesis, solvent extraction, wet chemistry laboratory techniques and all accompanying analytical chemistry techniques, produce clear written reports and presentations and have the ability to collect and manipulate data.

What we can offer you

This role is part of the wider European Union project PROPEL: Protein Production in Fully Sustainable Syncells for Biomaterials Manufacturing and Waste Upcycling. The project also involves Imperial’s Department of Bioengineering (Prof Rodrigo Ledesma) and EU academic and industrial project partners in Spain, Denmark and the Netherlands.

· The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity.

· Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression.

· Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 39 days off a year and generous pension schemes).

· Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

Further information

The post is available immediately and the appointment is for a maximum of 24 months. The post is based in the Department of Chemical Engineering at Imperial College London (South Kensington Campus).

If you require any further details about the role, please contact: Professor Jason Hallett (j.hallett@imperial.ac.uk).

About the role

We are looking to recruit a skilled, reliable, and enthusiastic Research Associate who will be funded by Macmillan Cancer Care to work on the analysis of data from the INDIGO research trial (NCT06095024)). INDIGO is the largest ever study of cancer survivors, and has recruited 70 000 patients nationally.

This work will build on our initial work and analysis, and provide the opportunity to apply cutting-edge computational tools to a large, real-world clinical dataset. The aim is to both deliver analyses and use those analyses to inform the development of simple interventions with the scope to improve the quality of life for cancer survivors at scale across the UK.

What you would be doing

The postholder will carry out work based around the analysis, interpretation and publication of multiple cohorts from the INDIGO dataset, and to develop new methods for clustering and analysing free-text data, including linked national cancer data.

They will also be involved in using that information to plan the next phase of trials, including working with other staff in the group.

What we are looking for

You should hold a PhD in Data Science or a related discipline, with strong and significant experience of analysing tabular clinical data. You should have a good knowledge of common statistical approaches and software packages, and be willing to explore novel and developing approaches to deliver more refined insights into the data.

You must be organised, highly self-motivated, have excellent communication skills and relish working towards milestones.

What we can offer you

The Division of Cancer at Imperial College London offers a dynamic and supportive environment for new Research Associates, providing opportunities to engage in cutting-edge research. The Computational Oncology Group is a translational research group that uses computational and mathematical approaches to improve patient care. We have a strong track-record in clinical implementation, and this project offers the opportunity to continue this.

New Research Associates will benefit from access to state-of-the-art facilities and the chance to collaborate with leading academics, clinicians, and commercial partners. This vibrant research community is dedicated to advancing cancer prevention, diagnosis, and treatment through multidisciplinary collaborations, fostering an outstanding environment for both academic growth and impactful research contributions

Further information

This is a parttime, fixed term contract based at Charing Cross Hospital.

For informal discussions about the post, please contact Dr. Matt Williams at email matthew.williams@imperial.ac.uk

About the role

This Postdoctoral Research Associate position is part of a NERC-funded project to develop ChemPI, the first absolute palaeointensity protocol for chemical remanent magnetisation (CRM). The aim of this project is to recover reliable ancient magnetic field strengths from rocks whose remanence is chemical rather than thermal in origin, and to apply the new protocol to some of the most consequential open questions in early Earth science.

All current methods for determining absolute palaeointensities assume that a rock's remanent magnetisation formed on cooling, a thermoremanent magnetisation. Many rocks, especially from the Precambrian, have instead been remagnetised by chemical processes during metamorphism or metasomatism, producing a chemical remanent magnetisation (CRM) whose intensity existing methods can underestimate by more than half. This matters for some of the biggest open questions in Earth and planetary science, including when the Earth's inner core nucleated, whether early Earth had a magnetosphere capable of protecting a habitable atmosphere, and how magnetic fields shaped the protoplanetary disc. You will combine new micromagnetic models, machine-learning inversion of magnetic hysteresis data and laboratory-synthesised CRMs to build and ground-truth ChemPI, then apply it to 3.7-billion-year-old rocks from Isua, Greenland, to test whether the early Archean geomagnetic field was stronger than currently thought.

This position at Imperial will lead the experimental development and application of ChemPI under the guidance of Adrian Muxworthy and Dominik Weiss, whilst the numerical and micromagnetic modelling aspects of the project are undertaken at Edinburgh, and the application to Archean samples is led from Oxford.

What you would be doing

Working with the NERC project PI Adrian Muxworthy (Imperial), Co-Is Dominik Weiss (Imperial), Wyn Williams (Edinburgh) and Claire Nichols (Oxford), you will develop and ground-truth the ChemPI palaeointensity protocol. This will involve synthesising samples in the laboratory and collecting natural samples, making room-temperature magnetisation measurements, and developing micromagnetic models to predict CRM behaviour. Working with Edinburgh, the project will extend a machine-learning inversion algorithm and micromagnetic CRM database to interacting particle assemblages, and contribute to a user-friendly, open-access ChemPI web app. In the final phase you will apply ChemPI, with Oxford, to re-examine palaeointensity estimates from 3.7-billion-year-old samples from Isua, Greenland.

What we are looking for

You will have experience of palaeomagnetic or rock-magnetic measurement techniques, such as demagnetisation, hysteresis or FORC measurements.
You will ideally have experience of laboratory synthesis of materials.
You will ideally have some experience of micromagnetic modelling or machine-learning approaches to magnetic data.
You will have published or submitted first-author peer-reviewed scientific papers.
You will be comfortable working independently and collaboratively across three institutions, with regular visits to Edinburgh and Oxford.
You will have a PhD in Earth Science, Physics, Materials Science, Chemistry or a closely related discipline.

What we can offer you

A chance to develop the first absolute palaeointensity method for chemical remanent magnetisation, with applications ranging from early Earth habitability to planetary science.
The opportunity to work across three leading UK palaeomagnetic and micromagnetic modelling groups (Imperial, Edinburgh and Oxford), combining experiment, machine learning and software development.
The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution

Further information

This is a full-time, fixed term position for up to 30 months.

Should you require any further details on the role please contact: Adrian Muxworthy – adrian.muxworthy@imperial.ac.uk

Research Assistant

Location: Guy's Campus. Category: Research.

About Us

Kings College London is a world leading research-intensive university. The KCL Men’s Health Inequalities Research Hub is committed to improving men’s health in under-researched communities and disease groups with the poorest outcomes. This encompasses health inequalities research in sexual and gender minority patients with prostate cancer and outcomes research in patients with rare genetic disorders like Klinefelter Syndrome. The role will be based within the School of Immunology & Microbial Sciences  in the Faculty of Life Sciences & Medicine, which brings together expertise in basic science, clinical science, data science and artificial intelligence. The Department is highly interdisciplinary and collaborative, with strong links to clinical partners and access to outstanding research infrastructure.

About the role

The Andrology Men’s Health Hub at King’s College London is seeking an enthusiastic and motivated full-time Research Assistant to support an innovative programme of research aimed at improving outcomes for sexual and gender minority (SGM) individuals affected by prostate cancer.

Based within a multidisciplinary research team led by Professor Tet Yap, the postholder will independently lead and deliver to a portfolio of nationally significant projects spanning patient-reported outcomes, health inequalities, digital health innovation, and prostate cancer survivorship.

The successful candidate will play a central role in the delivery of a three-workstream research programme. The first workstream focuses on the validation of a novel inclusive patient-reported outcome measure (PROM) for SGM prostate cancer survivors. This study will compare the new PROM with established UK-based outcome measures and evaluate patient-reported outcomes before treatment and at three- and six-months following surgery.

The Research Assistant will independently lead and manage all aspects of study delivery, including ethical and regulatory approvals, participant recruitment, data collection and management, and coordination of collaborating research sites across the UK.

The second workstream explores barriers to inclusive prostate cancer care through a mixed-methods programme of research. Working closely with patients, partners, carers, and healthcare professionals, the Research Assistant will independently organise and conduct focus groups, interviews, and questionnaire-based studies. The postholder will lead to qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis, identifying barriers to sexual healthcare access and informing the development of more inclusive models of care.

The third workstream focuses on the development, testing, and implementation of digital resources designed to improve support for SGM patients, partners, carers, and healthcare professionals. The Research Assistant will work collaboratively with researchers at King’s College London, Guy’s Cancer Academy, and external partners to lead the design, evaluation, and pilot implementation of digital information resources, educational tools, and survivorship interventions. This will include independently conducting with studies evaluating the integration of these resources into routine clinical practice and future digital healthcare platforms.

This is a full-time post (35 hours per week) offered on a fixed-term contract for 12 months.

The role offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to pioneering research addressing health inequalities and improving prostate cancer survivorship outcomes for underserved communities. The postholder will be supported within a vibrant academic environment and will benefit from King's College London's commitment to researcher development.

Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. This entitlement, from the Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers, applies to Postdocs, Research Assistants, Research and Teaching Technicians, Teaching Fellows and AEP equivalent up to and including grade 7. Visit the Centre for Research Staff Development for more information.

About You

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria

Masters degree in the field of Medical Research
Experience in grant writing
Good IT and analytical skills
Track record in publishing high impact research
Previous/Current involvement in health inequalities research
Previous abstracts/posters at international Urology Conferences

Desirable criteria

Good communication skills
Experience with qualitative research methods
Previous research in high impact teaching institution

About us

King’s College London is an internationally renowned university delivering exceptional education and world-leading research. The University is dedicated to driving positive and sustainable change in society and realising our mission of making the world a better place.

The Strategic Vision 2029 looks forward to King’s College London’s 200th anniversary in 2029 and sets out ambitious plans in five key areas:

•       Educating the next generation of change-makers

•       Challenging ideas and driving change through research

•       Giving back to society through meaningful service

•       Working with our local communities in London

•       Fostering global citizens with an international perspective

As part of the Faculty of Social Science and Public Policy, the Policy Institute at King’s combine the rigour of academia with the agility of a consultancy and the connectedness of a think tank.

This role sits within the Evidence Development and Incubation Team (EDIT), a dedicated evaluation specialist team within the Policy Institute. EDIT partners with government departments, public bodies, charities and other organisations to understand the impact of their work. Our activities include:

•         Designing and delivering impact evaluations to assess the impacts of interventions on key outcomes, using experimental and quasi-experimental approaches

•         Conducting implementation and process evaluations to explore how interventions operate in practice and how they are experienced by those involved.

•         Supporting organisations to develop robust internal evaluation capacity, including the systems, skills and processes needed to embed evaluation in their work.

Beyond individual projects, EDIT advocates for the use of evidence in policy and practice, and works closely with members of the What Works Network to strengthen the wider evaluation ecosystem and promote the adoption of evidence-based interventions. See more at:  https://www.kcl.ac.uk/policy-institute/about/edit

About the role

The Research Associate (Evaluation Manager) will play a key role in delivering EDIT’s ongoing and new evaluation and research projects. Current work spans evaluations of programmes across primary, secondary, and further education; interventions aimed at reducing homelessness; and initiatives supporting young people into employment.

The role has a strong focus on impact evaluation design and delivery. The ideal candidate will have experience working with service delivery organisations to design and deliver robust and feasible impact evaluations. This would include, for example, working with a programme delivery partner to set up an impact evaluation or trial, managing relationships with delivery partners and funders throughout an evaluation lifecycle, and designing evaluations that are responsive to changing delivery environments. As this role has a particular focus on impact evaluation, the ideal candidate will also have training in quantitative research methods (for instance statistics, econometrics, or similar subjects), and experience using R.

We are particularly interested in candidates with experience working with the What Works Centres, and of delivering commissioned research within a research organisation, consultancy, or academic setting. We also welcome candidates who bring subject-matter expertise from working in relevant policy areas, such as education, employment, youth violence reduction, homelessness, or related fields.

The successful candidate will be highly organised, analytically rigorous, comfortable working collaboratively across multiple projects, with the flexibility and adaptability to thrive in a fast-paced research environment.

In your application, please provide a CV (maximum two pages, PDF) and a cover letter in which you respond to each of the essential criteria and, where applicable, the desirable criteria (maximum two pages, PDF).

This is a full-time post (35 hours per week), offered on a two-year fixed-term contract.

Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. This entitlement, from the Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers, applies to Postdocs, Research Assistants, Research and Teaching Technicians, Teaching Fellows and AEP equivalent up to and including grade 7. Visit the Centre for Research Staff Development for more information.

About you

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria

Practical experience designing programme evaluations in collaboration with delivery partners, funders, and other key stakeholders.
Substantial experience managing relationships with delivery partners, funders, and other stakeholders when designing and delivering research and/or evaluation projects.
Training in quantitative research methods, such as statistics or econometrics, and programme evaluation methods, including experimental and quasi-experimental approaches (e.g., randomised controlled trials, difference-in-differences, regression discontinuity) and matching approaches.
Practical experience applying these quantitative research methods in R evaluation or research projects, for instance cleaning, managing, and/or analysing complex datasets.
Excellent project management, organisational and time-management skills, with a high level of attention to detail.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work collaboratively and effectively as part of a project team across multiple projects.
A PhD in a relevant subject or equivalent professional experience

Business unit: Natural, Mathematical & Engineering Sci. Department: Engineering.

Contact details: Prof. Yansha Deng. yansha.deng@kcl.ac.uk

Location: Strand Campus. Category: Research.

Back to job search

About us

King’s College London is a globally renowned university ranked among the top 40 institutions worldwide in the QS World University Rankings 2025. The Centre for Telecommunication Research (CTR) at the Faculty of Natural, Mathematical & Engineering Sciences (NMES) has a long history of performing world-class research in wireless communication research.

CTR was established in 1994, as one of the first centre of excellence for telecom in the UK.
CTR has made extensive research contribution and portfolio in 2G, 3G, 4G, 5G and 6G mobile communications, networking, and applications.
Scientific contribution as well as standard, innovation and proof-of-concept.
Active collaboration with national and international industry.
Some of the first-in-the-world concept 5G/6G demonstrations. 

Applications are invited for one position as Research Associate in Goal-oriented Semantic Networking.

The role will be part of a 6G TITAN Hub, “Platform Driving the Ultimate Connectivity (TITAN)”, led by University of Cambridge.

You will be a conscientious, innovative scientist who has successfully completed a PhD (or equivalent) in Telecoms, computer science and engineering, including electrical/electronic engineering or similar. Experience in designing goal-oriented semantic system and network is preferred.

At King’s, you will join a research-leading and multi-disciplinary team, including Prof. Yansha Deng, and Professor Marco Di Renzo. You will be based at the Centre for Telecommunications Research (CTR) at the Department of Engineering. The successful candidate will also be expected to collaborate with the project partners and members of the research group.   

This is a full time post (35 hours per week), and you will be offered  a fixed term contract until 30th September 2028 

Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. This entitlement, from the Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers, applies to Postdocs, Research Assistants, Research and Teaching Technicians, Teaching Fellows and AEP equivalent up to and including grade 7. Visit the Centre for Research Staff Development for more information.

About you

The roles will involve carrying out research in Goal-oriented Semantic Networking, with the objective of developing goal-oriented dynamic semantic networking orchestration across sensing, computation, communication, and control via simulations and prototypes. The successful candidate will be able to develop skills in the exciting and emerging field of 6G goal-oriented semantic networking.

The role may involve irregular hours, with intense periods of activity leading up to deadlines such as publications or deliverable milestones.

The key challenges on which the applicant will focus can be briefly defined as the following:

Work closely with the Principal Investigators (PIs) to ensure that the aims and objectives of the project are achieved in a timely and effective way.
Write papers for publication in journals and for presentation at conferences, seminars and other research meetings.
Participate in relevant events within the institution or externally, in order to build contacts to facilitate the exchange of information and advance thinking.
Support events, conferences and workshops run by the project to develop the project outputs and research agenda.
Contribute to the development of further research proposals.

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria

Education/qualification and training:

1.      BSc in Telecoms, Computer Science, Electronic Engineering or related area.

About us

​​King’s College London is an internationally renowned university delivering exceptional education and world-leading research. We are dedicated to driving positive and sustainable change in society and realising our vision of making the world a better place. We are delighted to announce exciting new opportunities to join our community.

​

​EMBRACE is a visionary, multicomponent international research programme, the first of its kind in the world, supported by Inkfish with £35M core funds over six years, starting in April 2025. It is a global study of 60,000 participants, including 20,000 mothers, 20,000 infants and up to 20,000 partners.  It brings together world-leading clinician scientists across six distinguished Healthcare organisations, world-leading AI & technology companies, together with premier biotech companies, with the overarching aim to fast-track major scientific breakthroughs, revolutionise maternal and early childhood health through precision-personalised interventions, powered by a groundbreaking symbiosis of cutting-edge AI combined with human support.

About the role

The post of Research Scientist – Maternal Sleep leads a programme on obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) and nocturnal hypoxaemia in pregnancy and their impact on maternal and perinatal outcomes.  The post is responsible for the design and delivery of observational cohort studies and interventional trials of sleep-disordered breathing in pregnancy to generate pregnancy-specific diagnostic evidence in a field where adult diagnostic thresholds are poorly validated. The post holder is expected to secure external research funding and to translate findings into antenatal screening and treatment pathways.

The post holder will work closely with clinicians, researchers, data scientists, behavioural scientists, digital health specialists, and international collaborators across EMBRACE partner sites to develop and deliver high-quality, scalable, AI-enabled research studies and interventions.

The post holder could be a non-clinical sleep or perinatal scientist or a clinically qualified doctor in specialty training or beyond. The post does not include any clinical/healthcare delivery and is categorised by the university as a non-clinical/basic science post. The salary reflects this and is not linked to NHS salary scales.

This is a full time, fixed term contract for 4 years.

Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. This entitlement, from the  Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers, applies to Postdocs, Research Assistants, Research and Teaching Technicians, Teaching Fellows and AEP equivalent up to and including grade 7. Visit the  Centre for Research Staff Development for more information.

About you

​To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

**Essential criteria **

PhD in sleep or respiratory physiology, epidemiology, biomedical engineering, physiology or a closely related discipline, together with relevant postdoctoral research experience
Working knowledge of maternal and perinatal outcomes (hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, gestational diabetes, foetal growth restriction, preterm birth), including experience working with objective sleep measurement (PSG and/or home sleep apnoea testing) and interpretation of sleep study data.
Experience contributing to the design and delivery of clinical, behavioural, population health, or digital health research studies, including ethics approval and participant-facing protocols.
A record of publications in peer-reviewed journals, experience presenting research findings at national/international conferences and applying for research funding.
​Project management skills - ability to work across disciplinary boundaries with obstetricians, midwives, sleep physiologists and statisticians to initiate, plan, organise, implement and deliver programmes of work to tight deadlines.

**​ Desirable criteria **

​Experience of research in pregnant, perinatal or other populations requiring enhanced ethical safeguards, including randomised controlled trial experience.

​Quantitative research skills, including experience of longitudinal analysis using R, Python or equivalent statistical software, or demonstrable aptitude to develop these skills with appropriate statistical support.

Experience of large maternity cohorts, routine data linkage or other large-scale health datasets, including resources such as national maternity datasets or biobanks.

Experience of sleep, physiological or digital phenotyping, including validation of consumer wearables or novel sensing technologies against gold-standard polysomnography (PSG), and/or cardiovascular or placental phenotyping.

​Experience of translating research into practice, including implementation science or health economics, securing or contributing to externally funded research, and/or supervision or line management.

Job Title: Senior/ Research Associate in Plant Biochemistry

Contract: Indefinite with end date (currently 31/08/2028)

Position Summary:

Applications are invited for a postdoctoral researcher in Plant Biochemistry within the Lancaster Photosynthesis team under the supervision of Dr Doug Orr. This new position will join the Plant Biology grouping within the Lancaster Environment Centre, which consists of roughly 35 people including PIs, postdoctoral researchers, research technicians and postgraduate students.

This is part of a BBSRC-funded project that focuses on improving our understanding of Rubisco activity, and pursuing a novel target for increasing Rubisco activity in plants and cyanobacteria. This project is in collaboration with Prof. Martin Cann at Durham University. At Lancaster we will focus on understanding Rubisco activity of recombinant proteins in vitro, and testing these in planta to understand the impact of mutations on leaf level photosynthesis.

The ideal candidate for this position in Plant Biochemistry will have a genuine interest and the curiosity to pursue new research avenues in Rubisco. With training and support, you will be responsible for leading in vitro and in vivo research to advance the understanding of Rubisco activity. You will lead the molecular and biochemical study of novel Rubisco variants to build fundamental understanding, and lead the physiological characterisation of plants expressing these proteins. You will design and carry out experimental and computational work, analyse data, present results in oral and written form and lead the preparation of scientific manuscripts.

You will join the collaborative and supportive Lancaster Photosynthesis team and have access to state-of-the-art resources, including a well-equipped lab for plant molecular biology and biochemistry work using ionising radiation, high-specification plant growth chambers, and the Lancaster High End Computing (HEC) Cluster. Professional development opportunities and training courses to broaden your expertise and skills will be encouraged and are covered by the project.

Individuals from all diversity groups are encouraged to apply. LEC offers a collegial and stimulating environment for career development, based on departmental values and embedded Equality, Diversity and Inclusivity (EDI) considerations and actions. We are committed to family-friendly and flexible working policies on an individual basis, as well as the Athena SWAN Charter, which recognises and celebrates good employment practice undertaken to address gender equality in higher education and research. Furthermore, we are active and progressive around sustainability, wellbeing and social justice agendas.

You will join us on an indefinite contract however the role remains contingent on external funding. This position will initially have an end date of 30/08/2028, with the possibility for extension.

We anticipate interviews will be held within 3 weeks of the closing date, with decisions communicated 1-2 weeks after the interview date.

 

To apply for this post:

In reading your application documents, we are assessing if you are a good fit to this position and if this position is a good fit for you. To be able to do this, we need you to tell us about your expertise and experience to date, and your research interests. We want to know about the skills you had the opportunity to develop, put within the context of your previous study/work environment by, for example, briefly describing the research facilities available to you, and whether you had opportunities to attend conferences/scientific meetings and develop transferable skills. Please let us know if you have had a career break for any reason so that we can consider the achievements listed on your CV, including your publication record, in relation to these factors. 

There is flexibility to appoint either a junior (grade 6) or senior (grade 7) postdoc to this role, with responsibilities and salary set accordingly, and dependent on the successful candidate’s current expertise and experience level.

 

What to include in each section of your application?

Cover letter: Please discuss why you are interested in this position, your career goals, and how you anticipate this position will help you achieve those goals. Please also describe the skills you have developed that are relevant to this post and tell us about any skills you want to develop further. It is helpful for us to know your contribution toward the achievements and experiences listed on your CV that are relevant to this post.

CV: Please include the following sections: Scientific interests; Education history; Professional experience/Employment history; Areas of expertise/Skills; Publications; Presentations.  And, if applicable: Honours/Awards/Prizes/Funding (e.g. travel grant, best poster); Academic service (e.g. review of manuscripts); Outreach; Career development (e.g. training courses or workshops).

Dr Doug Orr d.j.orr@lancaster.ac.uk.

Location:  Bailrigg, Lancaster, UK

Closing Date:   Thursday 05 November 2026
Interview Date:   Friday 04 December 2026
Reference:  1075-26

Lancaster University’s School of Physics and Astronomy, together with the University of Southampton, the University of Oxford, and Queen’s University Belfast is seeking to appoint four Postdoctoral Research Associates, one at each institution, as part of the five-year STFC Large Award “TRANSCEND”.

The TRANSCEND collaboration will use Vera Rubin/LSST transient data and the 4MOST Time-Domain Extragalactic Survey (TiDES) to address pressing questions in modern astrophysics: how stars explode and drive chemical enrichment, how supermassive black holes grow, and the true nature of dark energy. Each Postdoctoral Research Associate will lead one of the following areas and also contribute to the broader science goals of the collaboration:

Simulations and selection effects for SN Ia cosmology and beyond (Lancaster University): lead the forward-modelling of the combined LSST+TiDES sample, and characterise its associated sample selection effects. This project will include building galaxy population catalogues validated against state-of-the-art cosmological simulations (e.g. IllustrisTNG). This simulation effort will be the foundation underpinning every rate, host-galaxy and cosmological result in TRANSCEND.
Host galaxies of transients (University of Southampton): derive host-galaxy properties from LSST+TiDES photometric and spectroscopic data, and use the unprecedented LSST+TiDES transient sample to study how transients correlate with their environments and measure rates of different classes of transient.
SN Ia cosmology groundwork or rare transient follow-up and characterisation (University of Oxford): use over 30,000 spectroscopically confirmed SNe Ia and 150,000 host-galaxy redshifts to improve SNe Ia standardisation and lay the groundwork for using this sample in future SN cosmological measurements. Alternatively, focus on follow-up and modelling of rare transients.
Transient physical properties and the black hole mass function of tidal disruption events (Queen’s University Belfast): measure key parameters such as luminosity and nickel masses for thousands of transients from TiDES and follow-up data to build population demographics, and use hundreds of live TDEs and thousands of host galaxies to derive scaling relations and occupation fractions for SMBHs.

All Postdoctoral Research Associate posts are full-time, funded for 5 years from 1st April 2027. This advertisement is for the Lancaster University post; apply separately to each university for the other three. Applicants are encouraged to apply for more than one post, and, once appointed, all four researchers will work closely, through regular collaboration visits, to maximise TRANSCEND’s scientific outcomes. State your order of preference (topic and institution) in each application.

If you have any queries regarding this position, please contact Mathew Smith at mat.smith@lancaster.ac.uk.

We are looking for an enthusiastic Research Assistant to join the Wirral Child Health and Development Study (WCHADS/First Steps), a long-running longitudinal study following families from pregnancy through childhood and adolescence.

You will join WCHADS at an exciting stage of its development, working on a new Wellcome-funded multi-cohort study examining how changes in social media policy affect young people's mental health and wellbeing. The project will recruit and follow approximately 550 young people aged 9–17 years and their families.

You will take a central role in recruiting and retaining families, communicating with young people and parents, coordinating repeated questionnaire assessments, and responding sensitively to participant queries and concerns. You will also contribute to the development and piloting of age-appropriate psychological measures and study materials and co-facilitate a young person advisory group, ensuring young people's perspectives help shape the research.

The role would particularly suit someone with an interest in child and adolescent mental health and developmental or clinical psychology who would value experience working directly with young people and families within a large longitudinal research study. You will work alongside psychologists and researchers specialising in child and adolescent mental health and development and as part of a wider collaboration involving several leading UK longitudinal cohorts.

We are looking for someone who is organised, approachable and confident communicating with young people and families, including about sensitive issues relating to mental health and wellbeing. Experience of working or conducting research with children, young people or families would be particularly valuable.

The role offers flexible hybrid working. Research Fellow in Nonlinear Photonics

£39,984 - £44,977 p.a. pro rata

Full time/Fixed Term - 2 years starting on 1st January 2027 (with the potential of extension).

About the role

We are seeking a Research Fellow to join an exciting European Research Council funded project focused on nonlinear nanophotonics and nonlinear metasurface-enabled spectroscopy and imaging in the Advanced Optics and Photonics (AOP) Group. The research will explore how engineered optical resonances and nonlinear light-matter interactions can enable new approaches to near-infrared detection, optical frequency conversion and computational imaging.

You will undertake innovative experimental and simulation-based research, contributing to the development of new knowledge in nonlinear nanophotonics, metasurfaces and optical spectroscopy. Key activities will include electromagnetic modelling, developing optical setups, measuring linear and nonlinear optical responses, and implementing imaging and image-reconstruction techniques. The work will investigate resonantly enhanced nonlinear processes, including harmonic generation and frequency mixing, and their application to wavelength conversion and the recovery of spatial and spectral information.

You will contribute to research planning, data analysis, publications, conference presentations and future funding applications. You will also support the wider research environment through collaboration with academic partners, supervision of student projects and occasional teaching of research methods and techniques. This is an excellent opportunity to develop your research profile while contributing to a cutting-edge area of photonics research.

Interview date: w/c 16th November

About Us

The School of Science and Technology at Nottingham Trent University (NTU) is an exciting multidisciplinary environment for learning, teaching and research, with some of the best facilities in the UK.

We pride ourselves on delivering high-quality teaching and diverse, real-world research. We specialise in biosciences, chemistry, computing and technology, as well as engineering, forensic science, mathematics, physics and sport science. This mix of traditional and modern subjects encourages and inspires future innovators.

In the Department of Engineering we deliver research and teaching in electronic engineering, mechanical engineering, biomedical engineering and sport engineering. We are building a global reputation in areas including human performance and human factors, future materials, biomedical engineering, and robotics. We are working with industrial partners in technology, automotive, aircraft, marine, healthcare engineering, and with sports teams to help them beat world records.

SOAS University of London is the leading Higher Education institution in Europe specialising in the study of Asia, Africa and the Near and Middle East.  SOAS University of London is positioned to play a leading role in reimagining higher education globally, with a new strategic plan in place as the basis for the renewal and revitalisation of the School which commits SOAS to both student responsiveness and research intensity. SOAS is moving towards a new model of international partnerships which is responsive to the transnational character of our global challenges.

About the Role

Ethnos-MH, funded by the John Templeton Foundation  seeks to recruit two Postdoctoral Research Fellows for Ethnos-MH, a novel, global Religion and Spirituality (R/S) competency program based on ethnographic methods for mental health professionals, which will be piloted in the United States, United Kingdom, and India. This project is led by Bhrigupati Singh (SOAS, CAMHRA) and Swayam Bagaria (Harvard Divinity School).

The two postdoctoral fellows at SOAS will work directly under the supervision of Singh. Each postdoctoral fellow will respectively oversee either the India or the UK segment of Ethnos MH. In your application, please make it clear in which of these two regions your research and mentoring expertise is located.

These positions are intended to support exceptional early-career academics, with existing anthropological training at doctoral and/or postdoctoral level in anthropology, religion and mental health. The fellows will be directly involved in the design, execution, and mentoring segments of the Ethnos-MH training program. 

More information about the project is available here: https://www.templeton.org/grant/developing-a-global-training-program-in-ethnographic-methods-to-enhance-r-s-competencies-for-mental-health-professionals-ethnos-mh  

About the Department

The Centre for Anthropology and Mental Health Research in Action (CAMHRA) is a globally oriented and locally connected Centre of excellence for cutting edge anthropological research, education and public engagement in the field of mental health. It works to promote research on critical issues of inequality in access, experience and outcomes of mental health care with benefits for marginalised groups in the London area and cascading effects at national and global levels, and with special emphasis on mental health lived-experience and clinical practice-based research, and coproduced research outputs.
