postings.advert_text:
Research Fellow in Multimodal Physics-Informed Foundation Model for Air Quality Applications

The University of Surrey is a global community of ideas and people, dedicated to life-changing education and research.

We have a bold vision of what we want to achieve - shaping ourselves into one of the best universities in the world, which we are achieving through the talents and endeavour of every employee.

Our culture empowers people to achieve this aim and to make a real difference.

The role

Do you want to build the first-ever Foundation Model for air quality? We are looking for a world-class AI researcher to join the FMAI4Air project, a high-stakes mission to revolutionise how we predict air pollution, evaluating its impacts on people’s health and protecting millions of lives.

This isn't just another incremental AI project; we are pioneering a Physics-Informed Multimodal High-Resolution Foundation Model. You will be at the intersection of deep learning and atmospheric sciences, working within the prestigious and word-leading ecosystem of Surrey's PAI, CVSSP and GCARE, under the leadership of Assoc Prof Erick Sperandio. Your role will be: 

Architect the Future of AI for Environmental Sciences: Design and pre-train a novel, task-agnostic, multimodal, high-resolution and physics-informed Foundation Model (FM) for air quality prediction that fuses heterogeneous data, from satellite imagery and surface sensors to meteorological grids and emissions inventories, and evaluates the impacts of air pollution on people’s health.
Bridge AI and Atmospheric Physics: Move beyond the "black box" by embedding physical constraints (such as advection-diffusion equations) directly into the model architecture to ensure scientific consistency, interpretability and trustworthiness.
Push the Resolution Limit: Implement state-of-the-art super-resolution and downscaling techniques to translate coarse global data into street-level, actionable insights.
Solve Real-World Grand Challenges: Fine-tune the pretrained FM for critical downstream applications, including early-warning systems for wildfires and simulating urban air-quality mitigation scenarios to inform government policy through a web-based application for FMAI4Air proof-of-concept.
Leverage High-Performance Computing: Pretrain and fine-tune the models on world-leading HPC infrastructure, including Surrey’s AI@Surrey and the national Isambard-AI HPC.
Collaborate Nationally and Globally: You will work alongside a powerhouse consortium including Imperial College London, the University of Manchester, and NTNU (Norway), as well as with consortium partners from academia including IAG-USP (Brazil), NC Climate Office at NCSU (USA), Chiba University (Japan), from industry including NVIDIA and WSP Global, and from government such as Guildford Borough Council. 

About you

Expertise in designing and training large-scale Deep Learning architectures (e.g., Transformers, Mamba, or similar spatiotemporal models).
Proven experience in multimodal data fusion (handling a mix of time-series, imagery, and tabular data).
Strong proficiency in PyTorch and Tensorflow, and experience deploying models on HPC clusters and on the edge for fast and efficient inference.
Expertise in developing and deploying Web applications that will be used to operationalise FMAI4Air models for policy and decision making.
A solid mathematical foundation in calculus and linear algebra, with the ability to implement physics-informed constraints into neural networks’ loss functions.
A track record of publishing high-quality research in top-tier AI or environmental science conferences/journals.
Commitment to deliver high-quality research and innovation outcomes, including publishing papers in top-tier venues, and support research, dissemination, communication and management activities.

How to apply

To apply please submit your CV and a cover letter via our website.

For an informal conversation about the role please contact Erick Sperandio via erick.sperandio@surrey.ac.uk

Research Assistant for Lunar In-Situ Resource Propellant Extraction

The University of Surrey is a global community of ideas and people, dedicated to life-changing education and research.

We are seeking two part-time Research Assistants (0.33 FTE) to support MAGPIE, a European Space Agency-funded project investigating whether magnesium derived from lunar material could serve as a practical feedstock for electric propulsion. The nine-month project brings together the University of Surrey and Eos Space Technology Ltd.

The roles offer an opportunity to contribute to lunar resource research and to prepare high-temperature experiments at Surrey Space Centre, working with the project team under the supervision of Dr Sungwoo Lim and Dr Andrea Lucca Fabris. These are fixed-term positions until June 2027.

The role

The two Research Assistants will undertake complementary activities.

Lunar resources and feedstock assessment

You will review published measurements of lunar samples and composition maps to assess magnesium abundance and the minerals that contain it. You will compare these findings with available lunar regolith simulants and help select a representative material for laboratory testing. You will also conduct chemical and mineralogical characterisation. Your work will provide a documented feedstock specification and estimates of magnesium availability for extraction and for system studies.

Extraction assessment and laboratory investigation

You will compare molten regolith electrolysis, carbothermal reduction and vacuum pyrolysis using published evidence and preliminary thermodynamic, mass and energy calculations. You will help prepare the experimental plan, vapour-collection interfaces and analytical methods for a high-temperature vacuum furnace. You will also conduct laboratory experiments and analyse the feed, residue and collected deposits to assess magnesium redistribution or recovery.

Both roles will involve maintaining research records, interpreting results, and contributing to technical reports and project meetings.

About you

You will have a degree in a relevant subject, such as space engineering, chemical engineering, materials science, chemistry, physics or planetary science, or equivalent experience.

You will need:

The ability to critically review scientific literature and to interpret quantitative data.
Relevant knowledge of mineralogy or geochemistry for the resource role, or of thermal processing, thermodynamics or experimental engineering for the extraction role.
The ability to perform scientific calculations and to document methods, assumptions and results clearly.
An organised approach to research, strong written communication, and the ability to work with colleagues across disciplines.
For duties involving laboratory work, the ability to follow approved procedures and work safely, with appropriate training and supervision.

To apply, please submit your CV and cover letter via the University website.

About the role

The University of Sussex is seeking to appoint a Research Assistant to join Clean Slate at Scale, a major Innovate UK-funded collaborative research project evaluating a novel digitally enabled alcohol detoxification and recovery service across Kent, Surrey and Sussex.

The Research Assistant will play a central role in the University's evaluation work package. Working closely with Dr Faith Matcham and colleagues across Sussex and partner organisations, the postholder will support study set-up, ethics and governance activities, participant follow-up, data collection, data management, analysis, dissemination, and patient and public involvement activities.

The postholder will be part of a collaborative and multidisciplinary team spanning psychology, public health, health economics, clinical services, and digital health innovation. The role offers experience across the full research lifecycle, from study set-up, ethics and governance activities, and data collection through to analysis, dissemination, and research impact. Working closely with NHS, academic, industry, and public contributors, the successful candidate will have opportunities to contribute to publications, conference presentations, and the development of future research. This post would be particularly suitable for an individual seeking to develop a career in health, psychological, public health, or applied research, including those considering future doctoral study.

About you

You will have a degree in Psychology, Public Health, Health Sciences, Social Sciences, Epidemiology, or a related discipline, and experience supporting health, clinical, psychological, or applied research projects. You will be highly organised, with excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage research data accurately and securely.

You will be a strong communicator who is comfortable working both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team. You will have the ability to manage your workload effectively, contribute to multiple aspects of a research project, and build positive working relationships with academic, NHS, industry, and public stakeholders.

Ideally, you will have experience of participant-facing research activities, such as recruitment, interviews, or outcome assessments, and some familiarity with research ethics, governance processes, and data analysis. Experience of quantitative and/or qualitative research methods would be advantageous, as would an interest in digital health, addiction, mental health, public health, or health services research.

This role would suit someone seeking to develop a career in health or applied research, including individuals considering future doctoral study. extensive practical and formal training

Job description

Role:  Research Assistant in Software Engineering and AI

Department:  School of Computing, Engineering and Intelligent Systems (Intelligent Systems Research Centre)

Grade: 6 (£33,680 per annum)

Responsible to: Principal Investigator

Campus: Derry~Londonderry

Fixed-Term until 31st March 2027 / Full-time 

Due to the short-term nature of this post, the successful candidate must be available to commence immediately and will be required to hold proof of right to work in the UK at the time of application and for the duration of the post.

Job Purpose:

The AI-EPOCMON team at the Intelligent Systems Research Centre (ISRC) is seeking a motivated Research Assistant with strong software engineering skills and experience in AI. The post will support the completion of the software delivery work package of a US-Ireland Centre-to-Centre project developing an AI-driven, low-cost, multianalyte point-of-care platform for detecting systemic therapeutic concentrations in biofluids.

The project showcases the platform's ability to measure anti-epileptic drug levels in patients with epilepsy. It combines advanced AI techniques with sensor technologies, including surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) and electrochemical detection, to analyse complex multimodal patient data. The Research Assistant will develop, test and integrate robust software that incorporates deep learning and evolutionary optimisation algorithms, and will help turn the project's AI models into real-time prototypes ready for delivery.

The post-holder will work with the project team at Ulster University and with partners at Dublin City University (DCU), Trinity College Dublin (TCD) and Texas A&M University. They will contribute to data management and analysis, to software and prototype development, and to reporting and disseminating project outcomes, including journal publications.

Location: 	Aston University Main Campus

Release Date: 	Monday 12 October 2026

We are seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Associate to join a newly funded BBSRC Pioneer Award exploring the fundamental principles that govern mammalian membrane protein folding and assembly during biogenesis using dynamic mass photometry (DMP), a label-free single particle tracking technique.

This position is embedded within the vibrant, collaborative environment of the Aston Institute for Membrane Excellence (AIME). AIME is a first-of-its-kind institute that synergistically combines world-leading expertise in membrane biology and novel polymer chemistries. 

In this highly collaborative project, the successful candidate will combine cell-free methodologies to track mammalian membrane protein synthesis on ribosomes, using DMP to visualise membrane protein insertion, folding, and assembly within artificial lipid bilayers which mimic mammalian lipid composition. 

We are looking for candidates with a strong background in membrane biology protein and lipid biochemistry, or microscopy and image analysis, and a passion for applying multidisciplinary methods to understand de novo membrane protein folding. The ability to rapidly learn new techniques is highly desirable, and enthusiasm for working across disciplinary boundaries is essential. Full training will be provided where needed. We are seeking a postdoctoral researcher to join the AHRC-DFG funded project Forging And Belonging: Researching children's social relations and Imagined futures through Crafting in rural West Africa (FABRIC).

FABRIC is a three-year AHRC-DFG funded project investigating how the changing value of craft in Senegal and Benin shapes social belonging and imagined futures of teenagers in craft families. We have collected ethnographic data from families in three villages in each country. You will have access to this data and will collaborate with the co-Investigators in analysing and writing up the ethnographic material.

This is a highly innovative research project about how the changing economic, ecological, epistemological and cultural value of crafts in West Africa shapes social belonging and imagined futures of teenagers in craft families. Researchers in Benin and Senegal have completed participant ethnographies with potters, weavers and blacksmiths, conducted qualitative interviews with a range of interested actors in each country, and future-me workshops with children in craft families. You will collaborate with the research team on the analysis of this data and on writing research outputs. You will have completed a doctorate in anthropology, sociology or archeology and have knowledge of West African culture and society. Ideally, you should be fluent in French and Wolof or Baatonum.

This opportunity would build on experience developed during PhD and postdoctoral research in the anthropology or sociology of material culture, especially with regard to West African cultures.

Contract

This role is offered on a fixed-term basis for 11 and half months.

This is a part-time role working 21 hours per week. You need to be based in the UK and able to come to the office at least one day a week but you can work remotely for up to 14 hours per week, by arrangement.

Interviews will be held on November 13 2026.

Salary and benefits

£27,079 rising to £30,832 per annum pro rata (60% of £45,132.00 rising to £51,387.00 FTE)

Birkbeck offers a competitive salary and pension scheme, 31 days paid leave, flexible working arrangements and some of the most generous benefits in the HE sector, all while being located right in the heart of Central London.

The salary quoted is on the College's London Pay Scale which includes a consolidated Weighting/Allowance which applies only to staff whose normal contractual place of work is in the London area.

Enquiries

If you would like to know more about the role, please click on apply below or contact Karen Wells, Professor International Development and Childhood Studies, PI FABRIC, k.wells@bbk.ac.uk

If you have technical issues or difficulties using the recruitment portal, please contact jobs@bbk.ac.uk providing your name and the job reference number of the position. While we are happy to respond to all informal enquiries, only formal applications through the online system will be considered.

We welcome applicants from all sections of the community. The College is committed to improving the gender and cultural diversity of its workforce, holding an Athena Swan and Race Equality Charter awards and operating Disability Confident & Mindful Employer schemes.

We are seeking a motivated Research Fellow to join the University of Brighton’s team within RESCu-M², the EPSRC Manufacturing Research Hub in Robotics, Automation and Smart Machine Enabled Sustainable Circular Manufacturing and Materials.

RESCu-M² aims to advance circular manufacturing through robotics, artificial intelligence and intelligent automation, enabling more effective reuse, repair, repurposing, remanufacturing and recycling. Led by the University of Birmingham, the hub brings together the universities of Brighton, Strathclyde, Leeds, Sheffield and Loughborough, industry partners, standard agency, city councils to deliver cutting-edg research and impacts

About the role

At Research Fellow level (AC2), staff are expected to be involved in the developing, planning and managing of research projects in consultation with a Principal Investigator, developing a publication record and learning to generate funding and supervise less experienced researchers. The role will normally require a level of research knowledge, skill, and experience equivalent to PhD. Research Fellows may also be expected to contribute to the teaching and/or consultancy activities to ensure continuous development of knowledge in the subject area.

Working with Professor Yan Wang and colleagues across the hub, you will undertake research to improve the assessment, recovery and continued use of products, components and materials. You will contribute to Brighton’s research in inspection, sensing and analysis; testing, validation and certification, robotics; and circular business models.

The role offers opportunities to collaborate with researchers across the partner universities and work with industry to develop and validate practical solutions. You will also support Brighton’s role as the hub’s south-east regional spoke, helping manufacturers access research expertise and develop circular manufacturing capabilities.

Your responsibilities will include:

Designing and conducting research into circular manufacturing and value retention processes.

Developing and evaluating methods to assess product or component condition, performance and suitability for further use.

Working with academic and industrial partners to identify challenges, collect and analyse data, and validate research outcomes.

Publishing findings and contributing to project reports, conferences and knowledge exchange activities.

Supporting the wider research team and contributing to student research where appropriate.

The successful candidate will have:

A PhD in design, manufacturing, circular economy or life extension, or equivalent experience
Sufficient, up-to-date breadth or depth of specialist knowledge and research experience in one or more relevant areas.
Experience in applying appropriate research methods to engineering or quantitative problems, which may include engineering design and analysis, circular manufacturing, intelligent systems, data analysis.
Ability to conduct high-quality independent and collaborative research, analyse and interpret results, and communicate research findings effectively.

This role is a fixed term position for 24 months and is not available on a job share arrangement due to it being 0.5 full-time equivalent.

EPSRC Postdoctoral Pathway Fellow

The role

The EPSRC Postdoctoral Pathway supports EPSRC-funded PhD graduates who are excited about taking the first steps towards research independence with a two-year Fellowship at the University of Bristol. The scheme offers the opportunity to launch your own, independent research career in an exciting and innovative research environment.

Postdoctoral Pathway Fellows will propose their own bespoke programme to conduct innovative research at the frontiers of Science and Engineering.

Project proposals are invited across the full range of topics in the EPSRC research portfolio EPSRC strategy, remit and programmes – UKRI.

Successful applicants will have the chance to take their research to the next level, whether by delivering high-impact original research, or by exploiting new interdisciplinary research opportunities. The Postdoctoral Pathway award should not be viewed as an opportunity to complete PhD work.

What will you be doing?

Successful applicants will receive funding for up to 2 years.

Benefits include:

Work within world-class research groups at the University of Bristol
In addition to a Project Sponsor (a Bristol academic staff member supporting your project proposal), you will have access to an academic mentor for advice on research and career development
Access to personal and professional development opportunities.

Postdoctoral Pathway Fellows will be recruited at Grade J on the University of Bristol salary scale and receive a grant of £5,000 for research costs.

You should apply if

This scheme is designed to support Early Career Researchers who are nearing completion of their PhD or have recently completed it.

Eligibility criteria:

All applicants must have received PhD studentship support from EPSRC (stipend and/or fees) or training award, for example CDT, ICASE, or IDLA studentship
Applicants must not hold a permanent academic position
Applicants must have submitted their PhD thesis before the post begins and meet either of the following two requirements:
Applicants who have recently completed their PhD they must have had their viva on or after 1st November 2025 (12 months prior to the application deadline)
Applicants who are near completion of their PhD must intend to submit their doctoral thesis on or before 31st January 2027 (within 3 months of the application deadline). If they do not submit their thesis by this date, the award offer will be withdrawn. Applicants who are yet to submit must include a statement of support from their PhD supervisor confirming their expected submission timeline.

 

Additional information

Whilst this vacancy is administratively linked to the School of Engineering Mathematics & Technology (SEMT), applications are welcomed from eligible candidates across all Schools

To apply for this role please download and complete the attached documents (as specified in the Application Guidance). Alongside completing the other sections of the application, the additional documents should be uploaded to the ‘Other documents' section of the application portal. Please see the Application Guidance for more details. Please contact doctoral-prize@bristol.ac.uk with any queries.

The interview date is anticipated to take place on Thursday 10th December 2026

Postdoctoral Research Associate In The Development of Novel Synthetic Boron-based Methodologies
 Apply
The role

Three postdoctoral research associate positions are available to work in the Aggarwal Lab (http://www.chm.bris.ac.uk/org/aggarwal/) to work on the development of novel synthetic boron-based methodologies.

The three positions are subject to fixed term funding between the following dates:

Position 1 - 1st January 2027 to 31st December 2027
Position 2 - 7th January 2027 to 6th January 2028
Position 3 - 11th January 2027 to 10th June 2028 

What will you be doing?

The PDRA will be required to work on multiple projects simultaneously, but their primary responsibility will be on the design and synthesis of complex molecules, and the development of new synthetic methodology using boron chemistry. We will use lithiation-borylation to grow carbon chains as well as larger building blocks to make C-C bonds. The researcher will employ their synthetic expertise to advance the project.  The research program will require a deep understanding of the processes involved together with strong grasp of fundamentals of organic synthesis for a successful outcome.

The successful candidate will have excellent opportunities to develop supervisory, written, teaching and organisational skills and therefore this post provides ideal training for a career in industry or academia. Duties may also include helping with the training and supervision of PhD and final year project students. The successful candidate will be accountable to Professor Aggarwal FRS and to Professor Crump as Head of the Organic and Biological Chemistry Section of the School of Chemistry.

You should apply if

•    Recent experience in synthetic organic chemistry.
•    Be able to plan and execute experimental work involved in organic syntheses successfully and safely with minimal supervision.
•    The ability to carry out, interpret and properly record the results of modern spectroscopic techniques, including NMR.
•    Familiarity with online database searching e.g. Belstein and Chemical Abstracts for use in the selection and planning of experimental work.
•    Excellent written and oral communication skills 
•    The ability to become part of a team working on the research project and to demonstrate the ability to work at this level, in particular to work supportively in a laboratory environment with junior co-workers as well as other research assistants.
•    The ability to present work in a clear and concise manner. 
•    The successful candidate will be asked to submit written reports of their experimental results as required for the information of the supervisor.
•    A body of published work in peer-reviewed learned journals relevant to the advertised post.
•    The ability to meet deadlines and excellent organisational skills.

Additional information

Contract type: Fixed term. If you are applying for a specific position please note this in your application. Applicants who do not specify may be considered for all posts.

Research Associate / Senior Research Associate in Neural Control of Cardioprotection
 Apply
The role

A Research Associate or Senior Research Associate is sought to join a British Heart Foundation-funded research programme investigating the neural control of cardioprotection and cardiac microcirculation. The project addresses how metabolic and oxidative stressors influence cardiac microcirculation at the cellular level, and how central brain circuits mediate cardioprotection and can be harnessed to promote angiogenesis in the infarcted heart. The work spans in vitro, ex vivo and in vivo approaches, including viral vector-based circuit mapping, human cell culture models and surgical models of myocardial infarction and heart failure. The grade of appointment (Grade I or J) will depend on the successful candidate's qualifications and experience. The project is funded for 2 years initially.

Hybrid working is not available for this role. 

What will you be doing?

You will plan, carry out and analyse experiments spanning in vitro, ex vivo and in vivo approaches. This includes performing in vivo surgical procedures (induction of myocardial infarction/heart failure, stereotaxic viral vector injections), designing viral vectors for neuronal circuit mapping, carrying out cell culture with primary cells and human hPSC-derived models, and performing advanced in vivo imaging (laser Doppler/laser speckle, echocardiography). A Senior Research Associate (Grade J) will independently plan and lead complex, multi-technique experiments, manage transgenic mouse colonies, and contribute ideas for the enhancement of techniques and methodologies. A Research Associate (Grade I) will carry out these activities under the close supervision of the PI. Both roles contribute to manuscript and grant preparation, literature review, and dissemination at scientific meetings.

You should apply if

You are passionate about cardiovascular and neuroscience research and have proven skills in critical thinking and problem-solving. For appointment at either grade, you will have hands-on experience with in vivo surgical procedures in rodents, including induction of myocardial infarction/heart failure and/or stereotaxic surgery, and demonstrated proficiency in at least three advanced technique areas such as cell culture (primary cells, human iPSC/hPSC-derived models), in vivo models of cardiac pathology, advanced in vivo imaging (e.g. echocardiography, Laser Doppler/Laser Speckle, 2P), stereotaxic surgery and viral vector delivery, viral vector design, or Ca²⁺ imaging. A Research Associate (Grade I) will have a PhD in a relevant subject or be working towards one. A Senior Research Associate (Grade J) will hold a PhD, have postdoctoral research experience (or equivalent) in a relevant field, a track record of first-author publications in peer-reviewed journals, and presentations at scientific conferences.

Additional information

Contract type: Open ended with funding until 30/09/2028 (start date – as soon as possible)

Work pattern: Full-time (100% FTE)

Grade: Grade I or J/Pathway 2

Salary: £39,906 - £44,746 (grade I), £44,746 - £50,253 (grade J) per annum

School/Unit: Bristol Medical School

Shift pattern: 35 hours per week

This advert will close at 23:59 UK time on 28/10//2026

For informal queries please contact: Dr Svetlana Mastitskaya (Senior Lecturer in Cardiovascular Regenerative Medicine) svetlana.mastitskaya@bristol.ac.uk

The role

We are seeking to appoint a fixed-term full-time Research Associate or Senior Research Associate with experience in organic geochemistry, stable isotope geochemistry, and/or culturing phytoplankton. The project will begin around November 2026 and will run for 17-19 months.

The postholder will be embedded in a research team led by Dr Caitlyn Witkowski within the Organic Geochemistry Unit, a world-leading research group in the field of organic geochemistry. Information on our policies and strategy is available on our websites, and we strongly encourage applications from all backgrounds.

Please include a full academic CV and a brief cover letter (1-page) that includes i) a statement on how this post will build on your previous experience and what you will bring to this project. For further information, see:

OGU: http://www.bristol.ac.uk/chemistry/research/ogu/

University of Bristol: https://www.bristol.ac.uk

What will you be doing?

The project aims are to understand how carbon is taken up during photosynthesis, specifically how photoautotrophic phytoplankton fractionate and biosynthesis carbon, with implications for understanding the evolution of phytoplankton and how CO2 has changed across geologic time.

You will be responsible for designing and conducting continuous culturing experiments using a chemostat bioreactor. Following the experiments, you will extract and analyse the phytoplankton lipids using analytical instrumentation (GC-FID, GC-MS, GC-C-IRMS, HPLC-MS). The aim is to identify the relationship between environmental conditions (e.g., CO2, light, pH) with the amount of stable carbon fractionation observed in the phytoplankton lipid suite. You will communicate the findings from this project to the relevant research communities through the use of scientific conference presentations and peer-reviewed publications.

You will have opportunities to explore a wide range of organic geochemistry and biosynthesis questions, present at international conferences, develop your own scientific and interdisciplinary ideas, and work with both local and international collaborators. You will be supported to take on leadership opportunities (e.g., student supervision) and have the freedom and resources to build your own career portfolio (e.g., via workshops, training, etc).

We are preferably looking for someone with:

A good honours degree (or equivalent) in PhD in Chemistry, Earth Sciences, Biology, Geography, or relevant subject
APhD in Chemistry, Organic Geochemistry, Earth Sciences, Geomicrobiology, Biology, or related disciplines
The ability to pro-actively and creatively implement wet chemistry and instrumental solutions to complex problems
Relevant experience of designing and implementing laboratory experiments, preferably analysing the lipid content in phytoplankton
Experience with environmental isotopes
Evidence of effective science communication through publications of scientific papers in peer-reviewed journals
Evidence of effective science communication through (inter)national conference presentations
Experience of liaison with (external) collaborators and organisations
Evidence for involvement in outreach activities
Appointment at the Senior Research Associate level will require previous experience in research and (under)graduate supervision at PDRA level or equivalent industry-level, as well as experience in leading independent project management

Research Associate/Senior Research Associate in Climate Science

The role

We are pleased to announce the exciting opportunity of an 18-month Postdoctoral Research Assistant position (Senior Research Associate) at the University of Bristol, UK, in collaboration with the University of Colorado at Boulder, USA, as part of the NSFGEO-NERC funded project "How well can we constrain past changes in ocean heat and freshwater content?".

The successful candidate will join a US-UK team funded by NSF and NERC, led by the University of Colorado at Boulder, USA (Dr Donata Giglio). The work at the University of Bristol is led by Prof Matt Palmer who also holds the position of Science Fellow at the Met Office Hadley Centre.

The research will focus on in situ observations of ocean temperature and the development of ensemble datasets that fully account the uncertainty associated with inter-platform biases. This work will build on research performed at the Met Office Hadley Centre and involve regular contact with scientists working in the Climate Monitoring & Attribution team.

The new ensemble datasets will be combined with novel mapping approaches developed by US colleagues at the University of Colorado to provide 3D time-evolving estimates of historical heat and freshwater content. The job holder will also work with scientists at the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis and the Met Office Hadley Centre to develop and analyse new surface temperature and sea-level rise projections as part of the project.

There will be opportunities to visit the US Team in Colorado and attend international conferences and/or working group meetings to present results as part of the project.

More details of the project are available from Matt Palmer on request (m.d.palmer@bristol.ac.uk).

What will you be doing?

The successful candidate will be responsible for developing a new ensemble ocean temperature profile dataset that fully characterises the uncertainty associated with historical inter-platform biases (i.e. differences in apparent ocean temperature that arise through sensor/device characteristics). They will work alongside the US-led team to develop these into ensemble estimates of ocean heat uptake. This improved knowledge of ocean heat uptake and its uncertainty will be used to develop a new set of surface temperature and sea-level rise projections in collaboration with scientists at the Met Office Hadley Centre (UK) and International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (Austria).

In addition to the functional aspects of the work, there will be opportunities for research collaboration across many aspects of the project, including mechanistic analysis of ocean heat and freshwater content change and the impact of the new observational constraints on projections of global climate change. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to visit the US-based team at the University of Colorado at Boulder.

You will have a PhD or equivalent professional experience in a relevant science discipline.

You should also have:

Proficiency in the Python programming language
Strong quantitative and data analysis skills
Ability to work both independently and collaboratively

 

And ideally:

Experience of modern software development practices, including version control and use of online repositories, such as GitHub
Experience in the analysis of geophysical datasets

What's the research culture like at the University of Cambridge?

At the University of Cambridge, we’re at the forefront of global research. Renowned for our pioneering contributions across disciplines, we aim to foster a vibrant research environment that blends tradition with innovation.  

Researchers here are empowered by a culture of intellectual freedom, interdisciplinary collaboration, and access to world-class facilities. Scholars here are free to pursue transformative ideas and tackle some of the most pressing challenges of our time. 

Our researchers are driving breakthroughs in cancer care, highlighting the university’s powerful blend of clinical expertise and cutting-edge science. They’re leading bold, interdisciplinary projects in the fields of technology and sustainability – from engineering programmable plants to advancing robotics through major national initiatives. It’s a place where world-changing ideas are not only imagined – they’re realised. 

At Cambridge, you can become part of a dynamic, supportive community that values curiosity, creativity, and collaboration. We’re right at the centre of UK innovation, connecting academia, industry, and policy. It’s an inspiring environment where researchers at every stage can thrive and make a lasting difference. 

As a researcher at Cambridge, you can: 

Participate in our new annual Academic Career Pathways (Research) promotions scheme, offering progression to more senior research roles. 
Apply for pay progression within your current band, through our termly Researcher Contribution Increment scheme.
Get support from the University’s Postdoc Academy, who enable our Postdocs to realise their potential through information, community, advocacy and professional development.

The Deane and Rayner laboratories at the Cambridge Institute for Medical Research are recruiting a Postdoctoral Research Associate to work as part of an ongoing team project that explores the function of a multi-gene family that is expanded in the genomes of Plasmodium vivax and other related neglected human malaria parasites.

The project builds on a recent publication that established that these tryptophan-rich antigens (TRAgs) have lipid binding activity (PMID: 37709739). This is a short-term position to produce high-quality purified TRAg proteins for structural and functional studies. It will be absolutely essential that the successful candidate has demonstrable experience in: protein expression using HEK293F-based mammalian expression systems; structure determination including X-ray crystallography of protein-ligand complexes; and biophysical characterisation of protein interactions such as using biolayer interferometry or isothermal titration calorimetry. Additional desirable skills include computational modelling of protein complexes and protein-ligand complexes as well as experience with molecular biology approaches for cloning and mutagenesis of new expression constructs. An understanding of how pathogens hijack host-cell pathways will also be advantageous. The successful applicant will also have demonstrated their capacity to produce high-quality data by having first author peer-reviewed publications.

The primary focus will be on carrying out outstanding academic research which will contribute directly to collaborative papers. The project provides substantial scope for innovation, creativity and exercising scientific judgement. You will work as part of a vibrant interdisciplinary team with colleagues in both the Rayner and Deane laboratories in the Cambridge Institute for Medical Research. You are expected to contribute to that positive team environment, supporting and training others where needed and working together to create the best possible outputs within the time available.

The Cambridge Institute for Medical Research (CIMR) is located on the Cambridge Biomedical Campus and it is a collaborative institute at the interface between fundamental research and the clinic, with a mission to determine the molecular mechanisms of disease in order to advance human health.

The University of Cambridge wishes to appoint a talented postdoctoral research associate to join the research group of Prof Rita Horvath at the Department of Clinical Neurosciences and the John Van Geest Brain Repair Centre.

The position is part of a research grant from the joint call of the Action Medical Research and Action for AT, to characterise novel biomarkers of ataxia telangiectasia that support monitoring neurological progression and measuring treatment effect. The focus of your work will be to study how neuron-specific biomarkers reflect the progression of ataxia and how these change on treatment with novel antisense oligonucleotides.

You will use cutting-edge technologies, including functional studies on neuronal stem cells and human neurons. Proteomics, RNA sequencing and other omics technologies will be performed to identify the molecular mechanism of neurodegeneration and ataxia in children and adults. You will have access to a team of experienced bioinformaticians, but have the opportunity to be trained and perform independent in-depth bioinformatic analysis of large datasets. You will have access to clinical samples from the MitoCamb neurogenetics clinic, to apply and translate novel technology and insights towards a human disease context.

The Research

Luke Harland is establishing a new research group based in the Loke Centre for Trophoblast Research within the Department of Physiology, Development and Neuroscience at the University of Cambridge. The group investigates how specialised blood and vascular cell types arise during mammalian development and uses this knowledge to generate defined cell populations from pluripotent stem cells for mechanistic studies and tissue modelling.

We aim to understand how developmental history shapes blood and vascular cell identity and function, and to apply this knowledge to build improved vascularised tissue models. By recreating the developmental processes that generate specialised blood vessels, we hope to build more physiologically relevant models for studying human development and disease. Our initial focus is on reconstructing the fetal placental exchange interface, which enables the transfer of oxygen and nutrients required for fetal growth and development.

Our research combines embryology, stem cell biology, single-cell genomics, genome engineering, advanced imaging and computational biology.

Further information about Luke Harland and key publications relevant to the ongoing research programme can be found on the Loke Centre for Trophoblast Research website (https://www.trophoblast.cam.ac.uk/people/luke-harland)

We are seeking an enthusiastic and motivated Research Assistant to join our growing Wellcome-funded research programme. This is an exciting opportunity to become one of the founding members of a new research group and contribute to its development and culture.

The successful candidate will contribute to research spanning developmental and stem cell biology, with opportunities to work with pluripotent stem cell culture and directed differentiation, molecular biology, flow cytometry, microscopy, mouse developmental models and single-cell genomics.

About You

Applicants should hold a BSc or Master's degree in a relevant biological discipline and have practical laboratory experience in cell biology, developmental biology, stem cell biology, molecular biology or a related field.

We are particularly interested in candidates with experience in the culture and directed differentiation of mouse and/or human pluripotent stem cells. Experience with R or Python is desirable, and previous analysis of single-cell RNA-sequencing data would be an advantage. Experience with flow cytometry, microscopy or mouse developmental biology would also be beneficial. Training will be provided, and experience across all of these areas is not expected.

We are looking for an organised, enthusiastic and collaborative individual with excellent attention to detail and an interest in combining experimental and computational biology.

Research Associate, CASCADE
 
Cardiff University School of Social and Spatial Sciences is seeking to recruit a Research Associate to work within the Children's Social Care Research and Development Centre (CASCADE), Research Centre that is located within the School.
 
CASCADE is recruiting up to four fixed term positions, each available at 0.5 FTE, within the following sub areas of Children’s Social Care Research
Reducing Inequalities - We examine how structural, organisational and practice factors shape unequal experiences for children and families. Our aim is to understand, reduce and ultimately eliminate inequalities, and to ensure our research includes and amplifies underserved voices
Supporting Relationships - This area focuses on the importance of loving, stable and lasting relationships for children and families. We examine how relationships are formed, maintained and protected throughout involvement with social care.
Supporting Excellent Practice - This area focuses on the skills, judgements and approaches that enable practitioners to work effectively. It covers direct work, assessment, decision-making and emerging tools such as AI designed to support practice
Effective Organisation & Systems - We explore how leadership, culture, systems and resources shape the conditions for good practice. Strong organisations enable confident decision-making, learning and sustained improvement.
Further information about each area can be found in the attached Job Description.
 
This post is part-time (17.5 hours per week), fixed term for a period of 12 months, from 1st December 2026 or 1st January 2027
 
Salary: £41,064 - £46,049 per annum, pro rata for part time hours (Grade 5), with annual increments up to final salary at top of grade). New appointments are usually made at the starting point of the salary scale.
 
Responsible to Professor Donald Forrester, CASCADE Research Centre Director/Priority Theme Lead
 
For an informal discussion about the role please contact Donald, ForresterD@cardiff.ac.uk/Priority Theme Lead
From the 1st August 2026 the School of Social Sciences and the School of Geography and Planning will come together to create the new School of Social and Spatial Sciences, building on and strengthening existing interdisciplinary research and education
 
Cardiff University offers many excellent benefits, including 45 days annual leave, pro rata for part time workers (including bank holidays) blended working (meaning you will be able to work from home for some of your time), a cycle to work scheme and other travel initiatives, annual increments up the pay scale, and more. It is an exciting and vibrant place to work, with many different challenges and is a proud Living Wage supporter.
 
As the biggest university in Wales – and a major employer, with more than 7,000 staff – we are an ambitious and innovative university located in a beautiful and thriving capital city. postings.listing_context: Marie Sklodowska-Curie Early Stage Researcher (ESR) in in Network Ecology and Response Diversity
postings.advert_text:
Home  Vacancies  Marie Sklodowska-Curie Early Stage Researcher (ESR) in in Network Ecology and Response Diversity
Marie Sklodowska-Curie Early Stage Researcher (ESR) in in Network Ecology and Response Diversity
Posted on 13/10/2026
Save Job
Apply
Job Advert

Marie Sklodowska-Curie Early Stage Researcher (ESR) in in Network Ecology and Response Diversity

School of Biosciences

Response diversity describes the variation in how individuals, species, or functional groups respond to environmental change and the concept is increasingly recognised as a key driver of ecosystem resilience. Understanding and promoting response diversity is therefore essential for conserving biodiversity and supporting resilient ecosystems in a changing world.

Cardiff University invites applications for a Doctoral Candidate position within the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network ReDiLEEP. ReDiLEEP brings together leading universities, research institutes, and non-academic partners across Europe and beyond to advance response diversity research and translate new knowledge into ecosystem management, restoration, and biodiversity policy.

The Doctoral Candidate will contribute to this effort by investigating response diversity across ecosystems, focusing on the development of monitoring methods to investigate response diversity in the real-world.

Cardiff University is looking for an Early Stage Researcher within the Division of Organisms and Environment for the collaborative research projects ‘Do biotic interactions homogenise responses and reduce response diversity?’ of the EU Horizon2020 Marie Sklodowska-Curie Action: “ReDiLEEP” Using science-driven response diversity knowledge to leverage efficient ecosystem preservation and restoration. ReDiLEEP brings together leading universities, research institutes, and non-academic partners across Europe and beyond to advance response-diversity research and translate new knowledge into ecosystem management, restoration, and biodiversity policy.

As part of the position, the successful candidate will be enrolled as a staff candidate for a PhD at Cardiff University. ESR PhD students will benefit from a dedicated training program in the various fields of expertise of the consortium partners.

Conditions of international mobility of researchers: Researchers will undertake trans-national secondments (i.e. move from one country to another). At the time of selection by the host organisation, researchers must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the UK for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to their recruitment. Short stays, such as holidays, are not taken into account.  The candidates must not yet have been awarded a doctorate degree and should have <4 years past M.Sc. or equivalent.

English language: It is a requirement that applicants will show that their ability to understand and express themselves in both written and spoken English is sufficient for them to derive the full benefit from the network training, and to embark on a doctorate at a UK University.

This is a full-time position (35 hours per week), fixed-term for 3 years and is available from 1st April 2027.

For informal enquiries please contact Dr Fredric Windsor WindsorFM@cardiff.ac.uk 

It is anticipated the basic annual salary will be in the region of £34,610 to £38,784 per annum, exact salary will be confirmed upon appointment.  In addition to basic salary, Marie Sklodowska-Curie Early Stage Researcher positions also attract living and mobility allowances, dependent on individual circumstances.

Date advert posted: Tuesday, 13 October 2026

Closing date: Tuesday, 10 November 2026

Please be aware that interviews will be held week commencing 16th November 2026 via Microsoft Teams.

ESR eligibility criteria

Applicants should not have resided or performed their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the UK for more than 12 months in the 3-year period immediately prior to the start date of the PhD research.

Applicants for the ESR PhD positions should be in the first 4 years (full-time equivalent) of their research careers and not yet have been awarded a doctorate. This 4-year period is measured from the date of obtaining the degree which would formally entitle to embark on a doctorate.

Save Job

Job Advert
 Research Associate 
 UK Dementia Research Institute Cardiff
 School of Medicine
 College of Biomedical and Life Sciences

Applications are invited for Research and Innovation Associate position in Neuroinflammation/ Complement Biology in the UK DRI at Cardiff University School of Medicine, based at the Heath Campus.

This post will join a new programme of research supported by a UKRI Future Leaders  Fellowship programme awarded to Dr. Wioleta Zelek that explores the role of neuroinflammation in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and other dementias. The work focuses on defining the role of the complement system in Alzheimer's disease using integrated multi-omics approaches, including transcriptomics, proteomics and spatial profiling, followed by functional validation in human iPSC-derived in vitro cell-based models. The successful candidate will investigate complement-mediated neuroimmune mechanisms underpinning disease progression and identify novel therapeutic targets through computational and experimental approaches.

Candidates with expertise in complement biology, immunology and Alzheimer's disease or  relevant industrial experience are encouraged to apply. Experience in one or more of the following is highly desirable: analysis and integration of transcriptomic, proteomic or spatial omics datasets; bioinformatics; human iPSC-derived neuronal and glial models; molecular and cellular biology; and mechanistic validation of disease pathways.

The post will involve generation and analysis of multi-omics brain atlases, integration of large-scale datasets, and validation of key findings using human iPSC-derived microglia, astrocytes and neuronal models.

Informal enquiries should be made to Dr Wiola Zelek (zelekw@cardiff.ac.uk).

Division: http://medicine.cf.ac.uk/infect-immun/
UK DRI Cardiff:  https://ukdri.ac.uk/centres/cardiff

This post is full time (35 hours per week), available from 1st November 2026 and fixed term for 1 year.

Salary: £41,064 - £46,049 per annum (Grade 6). Appointments to roles at Cardiff University are usually made at bottom of scale unless in exceptional circumstances.

Cardiff University offers many excellent benefits, including 45 days annual leave, (including bank holidays), local pension scheme, a cycle to work scheme and other travel initiatives, annual increments within the pay scale, and more. It is an exciting and vibrant place to work, with many different challenges and is a proud Living Wage supporter.

Date advert posted: Tuesday, 13 October 2026

Closing date: Wednesday, 28 October 2026

Cardiff University is committed to supporting and promoting equality and diversity and to creating an inclusive working environment. We believe this can be achieved through attracting, developing, and retaining a diverse range of staff from many different backgrounds.  We therefore welcome applicants from all sections of the community regardless of sex, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, trans identity, relationship status, religion or belief, caring responsibilities, or age.  We especially welcome and encourage applications from those under-represented groups within the University workforce, such as those who identify as LGBT+, Ethnic Minority or those with disabilities. In supporting our employees to achieve a balance between their work and their personal lives, we will also consider proposals for flexible working or job share arrangements.

 Cardiff University is a signatory to the San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA), which means that in hiring and promotion decisions we will evaluate applicants on the quality of their research, not publication metrics or the identity of the journal in which the research is published. More information is available at: Responsible research assessment - Research - Cardiff University
 
Applications may be submitted in Welsh, and an application submitted in Welsh will not be treated less favourably than an application submitted in English.

Posted on 09/10/2026

Job Advert

Marie Sklodowska-Curie Early Stage Researcher (ESR) in Network Ecology and Response Diversity

School of Biosciences

Response diversity describes the variation in how individuals, species, or functional groups respond to environmental change and the concept is increasingly recognised as a key driver of ecosystem resilience. Understanding and promoting response diversity is therefore essential for conserving biodiversity and supporting resilient ecosystems in a changing world.

Cardiff University invites applications for a Doctoral Candidate position within the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network ReDiLEEP. ReDiLEEP brings together leading universities, research institutes, and non-academic partners across Europe and beyond to advance response diversity research and translate new knowledge into ecosystem management, restoration, and biodiversity policy.

The Doctoral Candidate will contribute to this effort by investigating response diversity across ecosystems, focusing on the development of monitoring methods to investigate response diversity in the real-world.

Cardiff University is looking for an Early Stage Researcher within the Division of Organisms and Environment for the collaborative research projects ‘How can we measure response diversity at scale and across different taxa?’ of the EU Horizon2020 Marie Sklodowska-Curie Action: “ReDiLEEP” Using science-driven response diversity knowledge to leverage efficient ecosystem preservation and restoration. ReDiLEEP brings together leading universities, research institutes, and non-academic partners across Europe and beyond to advance response-diversity research and translate new knowledge into ecosystem management, restoration, and biodiversity policy.

As part of the position, the successful candidate will be enrolled as a staff candidate for a PhD at Cardiff University. ESR PhD students will benefit from a dedicated training program in the various fields of expertise of the consortium partners.

Conditions of international mobility of researchers: Researchers will undertake trans-national secondments (i.e. move from one country to another). At the time of selection by the host organisation, researchers must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the UK for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to their recruitment. Short stays, such as holidays, are not taken into account.  The candidates must not yet have been awarded a doctorate degree and should have <4 years past M.Sc. or equivalent.

English language: It is a requirement that applicants will show that their ability to understand and express themselves in both written and spoken English is sufficient for them to derive the full benefit from the network training, and to embark on a doctorate at a UK University.

This is a full-time position (35 hours per week), fixed-term for 3 years and is available from 1st April 2027.

For informal enquiries please contact Dr Fredric Windsor WindsorFM@cardiff.ac.uk 

It is anticipated the basic annual salary will be in the region of £34,610 to £38,784 per annum, exact salary will be confirmed upon appointment.  In addition to basic salary, Marie Sklodowska-Curie Early Stage Researcher positions also attract living and mobility allowances, dependent on individual circumstances.

Date advert posted: Friday, 9 October 2026

Closing date: Friday 6 November 2026

Please be aware that interviews will be held week commencing 16th November 2026 via Microsoft Teams.

ESR eligibility criteria

Applicants should not have resided or performed their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the UK for more than 12 months in the 3-year period immediately prior to the start date of the PhD research.

Applicants for the ESR PhD positions should be in the first 4 years (full-time equivalent) of their research careers and not yet have been awarded a doctorate. This 4-year period is measured from the date of obtaining the degree which would formally entitle to embark on a doctorate.

Applicants must confirm and be prepared to provide evidence that they meet the Marie Sklodowska-Curie eligibility criteria as specified below.

Conditions of international mobility of researchers: Researchers are required to undertake trans-national mobility (i.e. move from one country to another) when taking up the appointment. At the time of selection by the host organisation, researchers must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the UK for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to their recruitment. Short stays, such as holidays, are not taken into account.

*The Marie Sklodowska-Curie programme offers highly competitive and attractive salary and working conditions. The successful candidates will receive a salary in accordance with the Marie Sklodowska-Curie regulations for early stage and experienced researchers.

Exact salary will be confirmed upon appointment. In addition to their individual scientific projects, all fellows will benefit from further continuing education, which includes internships and secondments, a variety of training modules as well as transferable skills courses and active participation in workshops and conferences.

About The Role
Graduate Research Assistant: Black in the UK Science Pipeline Project

This part-time (0.9 FTE) post is available from 1 November 2026.

This post is offered as a fixed term contract and is funded by UKRI NERC until 30 November 2028.

In line with the University’s fair employment for all principles,, any further funding opportunities identified will be reviewed and discussed during the contract.

Salary will be £34,630 on Grade E subject to knowledge, skills and experience.

We welcome applications from candidates interested in job-sharing arrangements.

Please note that this role is subject to a DBS check. At the University of Exeter, we are committed to the safeguarding and welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults.  We expect all our staff to share this commitment.

The Role

Faculty of Health and Life Sciences

The Faculty wishes to recruit a Research and Evaluation Assistant for a national project working towards equity in access and opportunity within the UK natural environment science education and workforce pipeline. The project focuses on pipeline inequity for individuals from Black heritage backgrounds and relies on the collection and analysis of data from a diversity of participants, settings and methods. 

The position, which can be filled as a job-share, will run for the duration of the project to assist with a diversity of aspects of data collection and analysis and project evaluation. This includes, but is not limited to, carrying out literature searches for a quantitative survey, collating and preparing evaluation materials, organising files and updating databases, coordinating transcription and coding of data, contributing to transcription and coding of data and archiving of qualitative materials for content analysis, managing the evaluation calendar and assisting with dissemination of a national survey and analysis of results. Training will be provided and tasks adapted as appropriate to skills and interests of the appointed individual. 

The Project
 
Context and Overview
Belonging is a core human need and fundamental determinant of educational experience, career trajectory and social integration for marginalised groups. In England, Black representation in NERC-facing subjects declines sharply from GCSE to A-level and undergraduate stages,reaching close to 0% in some NERC disciplines. This pattern continues into employment: in 2022 only ~4.8% of those in NERC-related employment roles identified as Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic, compared with 12.6% across other sectors. Against entrenched anti-Black praxes in UK education manifested as tracking bias, inflated exclusion rates and persistent inequities in degree awards, lack of representation fundamentally erodes belonging. Interventions explicitly cultivating belonging are both urgent and effective for improving retention and progression and, when cultivated at scale, for reshaping norms, networks, institutional cultures and policy trajectories.
 
Meeting the Challenge: Approach and Aims
Our theory of change centres connecting representation across the education and employment pipeline through coordinated interventions that operate at individual, institutional and policy levels. We will create spaces that normalise Black presence, leadership and expertise in environment sciences and use participatory and Afronographic (learning as people of African descent) methods to cultivate agency and translate lived experience into systems change. This “pipeline of belonging” will be leveraged to meet our aims of transforming individual trajectories and driving institutional and policy reform. 
 

About You

Applicants will be educated to bachelor's degree level or possess an equivalent qualification/experience in a related field of study or equivalent experience and be able to demonstrate some knowledge in the discipline and of research methods and techniques to be able to begin work within established research programmes. Applicants will be able to demonstrate depth of understanding of day-to-day lived experiences of Black heritage individuals living in the UK and elsewhere in the Diaspora and meet the remaining essential person specifications for the role.

Please ensure you read the Job Description and Person Specification for full details of this role. 
 
We would particularly encourage anyone interested in pursuing a postgraduate research degree in psychology or other closely aligned discipline to apply for this position.

About The Role
Postdoctoral Research Associate/Postdoctoral Research Fellow
 

Internal only

This full-time post is immediately available. 

This post is offered as a fixed term contract and is funded by NIHR until 30 September 2027.  

In line with the University’s fair employment for all principles, any further funding opportunities identified will be reviewed and discussed during the contract.

The starting salary will be from £35,302 on Grade E for the PDRA level and from £43,482 on Grade F for the PDRF level, depending on knowledge, skills and experience.
  
 Please note that this role is subject to a DBS check. At the University of Exeter, we are committed to the safeguarding and welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults.  We expect all our staff to share this commitment. 
 
The Role
 
Faculty of Health and Life Sciences

This post will support the final year of the NIHR-funded ATTEND Programme Grant, with a particular focus on leading the analysis, interpretation and publication of findings from the implementation work package. The role will be central to ensuring that the programme delivers high-quality, impactful outputs that inform the future implementation and scale-up of the intervention. Given the advanced stage of the programme and the emphasis on timely dissemination, applicants must demonstrate a strong track record of producing high-quality, peer-reviewed publications. The postholder may also be required to contribute to activities across the programme’s other four work packages.

About ATTEND

ATTEND is a four-year NIHR Programme Grant led by Professor Tamsin Ford and Dr Patrick Smith. The programme is evaluating whether a novel intervention, Mindfulness for Adolescents and Carers (MAC), can improve recovery outcomes for young people aged 15–18 years with depression who have not fully responded to first-line treatment or who have experienced relapse.

While Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT) is recommended by NICE for preventing depressive relapse in adults, there is currently insufficient evidence regarding its effectiveness in adolescents. ATTEND has adapted MBCT specifically for young people with depression and is evaluating the clinical effectiveness, cost-effectiveness and implementation potential of MAC using a hybrid effectiveness-implementation trial design.

The programme comprises five interconnected work packages:

WP1: Development and delivery of a training package for CAMHS professionals.

WP2: Design and evaluation of a digital app to support and measure mindfulness practice.

WP3: Delivery of a multi-site randomised controlled trial.

WP4: Examination of theoretically derived moderators and mediators of treatment outcomes.

WP5: Development of an implementation strategy to support future adoption and delivery.

The successful candidate will play a key role within WP5, applying implementation science theories, models and frameworks to analyse study findings and develop evidence-based recommendations for the future rollout and sustainability of MAC should it prove effective.

The postholder will join the Children and Young People's Mental Health (ChYMe) Research Collaboration, a large multidisciplinary team committed to improving the mental health and wellbeing of children and young people through world-leading research. Further information about ChYMe can be found at: http://medicine.exeter.ac.uk/research/healthresearch/childhealth/chyme/.

About You

PDRA:
The successful applicant will be able to present information on research progress and outcomes, communicate complex information, orally, in writing and electronically and prepare proposals and applications to external bodies.
 
Applicants will possess a relevant PhD (or nearing completion) or possess an equivalent qualification/experience in a related field of study and be able to demonstrate sufficient knowledge in the discipline and of research methods and techniques to work within established research programmes. 

PDRF:
The successful applicant will be able to develop research objectives, projects and proposals; identify sources of research funding and contribute to the process of securing funds and make presentations at conferences and other events.
 
Applicants will possess a relevant PhD or possess an equivalent qualification/experience in a related field of study. The successful applicant will be a nationally recognised authority in the subject area and possess sufficient specialist knowledge in the discipline to develop research programmes and methodologies. The successful applicant will also be able to work collaboratively, supervise the work of others and act as team leader as required.
 
Please ensure you read the Job Description and Person Specification for full details of this role.

About The Role

Postdoctoral Research Associate / Fellow
 
This NERC-funded full-time post is available from 03/05/2027 until 02/05/2029 at the University of Exeter's Penryn Campus in Cornwall.
 
The starting salary will be from £35,302 to £40,704 on Grade E for the Postdoctoral Research Associate level and £44,352 on Grade F for the Postdoctoral Research Fellow level, depending on knowledge, skills and experience. 

The Role 

Faculty of Environment, Science and Economy

The Faculty wishes to recruit a Postdoctoral Research Associate or Fellow to join the Centre for Ecology and Conservation at the Penryn Campus, Cornwall.

The successful applicant will work with Dr Bram Kuijper, Professor Alex Thornton and collaborators on the theoretical components of their NERC Pushing the Frontiers grant: “The co-evolution of learning and social structure: how minds shape societies and societies shape minds” (UKRI4324).

It has long been suggested that the demands of social life drive cognitive evolution. However, if cognition allows individuals to learn who best to associate with, individuals’ mental processes may shape societies in return. To understand such dynamics and generate testable predictions, this post will develop evolutionary models (primarily individual-based evolutionary simulations) to establish a predictive framework linking the evolution of learning in social decision-making to social evolution. It will include the development of simulation code using a programming language such as C++, R or Python, interpretation of model outputs, publication and presentation of findings. The work will be conducted in close collaboration with empirical researchers working on wild jackdaws as part of the grant, and the successful candidate will be a member of Thornton’s Wild Cognition Research Group.

About You

Postdoctoral Research Associate: The successful applicant will have proven skills in evolutionary modelling and be able to present information on research progress and outcomes, communicate complex information, orally, in writing and electronically and prepare proposals and applications to external bodies.

Applicants will possess a relevant PhD (or nearing completion) or an equivalent qualification/experience in behavioural ecology, evolutionary biology, theoretical biology or a related field of study. They will be able to demonstrate sufficient knowledge in the discipline and of research methods and techniques to work within established research programmes and possess relevant skills in computational evolutionary biology including individual-based simulations. Applicants should demonstrate experience of conducting and completing research from idea conception to publication and presentations, with experience in coding and data analysis. They should demonstrate excellent communication, teamwork and collaboration skills, and be enthusiastic about interdisciplinary research. Desirable skills include: the ability to develop simulation code using a programming language such as C++, R or Python, knowledge of social network analysis and game theory and experience of collaborations spanning theoretical and empirical research.

Postdoctoral Research Fellow: The successful applicant will be able to develop research objectives, projects and proposals; identify sources of research funding and contribute to the process of securing funds and make presentations at conferences and other events.

Applicants will possess a relevant PhD in behavioural ecology, evolutionary biology, theoretical biology or a related field of study. The successful applicant will have a strong track record of high quality publications, including evidence of published research in theoretical evolutionary biology. They must possess sufficient specialist knowledge in the discipline to develop research programmes and methodologies, with skills in evolutionary modelling including individual-based simulations and the ability to develop simulation code using a programming language such as C++, R or Python.

Applicants will be able to demonstrate interest and expertise in theoretical modelling in the fields of social evolution/cognitive evolution and experience of collaborations or discussions integrating theoretical and empirical research. They should demonstrate experience of conducting and completing research from idea conception to publication and presentations, with expertise in coding and data analysis. In addition to their track record of publications, they must demonstrate excellent communication, teamwork and collaboration skills, and be enthusiastic about interdisciplinary research. Desirable skills include: the ability to work with version control tools like git, experience with unix-based operating systems, experience of engaging with concepts from animal cognition (e.g. learning/decision-making), managing research teams and supervising students and/or junior colleagues.

Please ensure you read the Job Description and Person Specification for full details of this role.  

Further information

Please contact Dr Bram Kuijper, a.l.w.kuijper@exeter.ac.uk or Prof Alex Thornton, alex.thornton@exeter.ac.uk

About The Role
Postdoctoral Research Fellow in Nanofabrication 
 
Faculty of Environment, Science and Economy

This full-time QuIMS (Quantum Information with Mechanical Systems) funded post is available for a fixed term of two years from December 2026. The role is based at the University of Exeter.

The starting salary will be from £44,352 up to £46,970 per annum on Grade F, depending on knowledge, skills and experience. 

The Role
The Faculty wishes to recruit a Postdoctoral Research Fellow for QuIMS (Quantum Information with Mechanical Systems), a collaborative project exploring mechanical systems for quantum technologies. Working with Prof. Saverio Russo, you will fabricate nanoscale devices using the University’s cleanroom and characterisation facilities.

The post focuses on device design, electron-beam lithography, deposition, etching, material transfer and suspended structures. You will optimise process flows, characterise devices and improve fabrication yield and reproducibility, keeping clear process records and collaborating with experimental and theoretical colleagues.

About You
You will possess a relevant PhD or equivalent qualification/experience in physics, materials science or engineering, with hands-on cleanroom nanofabrication experience. You will be able to develop fabrication methods, assess device quality and analyse results, with a record of high-quality research publications.

Experience in fabrication of suspended graphene or van der Waals heterostructures is preferred.

You will plan and deliver research, communicate clearly, collaborate and support less experienced researchers. You will contribute to publications, presentations and proposals, and demonstrate a commitment to safe laboratory practice and an inclusive working environment.

Please ensure you read the Job Description and Person Specification for full details of this role.

Further information
For informal enquiries, please contact Prof. Saverio Russo at s.russo@exeter.ac.uk or Dr. Luca Dellantonio at l.dellantonio@exeter.ac.uk
