The starting salary will be from £44,352 on Grade F, dependent on knowledge, skills and experience.

We welcome applications from candidates interested in working part-time hours or job-sharing arrangements. Hybrid working is an option for this role.

   
The Role

We are looking to recruit a Postdoctoral Research Fellow to join the Centre for Net Positive Health and Climate Solutions (Net+ Centre). The Net+ Centre launched on the 1st of October 2024. This is a five-year research centre funded by UKRI, led by the University of Exeter alongside core partners at the UK Health Security Agency, The National Trust, and Forest Research (with many other partners across sectors and the UK). 

The key aim of the Net+ Centre is to establish interdisciplinary research infrastructure, partnerships, and capacity to proactively deliver novel, impactful research on climate change and health, with a focus on environmental-social-health inequalities. Key topics include resilient green and blue infrastructure, resilient urban environments, and resilient food systems.

The Postdoctoral Research Fellow will be based at the Faculty of Environment, Science, and Economy on the Exeter campus of the University of Exeter. They will be working closely with Net+ colleagues in the University of Exeter Medical School in the Faculty of Health & Life Sciences at both the Penryn and St Luke’s campuses, as well as have opportunities to collaborate with the wider Net+ network across the Faculty of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences.

We are looking for a mixed-methods researcher with experience working on resilient food systems/sustainable nutrition research questions, with strong evidence synthesis skills, and an ability for public and stakeholder engagement to co-produce positive impacts from research. The role will involve key tasks as part of the centre, as well as an opportunity to develop your own research interests and take part in research across the Net+ centre. The successful applicant will help to plan and deliver high-quality research, particularly feeding into the Centre’s objective of investigating how future food systems can be climate-resilient and healthy for all.

Key tasks include a review of evidence on the impact of climate change on nutrition in the UK, which may involve both peer-reviewed academic literature, as well as a media analysis, and/or key informant interviews. In addition, your role will involve contributing to capacity building, engagement, and outreach activities in the centre, such as co-organising and facilitating activities at the Centre’s Leadership Academy residential meetings, PhD summer schools, and working with STEM Learning to support STEM Ambassadors or curriculum development. 

About You

The successful applicant will be able to develop research objectives, projects, and proposals; identify sources of research funding to contribute to the process of securing funds; and produce a range of academic and policy-relevant outputs, including presentations for conferences and other events. Applicants will possess a relevant PhD or an equivalent qualification/experience in food systems or sustainable nutrition research, and have sufficient specialist knowledge in the discipline to develop/follow the research programmes and methodologies of the Net+ Centre. The successful applicant will also be able to work collaboratively, across disciplines and supervise the work of others where necessary. They will have the capacity to support engagement, involvement, and dissemination events and be motivated to communicate with non-academic audiences.

About The Role

Postdoctoral Research Associate / Postdoctoral Research Fellow (Science and Technology Studies) 

Salary Details  

The starting salary will be from £34,610 up to £39,906 for PDRA and from £43,482 for PDRF, depending on knowledge, skills and experience.
 
 This full time, ERC funded post is available January 2027 to 31 December 2031. The successful applicant will conduct outstanding, international quality research on the ethics of AI and military decision-making. They will produce outstanding publications in the course of the research with a view to consolidating their academic career and establishing themselves as an expert in the field.

The post

The Faculty is seeking either a Postdoctoral Research Associate or Fellow with expertise in Science and Technology Studies (STS), sociology of science, or a closely related field to work with Professor Anthony King (Principal Investigator) on his ERC Advanced Grant project GENERAL-AI: Artificial Intelligence and Military Decision-Making. 

Applicants must have lived continuously in the UK for at least 5 years and be a national of a NATO member state in order to be eligible to obtain and maintain the required security clearance level for the role. Applications from candidates that do not meet the criteria will not be considered.

Appointment will be conditional upon the successful completion of security vetting.

The Project: GENERAL-AI: Artificial Intelligence and Military Decision-Making 

GENERAL-AI is a five-year European Research Council Advanced Grant investigating how artificial intelligence is transforming military decision-making. The project challenges speculative accounts of AI taking over military command by examining what AI can actually do, how military commanders and their staffs use AI in practice, and the ethical implications of its use in war.

 Focusing on AI-enabled high-intensity land warfare, the project combines the sociology of science and technology, ethnographic research, and philosophy and ethics. It investigates the development of military AI by leading technology companies, its use within NATO and European military headquarters, and the legal and ethical frameworks governing its application.

 The project will provide a detailed empirical account of the relationship between AI and human decision-making, while developing new theoretical perspectives on how AI is changing cognition, organisations and military command. Its findings will contribute both to academic debates about AI and to contemporary European security and defence policy.

 GENERAL AI consists of three work packages: Work Package 1 examines the technology itself exploring the development and character of AI Decision Support Systems through engagement with the relevant tech companies. Work Package 2 explores the process of decision-making inside military headquarters. Work Package 3 will examine the ethics of military decision making with AI. This post refers to Work Package 1.

The Role:

The successful candidate will undertake research for Work Package 1 (WP1), AI Technology, investigating the development, adaptation and application of artificial intelligence for military purposes.

GENERAL-AI is deliberately empirical. Rather than projecting hypothetical future developments of AI, the project examines the capabilities and limitations of contemporary AI and how it is being developed and adapted for military use. WP1 will therefore investigate how AI technologies are produced, how they acquire particular military functions, and how human expertise and organisational practices shape their development.

Key responsibilities

The successful candidate will:

conduct a programme of documentary and qualitative research into the development of contemporary AI and its military applications;
survey relevant academic and technical literature in order to establish the current capabilities, limitations and development of AI;
develop sufficient understanding of the data, computational processes and mathematical principles underpinning contemporary AI models to engage critically with their technical capabilities;
conduct qualitative interviews with executives, data scientists, programmers, engineers and other specialists working in leading defence and AI technology companies in the UK, Europe and the United States;
investigate how technology companies develop and adapt AI software for military applications;
examine the organisational cultures and working practices through which AI systems are developed, following the project's STS approach to the social production of technology;
investigate the role of human expertise, judgement and technical labour in the development, maintenance and adaptation of military AI;
examine how AI systems, data and algorithms are adapted to particular military requirements and operational contexts;
analyse the regulatory, organisational and practical challenges involved in collaboration between technology companies and the armed forces;
contribute to the project's broader investigation of the human decision team, examining how apparently autonomous AI capabilities remain embedded within networks of human technical and organisational activity;
analyse and publish research findings in high-quality academic publications;
contribute to presentations at international conferences and workshops;
work collaboratively with the Principal Investigator and the other researchers on GENERAL-AI, while developing an independent programme of research within the project.

The research will include engagement with leading defence and AI technology companies identified in the project, including Palantir, Anduril, Rebellion Defence, Hawkeye 360, Helsing, Mistral AI, Adarga AI and C3.AI. The precise research sample will depend on access and the development of the project.

A central question for WP1 is how AI becomes a military capability. The research will investigate how software, data and algorithms are produced collectively by teams of scientists, programmers and engineers, and how these systems are subsequently adapted to military requirements.

Research environment

The successful candidate will be based at the University of Exeter’s Strategy and Security Institute and will be integrated into the Defence Data Research Centre, providing access to an interdisciplinary research environment. The project also has an international academic and practitioner network spanning the UK, Europe and the United States. The postdoctoral researcher will also work closely with the wider GENERAL-AI team under the leadership of Professor Anthony King (PI).

About you

The successful applicant will be able to present information on research progress and outcomes, communicate complex information, orally, in writing and electronically and prepare proposals and applications to external bodies.

For PDRA applicants, you will possess a relevant PhD (or nearing completion). For PDRF applicants, you will possess a relevant PhD. Applicants will be able to plan, execute and conduct international level research and publish findings in peer reviewed journals and books.

Please ensure you read the Job Description and Person Specification for full details of this role.

Further information

For further information please contact Professor Anthony King , e-mail a.c.king@exeter.ac.uk or telephone (01392) 723259.

Interviews are expected to take place end of November/Early December

About The Role
Faculty of Environment, Science and Economy 
 
Postdoctoral Research Associate / Fellow
 
 This CLIMPEAT ERC Synergy funded full-time post is available from 1 January 2027 until 31 December 2029.
 
 The starting salary will be from £35,302 for Postdoctoral Research Associate and from £44,352 for Postdoctoral Research Fellow, depending on knowledge, skills and experience.
 
The Role 

The Faculty wishes to recruit either a Postdoctoral Research Associate or Fellow to participate in the CLIMPEAT ERC Synergy project. The successful applicant will be part of the CLIMPEAT team (University of Exeter, University of Stockholm, University of Innsbruck and LSCE) which aim to understand and quantify the abrupt and gradual responses of Northern peatlands and permafrost to climate change and their feedback on future warming. 

The post will include contribution to the development of the PEAT model, in close collaboration with the LSCE team in France; design and evaluate model's simulations of the evolution of the northern peatland biome from the last glacial  maximum (22kyr BP) to pre-industrial times; along with other approaches, the role of peatlands in the historical and present-day greenhouse gases budget, quantify the vulnerability of peatland and permafrost to climate change and feedback to the climate system.

About You

Postdoctoral Research Associate: The successful applicant will be able to present information on research progress and outcomes, communicate complex information, orally, in writing and electronically and prepare proposals and applications to external bodies. Applicants will possess a relevant PhD (or nearing completion) or possess an equivalent qualification/experience in a related field of study and be able to demonstrate sufficient knowledge in the discipline and of research methods and techniques to work within established research programmes.

Postdoctoral Research Fellow: The successful applicant will be able to develop research objectives, projects and proposals; identify sources of research funding and contribute to the process of securing funds and make presentations at conferences and other events. Applicants will possess a relevant PhD or possess an equivalent qualification/experience in a related field of study. The successful applicant will be a nationally recognised authority in insert subject area and possess sufficient specialist knowledge in the discipline to develop research programmes and methodologies. The successful applicant will also be able to work collaboratively, supervise the work of others and act as team leader as required.

For both Associate/Fellow roles, the applicants should be able to run global vegetation or climate models over long temporal integration, to analyse large climatic and environmental datasets, to synthesise results, lead publications/presentations of results, and work in close collaboration with the LSCE partner (Saclay, France).   

Please ensure you read the Job Description and Person Specification for full details of this role.  

Further information
Please contact insert Prof. Pierre Friedlingstein, p.friedlingstein@exeter.ac.uk.

About The Role
Postdoctoral Research Fellow

This UKRI funded part-time (0.6FTE) post is available from 1 December 2026 until 31 May 2027.
 
Salary will be from £44,352 per annum, pro rata on Grade F subject to knowledge, skills and experience. 
  
We welcome applications from candidates interested in working part-time hours or job-sharing arrangements.    
 
The Role
 
Faculty of Environment, Science and Economy

The Faculty wishes to recruit a part-time Postdoctoral Research Fellow to participate in research on social behaviour in animal societies. This UKRI funded 0.6 FTE post is available from 1 December 2026 for a period of 6 months. The successful applicant will work with a team led by Prof Michael Cant to investigate the causes of individual variation in social behaviour in wild banded mongooses, using genetic, life history and animal movement data from our long-term field study.

In addition to conducting original research, the successful applicant will help to oversee the transition of the project database to a new platform, and assist with the development of a behavioural data collection application. 

About You
The successful applicant will be able to develop research objectives, projects and proposals; identify sources of research funding and contribute to the process of securing funds and make presentations at conferences and other events.

Applicants will possess a relevant PhD or equivalent qualification/experience in a related field of study. The successful applicant will be a nationally recognised authority in behavioural ecology, animal behaviour, or evolutionary biology and possess sufficient specialist knowledge in the discipline to develop research programmes and methodologies. The successful applicant will also be able to work collaboratively, supervise the work of others and act as team leader as required.

Applicants will have good statistical and IT skills and familiarity or experience with field data collection, experimental design, database management and animal behaviour research. Experience studying among-individual behavioural variation in terrestrial species, including from observational and tracking data, is desirable. Any experience handling pedigree or social network data in these contexts would be considered advantageous.

Please ensure you read the Job Description and Person Specification for full details of this role. 
 
Further information

Please contact insert Professor Michael Cant, insert m.a.cant@exeter.ac.uk.

Postdoctoral Research Associate/Fellow
Posted on 09/10/2026
Save Job

Home  Vacancies  Postdoctoral Research Associate/Fellow
About The Role
Postdoctoral Research Associate/Fellow

This EPSRC-funded full-time post is available from February 2027 on a fixed-term basis. Project funding is available for three years, until January 2030.

The starting salary will range from £35,302 to £37,369 for Grade E and will be £44,352 for Grade F, depending on skills and experience.

The Role

Faculty of Environment, Science and Economy

The Williams Lab, at the University of Exeter (Department of Physics) is looking to recruit a Postdoctoral Research Fellow to join an exciting EPSRC mid-infrared sensing project (SPECTROMETA) led by Dr. Calum Williams. 

Mid-infrared light reveals distinctive molecular fingerprints, but measuring these outside specialist laboratories remains challenging. This project combines metamaterial emitters that shape infrared illumination with photoacoustic detection. Together with intelligent inference, this approach aims to identify and quantify environmentally important substances in air and water.

You will lead the development and testing of metamaterial emitters and resonant acoustic cavities, connecting modelling, nanofabrication and sensing experiments. You will investigate what determines sensitivity and selectivity, shape the technical approach, explore AI-assisted inverse design and lead publications. Integration into a working sensor prototype will be a shared effort with the PI, PhD researchers and technical staff. You will use Exeter’s Savchenko Centre for Nanoscience (cleanroom) and Imaging Suite facilities to fabricate and evaluate devices, and build custom electro-optic systems to test their sensing performance. Collaborations with The Met Office and South West Water will connect the research to environmental measurement needs and realistic testing conditions. Based on the Streatham campus, you will join the Williams Lab and the Centre for Metamaterials Research and Innovation (CMRI).

About You

Postdoctoral Research Associate (Grade E)

The successful applicant will possess a relevant PhD (or be nearing completion), or possess equivalent qualifications or experience in physics, photonics, engineering or a related discipline. You will be able to demonstrate sufficient knowledge of the discipline and relevant research methods and techniques to work within established research programmes. You will be able to present research progress and outcomes, communicate complex information orally, in writing and electronically, and prepare proposals and applications to external bodies.

Postdoctoral Research Fellow (Grade F)

The successful applicant will possess a relevant PhD or equivalent qualification/s or experience in a related discipline. You will be a nationally recognised authority in an area relevant to the project, such as optical sensing, photonics, metamaterials or micro- and nanofabrication, with sufficient specialist knowledge to develop research programmes and methodologies.

You will be able to develop research objectives, projects and proposals; identify sources of research funding and contribute to securing funds; and present your research at conferences and other events. You will also work collaboratively, supervise the work of others and act as team leader as required.

For both roles

Applicants will be able to bring depth in at least one relevant area: mid-infrared spectroscopic sensing, metamaterial thermal emitters, instrumentation development, mid-infrared spectroscopy, liquid/gas phase sensing, photonic modelling (FDTD, FEM, RCWA, etc. using Ansys Lumerical, COMSOL, FlexCompute etc.), micro- and nanophotonics, cleanroom fabrication (electron-beam lithography, 2PP-lithography, RIE, PVD etc.) and characterisation (AFM, SEM, FTIR microscopy, custom electro-optic systems, liquid/gas phase sensing etc.). You should demonstrate independent research, relevant research outputs (publications, conference proceedings etc.) and sound judgement in analysing results and resolving technical problems. Strong knowledge of electron beam lithography (and cleanroom fabrication), photoacoustics, inverse design or machine-learning methods is highly desirable.

We do not expect expertise in every technique. We value intellectual curiosity, research rigour and the initiative to turn ideas into experiments. If you bring relevant strengths and are keen to broaden your skills, we encourage you to apply, even if you do not meet every desirable criterion!

Please ensure you read the Job Description and Person Specification for full details of this role.

Further information

For an informal discussion about the role, please contact Dr Calum Williams at c.williams15@exeter.ac.uk (https://experts.exeter.ac.uk/40847-calum-williams) 

 
About Us
Transform Your Career and Help Shape a Greener, Healthier, and Fairer Future

Join the University of Exeter, a top 200 Russell Group university (QS & THE World University Rankings 2025), excelling in teaching (triple Gold rating, TEF 2023) and leading groundbreaking research in the beautiful southwest of England. 

We are committed to understanding different cultures and perspectives, supporting diverse leadership, and striving for social justice. We encourage applications from all groups underrepresented in our community, including racially minoritised individuals and those with disabilities. Our inclusive, merit based recruitment processes seek to embrace a diverse set of experiences to ensure colleagues feel supported equitably. With over 30,000 students and 7,000 staff from 140 countries, we foster a culture where everyone can thrive.

You can read more about our current accreditations and commitment to Equality, Diversity and Inclusion here, including our commitment to the Armed Forces Covenant. 

What we can offer you:
 Freedom (and the support) to pursue your intellectual interests and to work creatively across disciplines;
Support teams that understand the University wide teaching goals and partner with our academics accordingly;
An Innovation, Impact and Business directorate that works closely with our academics providing specialist support for external engagement and development;
Our Exeter Academic initiative supports high performing academics to achieve their potential and develop their career;
 A multitude of staff benefits including sector leading benefits around maternity, adoption and shared parental leave (up to 26 weeks full pay), paternity leave (up to 6 weeks full pay), and a Fertility Treatment Policy;
A beautiful campus set in the heart of stunning Devon/Cornwall. 
 
How we can help

If you are considering applying and need support to do so, please get in touch with us at hrhelpdesk@exeter.ac.uk. You can request reasonable adjustments within your application or by contacting us. You can also choose to be considered under our Disability Confident Scheme and find out here how this is managed during our recruitment and onboarding process.

Description

Thank you for being so interested in joining the Countryside and Community Research Institute (CCRI).

 

CCRI is the largest specialist rural research centre in the UK, having expertise in all aspects of research in policy and planning for the countryside and the environment of the UK, Europe and further afield.  We are a team of social scientists with various disciplinary backgrounds ranging from anthropologists to policy analysts via data scientists and economists.

 

As the CCRI is in a period of expansion we are welcoming speculative applications for the posts of Research Assistant or Fellow, which will be considered as and when new opportunities arise.  We would encourage you to complete the application form and leave a tailored letter to support your CV or application, CV’s without supporting documentation are unlikely to be successful.

 

We are looking for people who have a knowledge of the topics studied at the CCRI (see our website) who are able to work at pace within a supportive but high achieving environment.  All those employed at the CCRI are actively engaged in publishing development activities and will have opportunities to develop their research skills. 

 

We are a diverse team with people with a strong ethos of mutual support and encouragement.  Our achievements have been recognised by the last REF, when we were described as ‘an internationally significant research institute’.  We work with a wide range of collaborators, communities, and partners to create meaningful change.

We are always looking to hear from those who have experience and desire to work in a research. If you have a masters, experience of research methods, research processes, and an interest in the end-to-end lifecycle of a research project, please submit a speculative application. We will keep your details on file for 12 months and if we feel we are recruiting for a suitable position to match your skills, we will be in touch with further information. Please ensure that if you see any opportunities that interest you, please contact askhr@glos.ac.uk.

On the 1 August 2026, the University of Greenwich and the University of Kent formed a pioneering new multi-university group called London and South-East (LASE) University Group.

Should you join us, you will be employed by LASE but will work as part of the University of Greenwich academic division, contributing to its distinct strengths, community and identity while also being part of a wider group that brings together the scale, resilience and shared ambition of both universities.

Through LASE we aim to deliver outstanding education, impactful research, and meaningful regional and global impact.

This is an opportunity to join a particularly vibrant research environment. The university’s Centre for Sustainable Cyber Security is recognised by the UK government as one of only nine Academic Centres of Excellence for both Research and Education in Cyber Security: https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/case-study/the-university-of-greenwich

This position is part of EU project GANNDALF and relates to studying and addressing the privacy-explainability tradeoff of explainable AI use in modern cyber crime investigations. Through agency-to-agency data sharing mechanisms and the deployment of a decision-support toolbox to identify cyber threats, GANNDALF is delivering a customisable and collaborative crime investigation sandbox for scenarios for sophisticated crime investigation. The role holder will help advance our existing work in optimising explainability strength in cyber crime investigations, taking into account privacy. The role holder will also take on the corresponding pilot implementations and evaluations. 

The role holder is expected to have a PhD in computer science or equivalent and a strong publication record in privacy-enhancing technologies or explainable AI. See the job specification for more details.

The post is until the end of the project (end of September 2027), but there is scope to extend further.

Methods and governance arrangements
Reviewing data-governance frameworks and statistical systems
Supporting culturally respectful fieldwork and partner engagement
Helping develop, pilot and disseminate the IP-STATS toolkit with partners in Ghana, Tanzania, Uganda, Peru, Nepal, India, Sri Lanka and Kyrgyzstan.

About the role

We are looking to appoint a part-time Senior Research Fellow, The project will develop a new technology for isotope-resolved fluxomics by extending the Universal Fragmentation Model (UFM) to provide mechanistically justified, atom-resolved interpretations of MS/MS and, where informative, MSⁿ data.

The research will: (1) implement persistent atom mapping and isotopologue support in UFM; (2) build and experimentally validate a flux-oriented fragment knowledgebase that classifies fragments by mechanistic reliability; (3) integrate UFM-derived fragment definitions with established EMU-based metabolic flux analysis tools; and (4) develop robust LC-MS/MS and MSⁿ acquisition and validation workflows, including studies of pentose phosphate pathway flux. Experimental work will use stable-isotope-labelled standards and tracer studies, with high-resolution MS/MS and MSⁿ on an Orbitrap ID-X at Imperial.

The post is funded by the Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC) through the Transformative Research Technologies (25TRT) programme to develop predictive, mechanistically informed tandem mass spectrometry for high-resolution metabolic flux analysis.

The post-holder will develop the UFM software for atom-resolved isotope tracing, perform computational and LC-MS/MS/MSⁿ validation, integrate UFM outputs with established MFA tools, analyse tracer data, and deliver reusable software, benchmark datasets and publications. The post-holder will also contribute to project management, dissemination and development of follow-on research opportunities.

About the role

We are looking for a motivated Postdoctoral Research Associate (PDRA/PostDoc) to join the Safety&Alignment lab at Imperial College London, led by Dr. Oana-Maria Camburu in a fully funded research role. 

The position is fully funded in the context of Dr. Oana-Maria Camburu’s grant on the project Detecting Unverbalized Dangerous Capabilities in Frontier Models. The project focuses on the detection of frontier model’s dangerous capabilities that are not verbalized in their Chain-of-Thoughts (CoTs). Externalized reasoning oversight is a safety paradigm focusing on monitoring the CoTs of large language models (LLMs). As frontier models learn that they are monitored, they can become incentivized to hide their dangerous capabilities from their CoTs. Moreover, as these models become increasingly capable, their obfuscation capabilities also increase, allowing them to bypass monitors. This project investigates ways to detect and defend against such emerging scenarios.  

The post is based in the Department of Computing at Imperial College London at the South Kensington Campus. The Department of Computing is a leading department of Computer Science in the UK and worldwide and has consistently been awarded the highest research rating. In the previous REF assessment, the Department was ranked third (1st in the Research Intensity table published by The Times Higher) and was rated as "Excellent" in the previous national assessment of teaching quality. 

What you would be doing

We strive in publishing in top-tier conferences and journals. Some of the areas you will work on are:

Designing and developing novel algorithms for detecting and defending against unverbalized dangerous capabilities in frontier models. 
Conducting independent and collaborative research within the group. 
Publishing results in top-tier conferences and journals (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, AIJ, TACL, etc). 
Contributing to research projects involving frontier models.
Contributing to the life and development of the Safety & Alignment lab, such weekly meetings, presentations, etc.
Mentoring PhD and MSc students. 

What we are looking for

Candidates should have, or expect shortly to obtain, a PhD in Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics or a closely related discipline, or equivalent research/industrial experience.  You will have practical experience within a research environment and publications in relevant and refereed journals/conferences, such as  NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, TACL, AIJ, etc as well as experience in a broad range of techniques including model checking, monitoring, and CoT.  Research experience in frontier models and in coding with deep learning libraries such as Pytorch is also essential.  

Please see job description for a full list of requirements.

Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes).

Full-time, fixed term for 12 months to start ASAP and before 8th April 2027.

About the role

We are looking for a candidate with experience in optimal quantum control for the collaborative QuantERA project FALCON. The successful candidate is expected to design optimised driving schemes that allow the experimental partner in Innsbruck (UIBK & AQT) to implement entangling gates with trapped ions that achieve high fidelities under practical conditions, i.e. at finite temperature and without accurate calibration.

The candidate should have strong interest in collaborative work, and they should collaborate both with the experimental partner in Innsbruck and with the theory partner in Sofia.

What you would be doing

Your main role would be the design of optimised driving patterns for the realisation of noise-resilient quantum gates of trapped ions. Together with the other consortium partners you would identify the main sources of imperfections in the consortium’s experiments that result in reduction of gate fidelities, and you would develop optimal control solutions to achieve resilience to the identified imperfections.

You would use both analytical and numerical tools for your work, and you would interact on a regular basis with all the project partners.

What we are looking for

We are looking for a candidate who holds a PhD with theoretical/numerical work in the fields of quantum information/quantum technologies. Additional experience as Postdoc is desired but not necessary.

You should have a strong interest in collaborative work, and the ability to communicate with experimental partners.

About the role

Please note interviews will be held on a rolling basis while the advert is live. It is therefore strongly recommended that you submit your application as early as possible. The advert will be closed once a suitable candidate is selected.

Are you an early-career researcher passionate about advancing fundamental knowledge in the field of atomic, molecular and optical physics and its rapid translation into real-life applications?

We are seeking a highly motivated individual to join the Department of Chemistry at Imperial College London as a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network Researcher, funded by the Horizon Europe Marie Curie Doctoral Network TRILOGY.

TRILOGY advances the emerging field of ultrafast chirality by exploiting attosecond light-driven electron dynamics to overcome the limits of conventional chiroptical methods. Targeting applications in the life sciences and advanced technologies, we aim to develop next-generation, high-sensitivity spectroscopic tools to excite and probe electron motion in chiral molecules, supported by close collaboration with industrial partners to enable rapid translation into applications.

TRILOGY brings together 11 leading institutions across Europe to train 16 Doctoral Candidates at the forefront of theory and experiment in ultrafast science. The programme offers a unique, interdisciplinary environment and equips researchers with highly competitive skills spanning fundamental physics, technology development, and industry.

At Imperial College London, the Research Assistant will contribute to the work package titled: “Enantiosensitive imaging and manipulation with locally chiral evanescent waves.”

What you would be doing

In this role, you will take a leading part in shaping the emerging field of ultrafast chirality. You will:

Develop a theoretical and computational framework to model light propagation in confined environments and the ultrafast electronic response of chiral matter to such tailored light.
Investigate how we can shape matter at the nanoscale to shape light’s polarisation in three dimensions for efficient chiral sensing and manipulation.
Explore how to bring the outcome of fundamental research in atomic, molecular and optical physics to real-life applications.
Work closely with international partners across the TRILOGY consortium and undertake up to two-month placements at academic and industrial partners, gaining first-hand experience of how fundamental research informs real-world applications.
Build your research profile through journal publications, conference presentations, and collaborative project deliverables, supported by an exceptional network of academic and industry mentors across Europe.

What we are looking for

A good Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Physics, Chemistry, or a closely related field.
Strong knowledge in atomic, molecular and optical physics.
Skills in computational modelling and data analysis (e.g., Python, MATLAB or similar).
Demonstrated interest or prior experience in theoretical and computational approaches to light-matter interactions.
Ability to meet the academic requirements for PhD registration at Imperial College London.
Willingness to undertake international travel and placements within the consortium. TRILOGY brings together 11 leading institutions across Europe to train 16 Doctoral Candidates at the forefront of theory and experiment in ultrafast science.

Eligibility requirements: 

Applicant must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of the organization they are applying to for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to the recruitment.
Applicant must not yet been awarded a PhD degree and must be in the first 4 years (full-time equivalent) of their research careers prior to the recruitment.
The successful candidate will be employed as a Research Assistant and must apply for admission as a PhD student with Imperial College London and be able to meet our criteria for admission.

What we can offer you

The opportunity to work at a world-leading institution developing novel approaches for ultrafast and highly efficient chiral sensing and manipulation through state-of-the-art theoretical and computational modelling.
A sector-leading salary and benefits package, including 43 days' annual leave.
Access to training modules, networking events and research exchanges within the Marie Curie Doctoral Network.
Support for developing your PhD thesis, career skills and publication record.
The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity.
Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression.
Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.
The Research Assistant will be paid an attractive salary for 36 months (as defined in MSCA guidelines). The exact (net) salary will be confirmed upon appointment and is dependent on local tax, social and health insurance regulations and on the country correction factor (to allow for the difference in cost of living in the different EU Member States).
The Research Assistant will also be compensated with a Mobility Allowance for researchers who have a family, as well as a Family Allowance. All amounts are subject to deductions and taxes. Family is defined as persons linked to the researcher by (i) marriage, or (ii) a relationship with equivalent status to a marriage recognised by the national legislation of the country of the beneficiary or of the nationality of the researcher, or (iii) dependent children who are being maintained by the researcher; family status is determined at recruitment and does not evolve.

Further information

Duration: 36 months (full-time, fixed term).
Base: Department of Chemistry, Imperial College London (White City Campus)
Salary: £44,284.07 per annum (without Family Allowance) or £48,796.89 per annum (with Family Allowance).

About the role

We are seeking to recruit an enthusiastic and motivated structural biologist to join the group of Prof Harry Low, Department of Infectious Disease (www.thelowlab.org).

The research project focuses on determining the molecular mechanism of bacterial secretion systems including the Tad and Type 4 pilus systems. The position is funded by an 8 year Wellcome Trust Discovery award.

What you would be doing

You will be leading your own project working from initial clones through to protein purification, structure determination and biochemical/biophysical mechanistic dissection.

What we are looking for

Experience in light microscopy studies is desirable. You must have a strong research track record demonstrated by at least one first author publication in an international journal or bioRxiv.

An inclusive and friendly lab environment that aims to support you in your mission to make important discoveries and generate impactful publications.
A well-funded lab underpinned by world class facilities.

About the role

Are you an ambitious bioinformatician looking to apply cutting-edge computational biology to one of the most exciting challenges in global health?

As a Bioinformatics Research Associate in this specially created position by Imperial College to support the success of the £7.5 million ARIA-funded M2M (Mechanism to Medicine) programme, you will play a central role in helping to uncover the innate immune mechanisms that protect individuals from respiratory viral infections and accelerate the development of a new generation of preventative medicines.

Working alongside Professor Ajit Lalvani and a multidisciplinary consortium of leading academic and industry partners (including Prof Marko Nikolic at UCL, Dr Adrian Grzybowski at AnuBio inc., and Dr Sarah Teichman at University of Cambridge among others), you will integrate and analyse complex multi-omics datasets, generate novel biological insights, and directly support AI-driven approaches to therapeutic discovery.

What you would be doing

Lead the harmonisation, integration and analysis of large-scale multi-omics datasets, including single-cell transcriptomics, epigenomics and proteomics data.
Develop, maintain and document robust computational pipelines for processing and quality control of next-generation sequencing and proteomics datasets.
Identify innate immune correlates of protection through advanced bioinformatics analyses across clinical and laboratory-derived datasets.
Work closely with AI and mathematical modelling teams to ensure bioinformatics outputs support downstream predictive modelling and therapeutic development.
Collaborate with researchers across Imperial, UCL, industry partners and international collaborators to deliver key project milestones.
Present findings to collaborators, funding bodies and at scientific conferences, while contributing to high-impact publications and future grant applications.
Support implementation of FAIR data principles and open science practices across the programme

What we are looking for

We are looking for a highly motivated and collaborative scientist with:

A PhD in bioinformatics, computational biology, computer science, genetics, statistics or a closely related discipline (or equivalent experience).

*Candidates who have not yet been officially awarded their PhD will be appointed as a Research Assistant within the salary range £45,399 - £48,876 per annum.

Strong programming skills in Python, R, Bash and/or Perl and experience working in Unix/Linux environments.
Hands-on experience analysing genomics and multi-omics datasets, including scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, bulk RNA-seq and proteomics data.
Experience developing reproducible computational workflows using tools such as Nextflow, Snakemake or equivalent workflow management systems.
Experience working with HPC or cloud computing infrastructure and modern reproducible research practices.
Excellent analytical, communication and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.
A passion for translating complex biological data into impactful scientific discoveries.

The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity.

The opportunity to work on a pioneering £7.5 million ARIA-funded programme with the potential to transform protection against respiratory viral diseases.
A unique position at the interface of bioinformatics, immunology, artificial intelligence and translational medicine.
Collaboration with leading researchers and partners from Imperial College London, UCL, industry and international institutions.
Genuine opportunities to contribute to high-impact publications, establish scientific independence and support future funding applications.

About the role

This research associated with this post will be part of a wider team within the new Horizon Europe OceanSOS project https://oceansos.net/. This exciting interdisciplinary project aims to determine the impact of seamounts and the currents they create on stimulating the overlying biological carbon pump (BCP), to then inform marine spatial planning. The knowledge generated will provide a stronger foundation for assessing future ocean risks and developing sustainable management approaches. By improving understanding of the links between biodiversity, food webs, and carbon cycling, this work will support decision-making aimed at protecting ocean ecosystems and the processes that sustain them. This is an exciting opportunity to be part of an international team of biogeochemists, physical ocean modellers, ecologists and policy makers.

What you would be doing

You will focus on identifying how seafloor topology influences the mesopelagic biological carbon pump, specifically looking at particle type, size and microbial remineralisation across a seamount and abyssal plain. You will be part of a wider team https://oceansos.net/wp3  capturing the contributions of larger organisms, deep-sea communities, and connections between the seafloor and the open ocean in the BCP. Your specific responsibilities will include going to sea in the North Atlantic (Summer 2027) and will use multiple techniques to determine the regional BCP, to then feed into the physical, food-web and statistical models, used by the OceanSOS team. The post-holder will also facilitate fieldwork south of South Africa (early Summer 2027) and the samples collected from this region. The tools you will use at sea include sediment traps, marine snow catchers and optodes to measure microbial remineralisation.

You will be responsible for organising your component of the fieldwork so it is essential you have fieldwork experience at sea. You will also process the samples you collect to then lead and co-author peer-reviewed publications, and will work closely with the wider project team. You will have the opportunity to present findings to the research team as well as at national and/or international conferences. As this project is part of a large consortium, the you will have the opportunity, and be expected to, collaborate widely within our smaller sub-team, but also with the rest of the consortia including at annual science meetings. There will also be the opportunity to work with international partners.

What we are looking for

Experience in fieldwork and sample analysis associated with the biological pump, sediment traps and/or microbial respiration
A track record of overseeing successful experiments from design, manipulation and sampling, to data analysis and publishing the results
Knowledge of processes involved in organic carbon cycling in the ocean
Ideally some experience of leading your own work at sea
Knowledge of how to analyse organic carbon samples
Enthusiasm for research in ocean carbon science

What we can offer you

Being part of a large international network of project partners from across Europe, with many travel opportunities

About the role

Supported by funding from the BBSRC, we are seeking a talented post-doctoral research associate to join the team in the group of Professor Andrew Edwards at Imperial College London. This role will investigate how polymyxin antibiotics kill Gram-negative bacteria.

The position is available full time, starting by October 2026 (or as soon as possible thereafter) and is available for 12 months.

Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents a significant and growing global health threat, with recent projections estimating that 39 million deaths will be directly attributed to AMR between 2025–2050. Of particular concern are Gram-negative bacteria such as E. coli. The emergence of multi-antibiotic resistant strains necessitates the use of reserve (last resort) antibiotics such as the polymyxins. However, this class of antibiotics are poorly efficacious and efforts to improve their use are hampered by an incomplete understanding of how they work.  

What you would be doing

The Edwards group is based in the Department of Infectious Disease and the Centre for Bacterial Resistance Biology and encompasses scientists at all levels of experience. We are looking for candidates who can thrive in this dynamic and creative environment. The appointed candidate is expected to lead studies that aim to understand how polymyxins function, including experimental planning and execution, data analysis and presentation and writing of manuscripts.

What we are looking for

Essential criteria for the role include:

A PhD in bacteriology or related field.

*Candidates who have not yet been officially awarded their PhD will be appointed as a Research Assistant within the salary range £45,399 - £48,876 per annum.

Experience in genetic manipulation of Gram-negative bacteria.
Experience in nanoscale imaging techniques including AFM.
Ability to work collaboratively, experience in experimental planning, troubleshooting, data analysis, and safe laboratory working practices.

 

Desirable experience for this role includes one or more of the following: Experience in studying membrane biology of Gram-negative bacteria, knowledge of antibiotics and resistance, evolution of resistance, assay development. 

 

What we can offer you

Become part of a multidisciplinary team working on the major challenge of antibiotic resistance.
The opportunity to develop your research career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity.
Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression.
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 41 days off a year and generous pension schemes).
Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

This is a full-time, on-site post (35 hours per week). This role is for a fixed-term contract for 12 months.

You will develop AI models to predict whole-cell antifungal activity across ultra-large, synthesis-on-demand chemical spaces. In addition, you will develop AI models to predict antifungal-induced toxicity across multiple biological contexts, including organ-specific iPSC-derived cell lines. Using pre- and post-treatment scRNA-seq profiles of C. auris, you will develop models to predict the susceptibility or resistance of individual C. auris isolates to specific antifungal treatments based solely on their pre-treatment transcriptional profiles. These models will support the selection of effective drug therapies and the identification of optimal treatment combinations for antifungal-resistant C. auris strains.

You will gain unique hands-on experience with both numerical techniques and with the most advanced lab equipment. You will get the opportunity to travel to International Scientific conferences and to University (Oxford) and industrial (Rolls-Royce) partners.

Your work will focus on developing innovative concepts to characterise and simulate translaminar fracture (such as in the case of a blade out event). You will design and develop innovative translaminar fracture characterisation and simulation capabilities for CFRP with advanced and complex microstructures (such as braided composites), suitable for aircraft engine fan blades. Location: Denmark Hill Campus. Category: Research.

Back to job search

THIS VACANCY IS OPEN TO INTERNAL APPLICANTS ONLY
About us:

The post will be based at King’s College London within the QUAHRC and the NIHR Research Support Service.

The successful candidate will join a multidisciplinary team delivering an NIHR-funded methodology project focused on Collaborative Data Analysis (CDA) in applied health and social care research.

Collaborative Data Analysis brings multiple perspectives into the interpretation of research data, including those of people with lived experience. While CDA has considerable potential to improve the relevance, inclusivity and usefulness of qualitative research, existing approaches are dispersed across methodological and participatory traditions and there is limited practical guidance to help research teams implement CDA well.

The project will address this implementation gap by co-designing a national, integrated CDA implementation toolkit for applied health and social care research. The toolkit will include an implementation framework, methodological decision-support tool, training and facilitation resources, and an accessible digital platform. The project will work closely with researchers, methodological specialists, PPIE professionals and people with lived experience throughout its development.

About the role:

About us

Applicants are sought for a postdoctoral position at the interface of quantum chemistry, condensed matter physics and quantum information theory, for research into novel computational methodology for correlated electronic structure problems. 

The position will be held at King’s College London, in the research group of Prof. George Booth, with the project also embedded within a wider EPSRC-NSF funded collaboration with research groups at Indiana University and Virginia Tech in the US. 

The position will be held within the Theory and Simulation of Condensed Matter group, part of the department of Physics, which belongs to the Faculty of Natural, Mathematical & Engineering Sciences (NMES), located on the Strand campus of KCL. 

The candidate will be part of an active research environment for numerical and analytical approaches to quantum many-body systems, in addition to the wider inter-disciplinary collaboration. Excellent opportunities for interactions also exist in an established and active London-based materials and molecular modelling environment.

About the role

We are seeking a motivated postdoctoral research associate, keen to work in a team, and be embedded in a wider project involving the development of scalable computational methods for correlated electronic structure theory. 

The project aims to broadly exploit emerging quantum information resource-theoretic ideas to extend the scope of existing electronic structure methodology towards correlated systems across chemistry and physics applications, in particular for ground state and spectral simulation. 

Applicants are expected to have a PhD, or are awaiting its award, in a relevant area (Theoretical/Computational Physics or Chemistry), and experience in the area of quantum many-body theory, its development or implementation, from a quantum chemistry, condensed matter physics or quantum information theory perspective. The successful applicant will be expected to work within a collaborative cross-disciplinary project, and actively contribute to the success of this collaboration.  

Key responsibilities, beyond the primary role of contributing to internationally-leading research in many-electron theory, include the development and maintenance of computer software, active collaboration, leadership and mentorship of more junior group members, as well as contributions to effective research culture and effective dissemination of the project outputs.

This is a full time post and you will be offered a fixed term contract until 31st August 2029 in the first instance. Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development.

About us

The post will be based on the Guy’s Campus within the School of Basic and Medical Biosciences at St John’s Institute of Dermatology. The candidate will work closely with the principal investigator Dr Joanna Jacków-Malinowska. We will closely work with Prof John McGrath and Prof Jemima Mellerio, both of whom are world-renowned experts in Epidermolysis Bullosa and will be the key clinical personnel to guide with clinical relevant questions to this project. The postholder also will benefit more broadly from the vast interdisciplinary research and academic networks at King’s College London  and elsewhere.

About the role

We are seeking an enthusiastic researcher to join an innovative project investigating blister fluid as a minimally invasive source of patient-derived cells in recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (RDEB). The project aims to establish a new liquid-biopsy approach for isolating and expanding keratinocytes, fibroblasts, stem/progenitor cells and mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) from EB blister fluid.

The successful candidate will develop and optimise cell-isolation and culture protocols, characterise patient-derived cell populations using cell-surface markers, immunostaining and molecular/transcriptional approaches, and assess their potential as disease-relevant models for RDEB. The work will ultimately support the development of a patient-derived EB cell biobank and future gene-editing and regenerative therapies.

This is an exciting opportunity to work at the interface of stem cell biology, dermatology, liquid biopsy and gene therapy, using patient-derived material to develop new approaches for understanding and treating EB.

This is a full-time post (35 hours per week) based on-site. You will be offered a fixed term contract until 31st October 2027.

Essential criteria.

Master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant biological or biomedical science subject.
Demonstrable research experience following completion of the Master’s degree keen in PhD afterwards.
Practical experience working with primary human cells, ideally keratinocytes and/or fibroblasts.
Experience in molecular and cell biology techniques and cell culture.
Ability to plan and deliver experimental work independently to agreed timescales and quality standards.
Good data-handling, analytical and scientific communication skills.
Ability to work collaboratively across KCL St John’s Institute of Dermatology and other Institutes.
Strong interest in EB, skin regeneration, patient-derived cells or gene-editing approaches, with enthusiasm to develop specialist expertise in EB blister-fluid-derived cells.

Desirable criteria

Experience working with epidermolysis bullosa (EB), wound healing or rare skin diseases.
Experience handling blister fluid or other liquid-biopsy samples.
Experience with mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) or other stem/progenitor cell populations.
Experience with 3D skin models, organotypic cultures or regenerative medicine.
Experience with gene-editing technologies, particularly in primary human skin cells.

About Us

Applications are invited for the position of Post-Doctoral Research Associate as part of a Medical Research Council Funded Research proposal in the Research Department of Imaging Physics & Engineering, School of Biomedical Engineering and Imaging Sciences (BMEIS) at King’s College London.

This position is based at St Thomas’ Hospital with additional close links to King’s College Hospital. We therefore work directly at the interface of clinical and engineering research which provides valuable insight into the challenges and opportunities in acquiring and interpreting clinical data, offering exciting opportunities to perform truly translational research.

About The Role

This is an exciting opportunity for an enthusiastic researcher to develop state-of-the-art methodologies and quantification for contrast enhanced ultrasound imaging. This will require experiences in data acquisition and processing related to ultrasound imaging and contrast enhanced ultrasound. This aims to provide a reliable and repeatable clinical technique to extract quantitative microvascular information.

The purpose of the role is to design, develop, and perform experiments and to develop associated processing strategies for contrast enhanced and super-resolution ultrasound imaging. The PDRA will work on the project’s experimental and data acquisition aspects, as well as signal and image analysis. This will involve designing, developing and performing experimental systems and acquisition protocols. The RA will assist with data curation and implementation of processing software. This will require computational skills, good knowledge of programming languages such as MATLAB, and an ability to plan experiments, make and record observations and test hypotheses. The candidate will propose and define strategies for extending the imaging strategies with a programmable research system.

This is a part-time post (7 hours per week), and you will be offered a fixed term contract for 14 months*.*

Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. Essential criteria

PhD in STEM subject OR equivalent industrial experience, in physics, medical imaging, acoustics, signal processing, or a closely related field*
Highly developed verbal and written communication skills in English (ranging from informal 1:1 discussions, formal presentations covering both oral and written skills), including the ability to liaise with staff at a range of levels internal and external to the organisation
Strong research background on a relevant field backed by published peer-reviewed work
Programming skills
Self-motivated and able to work independently

Evidence of collaborative work
Enthusiastic attitude and scientific approach to solving research problems.

Experience with ultrasound image analysis

The Role

Are you passionate about tackling health inequalities through community-engaged research? Kingston University is seeking a Research Associate for CHAMPIONS-PT, an NIHR-funded programme co-designing and piloting a Community Champions intervention to improve routine vaccination uptake among Black African and Caribbean pregnant women and young children in London.

Working with NHS and public health partners, local authorities, community organisations and people with lived experience, CHAMPIONS-PT will explore barriers to vaccination, develop culturally appropriate approaches and assess the feasibility and acceptability of the intervention.

Based in the School of Nursing, Allied and Public Health and working with Professor Tushna Vandrevala, you will:

-Support community engagement, lived-experience groups, co-design workshops and designathons.
-Undertake qualitative data collection and analysis.
-Support recruitment, study coordination and implementation and process evaluation of the pilot.
-Contribute to publications, reports, presentations and knowledge mobilisation.

This post offers an opportunity to develop expertise in participatory public health research, intervention development and health inequalities.

Please note, an enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check clearance is required for the role. 

The Person

You will normally be completing or have recently completed a PhD in social science, public health or a related discipline. You will bring qualitative research skills, experience of participatory or community-engaged approaches, and a commitment to inclusive research. Experience working with ethnically diverse communities or in maternal and child health would be valuable. You will be organised, collaborative and able to communicate effectively with academic, professional and community audiences.

School of Nursing , Allied and Public Health

NIHR ARCs bring together universities, NHS organisations, local authorities, health and care providers, voluntary and community organisations, and the public to deliver applied research that improves health and social care services and outcomes.

The ARC London Research Inclusion theme aims to strengthen inclusive research practices, address structural barriers to participation and ensure research better reflects and benefits London's diverse and underserved communities.

Based within Kingston University's School of Nursing, Allied and Public Health, you will play a leading role in delivering Research Inclusion initiatives across London. Working collaboratively with academic, NHS, local authority, VCSE and community partners, you will:

Design, deliver and evaluate research inclusion projects involving underserved communities.

Build partnerships and support training and capacity-building across the research community.
Contribute to academic publications, knowledge mobilisation activities and future research funding proposals.

Career development opportunities

This NIHR Career Development Award offers an opportunity to develop your interdisciplinary research profile and progress towards research independence and leadership.

Our ARC London Career Development Award holders will have regular networking opportunities and be members of the NIHR Academy (benefits of academy membership), with access to networking and professional development opportunities. These include a personalised development plan, peer mentorship, research leadership activities and opportunities to apply for training and development funding.

You will also benefit from support in research inclusion, patient and public involvement and engagement (PPIE), implementation science and knowledge mobilisation.

The Person

You will normally hold a PhD in a relevant discipline or have submitted your thesis for examination by the time of application and expect it to be awarded before taking up the post. You will have a strong track record in applied health or social care research. You will have experience or a strong interest in research inclusion, health inequalities and working with underserved populations.

We particularly welcome candidates with experience of co-production, PPIE, participatory research or community partnerships. You will be able to design and deliver high-quality research, collaborate across professional and community settings, and communicate findings effectively to academic and non-academic audiences.

You will demonstrate strong research integrity, organisational and communication skills, and a commitment to making research more inclusive and accessible. The post holder will join the School of Arts, to be part of an exciting 2-year £4m interdisciplinary project SOILL Step Up funded by the EU Horizon program. This project will help evaluate and understand the impacts of 100 living labs across Europe are having in improving our soils.

 As part of the landmark Soil-Deal for Europe, SOILL-Step up builds on the SOILL-Startup project for the implementation of the ambitious objectives of the Horizon Europe Mission. The aim is to establish 100 Soil Health Living Labs and Lighthouse projects. The project runs across 2026 and 2027 and aims to support and empower a growing soil health community in Europe. Lancaster University are one of the supporting organisations in this project with a focus on evaluation, impact and new engagement activities.

Key duties of the role include providing expertise in creative evaluation and understanding different dimensions or aspects of impact.  There is no requirement for technical knowledge of soil health measures, our area of concern will be more focused on areas including effect on policy at local, national or EU level, or the degree of engagement with local communities by the living lab. You will be involved in data gathering activities such as developing surveys and interviewing members of Soil living labs.  There will also be significant amount of analysis of this (mostly text based) data. An exciting opportunity arises to support two large projects: 1) a Royal Society funded fellowship: Harnessing island-ocean connections to support ecosystems and people, and 2) a UKRI funded fellowship: Ensuring Transformative Ecosystem Restoration by the Private Sector.

Location: Lancaster. Travel for fieldwork and project meetings as required.

Duration: 3 years with possibility of extension

We are seeking a highly motivated and enthusiastic individual to support the delivery of two research fellowships and the associated research teams:

A Royal Society Faraday Discovery Fellowship awarded to Prof Nick Graham to establish the Island-Ocean Research Hub. This new project will investigate island-ocean connectivity and the influence of seabird nutrients and island rewilding on island and marine ecology and ecosystem services. The project has collaborating parters at 4 other universities, fieldwork planned in 5 countries, and will employ a large team of researchers. Your role would support this fellowship for 0.5 FTE of your time (i.e. 2.5 days per week)

A UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship awarded to Dr Tim Lamont. This project will investigate mechanisms for scaling up tropical marine restoration (coral reefs, mangroves and seagrass), and the role of business sustainability initiatives in delivering large-scale ecosystem restoration. The project has collaborations with the world’s largest coral restoration programme (www.buildingcoral.com), and the private sector’s most widely used sustainability reporting standards (www.globalreporting.org). Your role would support this fellowship for 0.3 FTE of your time (i.e. 1.5 days per week)

 The role will include elements of the following, along with general support for the two projects: Fieldwork planning to include risk assessments, diving safety, ethics and research permits; fieldwork support and possible involvement as research assistant; lab work and organisation; website and logo development and maintenance; social media and public engagement support; team cohesion and coordination including organising socials and retreats; team visas and other needs; workshop and meeting organisation; budget oversight and spending; help with reporting; data management and requests for data sharing; maintaining contact with project partners and collaborators; welcoming and inducting visitors and new group members. 

You will work closely with Nick Graham and Tim Lamont, collaborate with other members of the research team, and coordinate with project partners.

Preferred candidates will have experience in marine / biological science and/or project management. A proactive and enthusiastic approach and good interpersonal skills are essential.

An exciting opportunity exists for a marine scientist or community ecologist to contribute to a Royal Society funded project: Harnessing island-ocean connections to support ecosystems and people. This is a 4 year role.

Location: Lancaster. Travel for fieldwork and collaborations as required.

We are seeking a highly motivated and enthusiastic temperate or warm-water marine scientist and/or community ecologist to join the Island-Ocean Research Hub. This new research hub will investigate island-ocean connectivity and the influence of seabirds and island rewilding on ecosystem structure, function, and benefits to people. This specific position will focus on how biodiversity-ecosystem function relationships and ecosystem recovery potential are influenced by seabird nutrient inputs. Potential study sites will include the inner and southern Seychelles, the Mediterranean Sea and island archipelagos around the UK, and ecosystems to explore include Mangroves, seagrass, coral reefs and kelp. This project is led out of Lancaster University, with a number of collaborating universities and NGOs. Fieldwork for the project will include periods in remote locations, working in small teams, and scuba and snorkel-based work, and experience of such working will be essential. The successful applicant will work closely with Prof Nick Graham on this project, and collaborate with other members of the research team, both in Lancaster and at collaborating institutions.

Preferred candidates will have a PhD in marine science/disturbance ecology, experience of fieldwork, skills in statistical modelling, and a proven ability to publish scientific papers. A proactive and enthusiastic approach and good interpersonal skills are essential. 

The Lancaster Environment Centre (LEC) is a large and multidisciplinary department, tackling environmental challenges across the natural and social sciences. Location:  Bailrigg, Lancaster, UK
Salary:   £39,906 to £46,049 (Full-Time/Indefinite with End Date)
Closing Date:   Sunday 29 November 2026
Interview Date:   Friday 18 December 2026
Reference:  1137-26

The School of Mathematical Sciences at Lancaster University invites applications for a three-year postdoctoral position to work on the EPSRC-funded project “Mutations and geometric models”. The Principal Investigator is Dr Coelho Simões. 

Calabi-Yau (CY) triangulated categories are ubiquitous in mathematics, particularly in geometry and representation theory. Due to their physical origin, n-CY categories have been extensively studied for n=2,3. However, as a homological condition, the n-CY property can be studied for any integer n meaning there are many more examples: categories naturally arising in modular representation theory, singularity theory, Fuss-Catalan combinatorics, and higher homological algebra are n-CY for n different from 2 and 3. The systematic study of CY categories in these wider contexts is in its infancy and many aspects remain poorly understood. The main aim of the project seeks to provide methods to address this shortfall using mutations and geometric models.

The successful candidate is expected to hold a PhD degree in mathematics or a related discipline, with specialism in one of the fields of homological algebra, representation theory or algebraic combinatorics. Expertise in triangulated categories, representation theory of finite-dimensional algebras, combinatorial/geometric models arising from surfaces, singularity theory or modular representation theory is highly desirable. You will be expected to learn quickly, engage with new ideas, and contribute new insights.

This work will take place in our thriving Pure Mathematics section, which has considerable expertise in algebra, geometry, analysis, probability, and discrete mathematics. Lancaster is one of the UK’s top mathematical science departments, ranked 7th in the most recent Research Excellence Framework, and joint 1st for the impact of its research. The School, which holds an Athena SWAN Bronze Award, strives to provide a supportive and friendly environment for early career researchers, and offers a comprehensive career development programme. You will be able to focus on your research as the post carries no teaching or administrative duties. Teaching experience will be available on a voluntary basis should you wish to gain teaching experience. You will be encouraged to conduct research visits and will have access to travel funds to do so. 

The position starts on 1st February 2027 (or as soon as possible after), for up to 36 months. When applying, in addition to completing the online application, candidates should attach a full CV, a cover letter, a 1-page research statement describing how your expertise is relevant to this position and your future research plans, and the details of two referees. Interviews will take place in December and will be conducted online.

Please contact Dr Raquel Coelho Simões (r.coelhosimoes@lancaster.ac.uk) for further information or to discuss the post informally.

The University of Lincoln is seeking a highly motivated Post-Doctoral Research Associate (PDRA) with substantial academic research background, with demonstrated expertise in food safety and hygiene or food process validation to join the Vitrum project. Vitrum is an ambitious Innovate UK-funded collaboration developing a commercially deployable robotic harvesting system for on-the-vine tomatoes, helping address labour shortages in UK horticulture through the automation of protected crop harvesting. 

Led by Dogtooth Technologies in partnership with APS Produce and the University of Lincoln, the project brings together expertise in robotics, AI-driven perception, commercial horticulture and food safety to validate robotic harvesting under real production conditions. 

The Role

You will lead research on the food safety and quality assurance aspects of robotic harvesting, with a particular focus on hygiene validation, microbiological challenge studies and process validation. Working closely with robotics researchers, academic colleagues and industry partners, you will contribute to the development and validation of a harvesting system that meets food safety, hygiene and regulatory requirements ahead of commercial deployment. 

Key areas of research will include:

Microbiological safety and contamination risks associated with robotic harvesting.
Process validation and microbiological challenge studies.
Hygiene validation of robotic harvesting equipment and food-contact surfaces.
Evaluation of cleaning and sanitation approaches.
Cross-contamination risks within commercial glasshouse environments.
The impact of mechanised harvesting on product safety and quality.

This is a highly applied research role, offering opportunities to undertake trials in both University research facilities and commercial production environments while contributing to high-quality project outputs, publications and future research activity.

About You

You will ideally hold a PhD in Microbiology, Food Safety, Food Science, Biological Sciences or a closely related discipline. You will have strong knowledge of food microbiology, food safety, hygiene regulation and validation methodologies, together with hands on experience of designing and conducting microbiological experiments, process validation, challenge studies and/or hygiene validation. 

You will be able to design and manage independent research, communicate complex scientific information effectively and work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary academic and industrial team. Experience of trials in food production environments or fresh produce and horticultural food safety research would be advantageous. 

This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to innovative research at the intersection of food safety, microbiology, robotics and commercial horticulture, while working with leading academic and industrial partners.

For informal enquiries, please contact Dr Bukola Onarinde (bonarinde@lincoln.ac.uk). 

As an Athena SWAN Bronze Award holder, the University is committed to advancing gender equality in STEM and welcomes applications from under-represented groups.
