Liverpool John Moores University (LJMU) is a distinctive, unique institution, rooted in the Liverpool City Region and with a global presence. Our students and staff, past, present, and future, are the beating heart of our city and can be found in every corner of every industry and community. We couldn’t exist anywhere else and have shaped the city in which we belong. Working with the people of Liverpool to improve lives and support communities is at the heart of why we were founded and why we exist today.

We are looking for a highly skilled and motivated Postdoctoral Research Associate for a full-time fixed term contract for 2 years to undertake applied research on the environmental sustainability of high water-table agriculture.

This work will support the delivery of the UK Innovate funded Farming Innovation Project (FIP): ‘System innovation to transform underperforming peatlands into profitable, carbon sequestering farmland’. This industry-led project focuses on the development and assessment of Typha-based paludiculture in order to deliver more sustainable, commercially viable agriculture and agricultural products (‘BioPuff®’) from high-water peatland farming. LJMU’s Role is primarily focused on assessing the environmental and ecological sustainability credentials of the agricultural systems associated with this project.

This exciting and hugely impactful project will develop one of the largest UK paludiculture sites, developing knowledge at a new scale which will have implications both commercially and for policy development. The role will be weighted strongly in three main fields: 1) peat biogeochemistry – specifically developing and undertaking a monitoring scheme and reporting of GHG emissions, soil and water physiochemistry and fluvial emissions for verification on environmental credentials and Life Cycle Assessments and 2) biodiversity/ecological surveys of the trial area and 3) assessing and reporting on the efficacy of the automated monitoring network and site establishment approaches.

You will lead elements in the coordination of project goals and collaborate with project partners (both NGO and commercial). You will (in collaboration with the project partners) help design and develop coordinated  approaches to the data collection and design the monitoring to support the reporting programme/timeline.  Lab work, data analysis and the drafting/ submission of peer-reviewed publications, alongside project reports aligning with deliverables will also be undertaken. Administrative tasks linked to purchasing, time sheet reporting and aiding in research assistant management/supervision will also be required. This is a strongly industry-led project and the outputs of which include a strong commercial component and so the postholder will be expected to undertake wider engagement with the larger project and partners and the reporting requirements will reflect this commercial expectation. 

You will also form part of both a wider peat research team (other PDRAs and PhDs) led by Professor Evers at LJMU but also collaborate more widely with both the project team and parallel projects the LJMU team is working on linked to sustainable management of UK lowland peat agricultural land. As such, being a strong team player and adaptable to a collaborative approach, as well as a strong independent worker will be critical to the success of this post.

Informal enquiries can be made to Professor Stephanie Evers at S.L.Evers@ljmu.ac.uk

In return, we offer an excellent benefits package including generous annual leave entitlement, pension scheme, induction and development support as well as family-friendly policies.

This is an exciting time to join the university as we deliver the LJMU Strategy 2030 and its vision of LJMU as an inclusive civic university transforming lives and futures, by placing students at the heart of everything we do.

If you feel that this is the role you have been looking for and your skills and experience can make a real difference at LJMU, we look forward to hearing from you.

LJMU values diversity and provides a supportive and inclusive environment where everyone can fulfil their potential.

Please note all of our vacancies will be closed to applications at midnight on the advertised closing date, unless otherwise stated.

LJMU are committed to adhering to the Principles set out in the Researcher Development Concordat; in line with this all fixed-term researchers will be supported to complete 10 days professional development activities per year (pro-rata).

Strong interest and/or training in primatology, genomics, conservation or related fields.

The Faculty of Science and Engineering is one of the UK's largest providers of science, engineering and technology education, combining world-leading research with innovative teaching and strong industry engagement. Our academics work across disciplines to address emerging global challenges while equipping graduates with the skills and knowledge needed to succeed in a rapidly changing world.   

About the School 

The School of Engineering and Environment brings together expertise across a broad range of engineering and environmental disciplines, delivering high-quality education, impactful research and strong industrial engagement.  Engineering at our University ranked 6th in the UK in the last REF for the impact of our research. We have real strengths in advanced materials and manufacturing in the school through our additive manufacturing facility PrintCity and our surface engineering group.   

About the Project  

The University was recently successful in securing funding to deliver the Challenge AI programme. The programme is funded by the Local Innovation Partnership Fund. ChallengeAI connects businesses with universities, researchers and industry experts through funded pathways designed to support the responsible adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI). It will give businesses the opportunity to explore how AI could have a real impact on their business and ensure that they the support and guidance that they need to make the right decisions for their business.  

About the Role & Team 

In this role you will be based at PrintCity our award winning additive manufacturing facility. PrintCity has over 100 additive manufacturing machines and a wide range of scanning equipment. Over £3.5M has been invested in state of the art equipment and you will join a team that has worked with over 300 industry partners in the last 5 years.  

You will be the lead in PrintCity for the Challenge AI project and will work closely with colleagues in the Centre for Enterprise in our Business school on projects with industry focused on the responsible adoption of AI solutions for companies involved in manufacturing, production and design.   

Key Responsibilities

Your key responsibilities will include: 

- Leading research and innovation projects in AI for product design,  manufacturing,  production and quality assurance for companies enrolled onto the Challenge AI programme.

- Utilising AI to implement solutions in organisations, to boost productivity,  improve efficiencies  or  enhance  quality control. 

- Supporting  colleagues with queries related to company recruitment , triage, supporting ideation workshops with technical activities related to  AI in design, manufacturing and production. 

- Working with companies on the programme to develop short or long term research and innovation programmes related to the implementation of  AI solutions, supporting skills development within companies on the programme.

Key Skills & Experiences 

You will be expected to: 

- Have the ability to lead the work of a research team, co-ordinating effort and resources. 

- Have the ability to build relationships and establish networks with internal and external contacts. Especially SMEs and large OEMs.   

- Have specialist knowledge of AI software, product design software, manufacturing processes (additive manufacturing in particular), and production operations. 

- An understanding of other industrial digital technologies and processes for example:  Industrial 3D Scanning, including software and workflows; Robotics and automation ; Machine connectivity, data extraction and custom dashboards

- Have Proficiency in programming languages (Python, PHP, MySQL, etc) and API development (RESTful,GraphQL, etc). 

To learn more about role and requirements, please read the Job Description provided below.  

If you would like to join our people and share our ambition, we would love to hear from you! 

Application & Assessment Process: 

- To apply, please submit a CV (2 page maximum) and covering letter (1 page maximum) detailing your suitability, on the application portal. 

- Please be aware that only applications including a cover letter may be considered at shortlisting stage.  

- Interviews to be held in the w/c 23 November 

- Assessment will include delivery of presentation followed by a panel interview.  

We believe in working together, sharing knowledge and valuing everyone's contributions. Develop your skills, further your knowledge and be part of a team who are transforming lives, every single day!

Senior Research Associate - (9586)

We are seeking an ambitious Senior Research Associate to join a multidisciplinary programme of research investigating Parkinson's disease, treatment response and deep brain stimulation (DBS).

The postholder will contribute to a new clinical neuroscience study involving people with Parkinson's disease undergoing assessment for and treatment with DBS. The research uses a combination of digital measures of motor function, neuroimaging and electrophysiology, including recordings of brain activity from implanted DBS systems.

Working closely with academic and NHS clinical collaborators, you will contribute to participant-facing research, acquisition and analysis of multimodal neuroscience data, and the development of biomarkers relevant to Parkinson's disease and treatment response.

ABOUT THE ROLE

You will:

contribute to the delivery and coordination of a longitudinal research study involving people with Parkinson's disease;
undertake and support research assessments and multimodal data collection;
process and analyse complex neuroscience datasets, including EEG and intracranial/depth electrophysiological recordings;
contribute to analysis of neuroimaging, digital and clinical measures;
develop robust and reproducible analytical approaches for multimodal human neuroscience data;
work closely with NHS, academic and other external collaborators;
prepare research findings for publication in high-quality peer-reviewed journals and presentation at national and international conferences;
contribute to supervision and training of students and junior researchers;
contribute to the development of future research questions and funding applications.
ABOUT YOU
You will have a PhD, or equivalent research experience, in neuroscience, psychology, biomedical engineering, neuroimaging, computational neuroscience or a related discipline, with significant experience of quantitative research.
We particularly welcome applicants with expertise in electrophysiology, neural signal processing, neuroimaging, DBS, movement disorders or multimodal neuroscience.
Previous experience across all of these areas is not required, but strong quantitative skills and experience of analysing complex biological or neural time-series data would be particularly valuable.
You will be able to work independently, use initiative in developing analytical approaches, communicate complex research clearly, and work effectively within a multidisciplinary academic and clinical team.
RESEARCH ENVIRONMENT
The successful applicant will join a growing programme of translational neuroscience and Parkinson's disease research at Manchester Metropolitan University, with strong links to NHS DBS services and academic collaborators.
The post offers an opportunity to develop expertise across human electrophysiology, deep brain stimulation, neuroimaging and digital neuroscience, while contributing to clinically relevant research in people with Parkinson's disease.

Application & Assessment

To apply, submit your CV and supporting statement outlining how best you met the criteria, via our online portal. Please note applications received without a supporting statement will not be considered.
Assessment will include a presentation and a competency-based interview round.
For informal enquiries about this vacancy, please contact Prof Nelson Trujillo Barreto on N.Trujillo.Barreto@mmu.ac.uk or Prof Nicola Ray on N.Ray@mmu.ac.uk

How to join us as a visiting scholar, academic or researcher

We welcome visiting academics, scholars and researchers 

We're a global university – we welcome visiting academics, scholars and researchers from institutions around the world.

There are many reasons to work with us at Portsmouth – from our outstanding facilities to our award-winning research.

 
How to apply

Joining us as a visiting scholar, academic or researcher takes a few simple steps.

Step 1

You need someone to propose you as a visiting scholar from your current institution. Your proposer should send your CV and a covering letter to the Dean of the relevant Faculty at the University of Portsmouth.

Your covering letter needs to explain how your research overlaps with our research priorities and existing expertise. 

If you're not currently based at a university, you'll need to supply 3 referees with your initial submission.

Step 2

After reviewing your CV and covering letter, the Dean will make a recommendation.

Step 3

If your application requires it, you may be invited to attend an interview.

Step 4

Once your application is accepted, we'll discuss your duties as a visiting member of staff. Your duties will be clearly defined and will include visiting the University for teaching activities, research work or a combination of both. There will also be a clear agreement regarding the intellectual property rights to any work you do while you're here.

Step 5

You'll need to obtain the right to work in the UK and sort out accommodation for when you arrive in Portsmouth. For more information, please visit our 'Arriving from overseas' page.

Grade 6 to 7 Researcher Promotion

The promotions processes at the University of Reading are based on the principles of fairness, equity and the recognition of the value and strength of an individual’s contribution.

This procedure outlines the promotions pathway for research staff Grade 6 to Grade 7. Research staff promotions to Grades 8 and 9 are considered under the academic staff promotion Personal Titles procedure.

All applications for promotion are considered afresh each academic year in line with the eligibility criteria detailed within this guidance.

Applicants are expected to have been employed at the University and to have held their Grade 6 Researcher position for at least 2 years and demonstrate they meet the required promotion criteria, as outlined in the Grade 6 to 7 Research Staff Promotion Procedure before applying for promotion.

In the interests of equity and consistency, the Heads of School will only consider the written evidence presented on the G6 to G7 Research Staff promotion application form and contained in the eligible additional documentation provided by candidates.

Heads of School will be accountable for decisions made. To assist them in considering cases and making decisions, Heads of School are encouraged to involve senior colleagues from within their School (such as members of their leadership team) or appropriate senior colleagues from outside the School, for example a Research Dean appropriate to the discipline or another Head of School. This may be helpful where a researcher has worked in multiple Schools during the course of their employment or where subject specific expertise may be required to help with decision making.

If you require guidance in relation to this procedure or in preparing proposals, please contact your line manager, Head of Department or relevant HR Adviser or HR Partner.

Full-Time, Fixed-Term for 5 years

The Department of Politics, International Relations and Philosophy at Royal Holloway seeks to appoint a Postdoctoral Research Fellow to work on the British Election Study. The successful applicant would be expected to start in January 2027. This is a full-time, fixed-term position for 5 years.

About the role. The successful candidate will facilitate high quality research using the British Election Study alongside Professor Oliver Heath and the BES Scientific Leadership Team. Duties will include contributing to a programme of original research using the BES; data analysis for inclusion in BES publications; public dissemination of BES research including conferences and events; data management; assisting with survey design; creating material for the BES website; supporting website maintenance; and assisting with events. The Department of Politics, International Relations and Philosophy is a research-intensive unit, ranking first in England in the Research Excellence Framework (REF) exercise. The Department provides a full range of undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral programmes to a diverse student body. We carry out research across different sub-disciplines, including but not limited to the Global Politics and Development Centre, Centre for International Security, Centre for Islamic and West Asian Studies, Democracy and Elections Centre, New Political Communication Unit and the Gender Institute.

This post is based in Egham, Surrey where the University is situated in a beautiful, leafy campus near to Windsor Great Park and within commuting distance from London.

Research Assistant

Right to work: Please note that it will not be possible for the University to issue a Certificate of Sponsorship to the successful candidate for this position. Therefore, the appointable candidate will need to be eligible to work in the UK or have leave to remain in the UK and associated right to work for the duration of their employment with the University, in accordance with the Immigration, Asylum and Nationality Act 2006.

Full-Time, Fixed-Term (until 21 September 2028)

We are pleased to invite applications for a Research Assistant on the Doctorate in Clinical Psychology to undertake research, audit and administration related to Clinical Psychology Course innovation and expansion. In the past 5 years significant expansion and change has occurred nationally in the field of clinical psychology training which requires evaluation to improve training delivery and develop the evidence base for effective clinical competence development in online and off-line training delivery. 

The post holder will co-design and conduct research evaluations and audits to support the development of clinical training innovations related to; clinician recruitment, clinical supervision, curriculum design, teaching delivery, assessment of clinical, academic and research competences, diversity and inclusion. There are a number of innovative projects related to digital practice and equality, diversity and inclusion which the research assistant will support.

The post holder will be required (under supervision) to; undertake the design and running of research and evaluations, set up stakeholder meetings, organise participant recruitment, recording and analysing data, searching relevant literature, writing up results, drafting papers and posters and organising dissemination events. 

This post is well established within the DClinPsy and would suit an organised individual, with initiative, who can work independently, managing their time effectively between a variety of projects. The post requires excellent communication skills and ability to work as part of a team. Applicants must hold a degree in Psychology, alongside and interest and competence in basic qualitative and quantitative research methods.

In 2026 the RHUL DClinPsy Programme had 60 commissioned places per cohort through its training contract with the Department of Health and Social Care. This is a really exciting time for clinical psychology, with substantial expansion and innovation in line with NHS priorities and professional body accreditation criteria. The RHUL DClinPsy is a large well-respected training programme with an existing BABCP CBT pathway and a Systemic pathway. The post-holder will join an innovative and supportive team of 20 clinical-academic staff with a range of expertise across child, adult, learning disability, health, older-adult and neuropsychology specialities. 

The course sits within a vibrant Psychology Department, internationally recognised for world-class research and teaching with strong ratings for research (REF) and for teaching (UK NSS). The Department has excellent facilities, including MRI, EEG, TMS, eye trackers, behavioural testing suites, and social and infant observation labs, as well as strong links with clinical organisations, government, industry, and charity affiliations. We are proud of our atmosphere of strong collegiality in the department, and we are highly committed to principles of equity and diversity. 

This full-time post is offered on a fixed term contract until 21 September 2028. We offer a highly competitive rewards and benefits package with generous annual leave and staff development opportunities.

Research Fellow A in Computational Linguistics
The role

We are seeking qualified applicants for up to a 2 year position (with possibility to extend to 4) as Research Fellow (postdoc) in Computational Linguistics on the UKRI FLF grant ‘Scaling predictability in Morphological paradigms’, led by Sacha Beniamine. The successful candidate will perform a key role in creating new software tools and employing them to measure predictability in morphology. The position is based at the Surrey Morphology Group at the University of Surrey, in Guildford, and provides the opportunity to work in the vibrant and highly collegial research environment for which the SMG is renowned.

The successful candidate will be in charge of the Work Package focusing on New Models, which aims to enable precise and comparable measures of morphological predictability, in order to understand how predictability is organized in realistic, complex inflectional systems. 

As a core member of the team, the successful candidate will use their skills in software development to extend existing software (Qumin) which analyzes morphological lexical data and evaluates inflectional predictability. They will rely on their qualifications in linguistics to study predictability in systems which challenge existing tools and analyses, pushing the edge of what can be reliably measured and contribute to the large comparative study of macro-variation in predictability, gaining experience in linguistic typology. They will collaborate closely with the team in the writing and dissemination of papers and presentations, and be expected to take initiative in the formulation of the research agenda.

About you

The successful candidate will have a dual background in linguistics and software development, with a PhD in computational linguistics, natural language processing, or a related field. The candidate will have a good grasp of linguistic concepts and methods. They will have an interest in the inflectional morphology of at least one language or language family, which can serve as a test-bed for the tools they will develop. They will have experience of software development, and are fluent in Python programming. Candidates with experience programming as part of a team will be preferred.  Mastery over software development tools (command line; git management; continuous pipelines and workflows; IDE) is essential. An interest in reproducibility in science will be an advantage. Experience in using these skills to answer linguistic questions is essential.

About the role

An exciting opportunity is available for a Postdoctoral Research Fellow to join the School of Psychology at the University of Sussex and contribute to cutting-edge research on the neural basis of misophonia. This full-time position is available from January 2027 and will run until 30 September 2028.

Misophonia is a poorly understood condition in which specific everyday sounds, such as chewing, breathing, or tapping, trigger intense emotional and physiological reactions that can profoundly affect quality of life. This project aims to transform our understanding of misophonia by revealing how the brain processes and represents the acoustic and semantic properties of sounds, and how these neural representations differ between individuals with and without the condition.

Working as part of a world-leading research team studying anomalous perceptual experiences, you will contribute to a project funded by the Ream Foundation that combines cognitive neuroscience and advanced neuroimaging methods. The successful candidate will contribute independently to all stages of the project, publish high-quality research, and advance understanding of an important but underexplored condition.

About you

You will hold a PhD in cognitive neuroscience, psychology, audiology, or a related discipline, with expertise in sensory perception (e.g. hearing or vision), attention, or a closely related area. You will have experience in the acquisition and analysis of EEG data and a strong interest in understanding the neural mechanisms that give rise to perceptual experience.

The ideal candidate will be a motivated and collaborative researcher capable of working independently. You will be excited by the opportunity to contribute to an emerging field, work as part of an internationally recognised research team, and help advance our understanding of the cognitive and neural mechanisms underlying misophonia.

About our Faculty

Our Psychology school has a rich history extending over half-a-century, marked from the start by our variety of research and courses. From the ground-breaking work of scholars such as Stuart Sutherland and Marie Jahoda, we've grown to cover all areas of psychology.

The School was formally established in 2009, bringing together academics across biological, cognitive, developmental, clinical and social psychology into one School. We've now entered the second decade of our existence as one of the largest and most influential academic communities for psychology in the country!

Anchored by our core values of kindness, integrity, inclusion, collaboration and courage, our research and teaching address societal challenges to create a better world.

About the role

Applications are invited for a 12 months full-time postdoctoral position (with the possibility for extension) in Experimental Quantum Technology at the University of Sussex. Applicants should have obtained a PhD in experimental quantum information, laser- or atomic physics and be able to demonstrate working experience in this field. The appointment is within the framework of the EPSRC Quantum Technology Hub: Quantum Computing via Integrated and Interconnected Implementations. The successful candidate will work in a team of experienced researchers led by Prof Matthias Keller.

The aim of the project is to combine two of the most successful techniques in quantum information processing, trapped ions and photons, and use them to create a distributed quantum network. The main challenge is the implementation of an efficient ion-photon interface based on strongly-coupled cavity-QED. 

We have developed a multi-zone ion trap that incorporates zones for loading, quantum information processing, and a cavity-based ion-photon interface. The first part of the project is to test and characterise the ion trap system and implement a highly efficient ion-photon interface. This involves the setting up and testing of the system as well as simulating and implementing novel schemes for ion-photon entanglement. 

Based on successful testing of the multi-zone trap, a second system will be established to implement a basic quantum network.

About you

Ideally, you will have a PhD in experimental quantum information, laser- or atomic physics and be able to demonstrate working experience in this field.

The project requires working with a complex optical system with diode lasers, ultra-high vacuum systems, and control electronics to operate the experiment. Having experience and a good understanding of such systems is highly beneficial.

About the role

We are seeking an ambitious and creative Postdoctoral Research Associate to join the Vasiljeva Lab and investigate how phosphorylation regulates RNA polymerase II (Pol II) transcription, RNA processing and gene expression.

Our research addresses a fundamental question in molecular biology: how does RNA polymerase II coordinate transcription with the processing and maturation of newly synthesised RNA to ensure accurate gene expression? We are particularly interested in how reversible phosphorylation of transcription and RNA-processing factors acts as a regulatory mechanism to connect these processes.

The project will form part of a multidimensional research programme combining biochemistry, structural biology, cell biology, functional genomics and large-scale genetic approaches. Depending on your interests and expertise, you will have the opportunity to develop and combine complementary experimental approaches to address molecular mechanisms from the level of individual protein interactions through to genome-wide regulation.

You will join a collaborative and intellectually stimulating research environment where we aim to understand how transcriptional regulation is integrated with RNA processing and genome function. The position offers considerable scope to develop your own ideas and expertise while contributing to a broader programme of research.

Our research

The Vasiljeva Lab investigates the mechanisms that coordinate transcription, RNA processing and RNA surveillance. Our recent work has revealed new mechanisms by which transcription factors and RNA-processing machineries communicate through regulated phosphorylation and protein–RNA interactions.

Recent publications from the lab include:

Ho, A., Southers, A., Kus, K., Schoemaker, N., Fournier, M., Audin, E., Kilchert, C., Grimes, J., and Vasiljeva, L. (2026) WDR82 Code Coordinates Transcription and pre-mRNA 3′-End Processing Through Regulated Phosphorylation. Nature Communications https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-77611-z

Kus, K., Carrique, L., Fournier, M., Audin, E., Kilchert, C., Grimes, J., and Vasiljeva, L. (2025) The role of DSIF factor Spt5 in coordinating Pol II processivity and Xrn2 exoribonucleolysis for timely termination of transcription. Nature Commun 16(1):10. doi: 10.1038/s41467-024-55063-7.

Slade, L., Kus, K., Filipovic, M., Sarkies, P. and Vasiljeva, L. (2026) The Intergator complex couples Non-coding RNA biogenesis, mitochondrial function and innate immunity to control life and health span. BioRxiv, doi: https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.04.18.719358 (in review)

Kus, K., Nielsen, S., Zenkin and Vasiljeva L. (2025) Conserved Pol II and RNA interacting protein is an anti-pausing transcription elongation factor. RNA. Oct 24:rna.080765.125. doi:10.1261/rna.080765.125

Heo, D.H., Kus, K., Grzechnik, P., Tan-Wong, S.M., Birot, A., Nielsen, S., Zenkin, N., and Vasiljeva L. (2021) Transcription and chromatin-based surveillance mechanism controls suppression of cryptic transcription. Cell Reports 36, 7, 10967.

Kecman, T., Kus, K., Heo, D. H., Birot, A., Mohamed, S., Geiss-Astggiante, L., Robinson C., and Vasiljeva, L. (2018) Elongation to termination factors exchange mediated by PP1 phosphatase orchestrate RNA polymerase II transcription termination. Cell Reports, 25(1):259-269.

Responsibilities

Manage own academic research and administrative activities. This involves small scale project management, to co-ordinate multiple aspects of work to meet deadlines.

Undertaking RNA analysis, ChIP, TT-seq, and bioinformatic analysis of the data

Maintaining mammalian cell culture and generating degron-tagged cell lines.

Adapt existing and develop new scientific techniques and experimental protocols.

Test hypotheses and analyse scientific data from a variety of sources, reviewing and refining working hypotheses as appropriate.

Develop ideas for driving project forward and Collaborate in the preparation of scientific reports and journal articles and occasionally present papers and posters.

Use specialist scientific equipment in a laboratory environment.

Act as a source of information and advice to other members of the group on scientific protocols and experimental techniques.

Represent the research group at external meetings/seminars, either with other members of the group or alone

Carry out collaborative projects with colleagues in partner institutions, and research groups

Embed the principles of mutual respect, equality, diversity, inclusivity and sustainability in all aspects of your work; undertake training as and when asked to do so.

About you

We are looking for a highly motivated researcher with a PhD in molecular biology, biochemistry, cell biology, genetics, genomics or a related discipline.

You may have expertise in one or more of the following areas:

RNA polymerase II transcription and transcriptional regulation
RNA processing, RNA surveillance or RNA metabolism
Protein phosphorylation and post-translational regulation
Molecular or cellular biology
Biochemistry and protein–RNA/protein–protein interactions
Functional genomics, genetics or genome-wide approaches
Structural biology or quantitative proteomics

We particularly welcome applicants who are excited by interdisciplinary research and interested in learning new approaches. Experience in every technique is not required. What matters most is scientific curiosity, experimental creativity and the ability to tackle challenging biological questions.

You will be expected to design and conduct experiments, analyse and interpret data, contribute to publications and presentations, and work collaboratively within the research team. You will also have opportunities to develop your own scientific ideas and build the skills needed for your future independent research career.

Why join us?

This is an opportunity to work at the interface of transcription, RNA biology and gene regulation, addressing fundamental questions using a combination of molecular, cellular and genome-wide approaches.

You will benefit from:

a strong and internationally visible research programme in transcription and RNA biology;
access to a broad range of biochemical, genomic and cellular approaches;
a collaborative environment spanning molecular mechanisms to genome-wide regulation;
opportunities to develop new technical expertise and independent research ideas;
close interaction with researchers working across transcription, RNA processing, chromatin and genome regulation;
an environment that values collaboration, scientific creativity and rigorous mechanistic research.

If you are excited by understanding how molecular events at RNA polymerase II are translated into accurate and dynamic patterns of gene expression, we would be delighted to hear from you.

In the School of Life Sciences we strive to understand the mechanisms that drive biological and chemical processes and to develop innovative and diverse approaches to enhance human health, technology and the environment. We undertake multidisciplinary research, teaching and engagement across a wide range of subjects, from Chemistry through Cellular and Molecular Biosciences to Conservation Biology. 

The School comprises five Departments: Biochemistry & Biomedicine, Genome Damage and Stability Centre, Neuroscience, Ecology & Evolution and Chemistry. We also house the Sussex Drug Discovery Centre which works to deliver the bench-to-bedside translation of our discoveries. The breadth and depth of our cutting-edge research and innovative teaching practice is delivered by a diverse community who work across boundaries to deliver excellence, engage with real world problems and produce impact. 

We pride ourselves on our world-leading research and have a strong research economy, with approximately 50% of our income stemming from research and an active grant portfolio of over £50 million. We host or form part of three University Centres of Excellence: the Genome Damage and Stability Centre, Sussex Neuroscience and Sussex Sustainability Research Programme. In the 2021 Research Excellence Framework, 90.6 % of our Biological Sciences outputs and 84.8% of our Chemistry outputs were rated as world-leading or internationally excellent. The School is committed to the University’s core values of kindness, integrity, inclusion, collaboration and courage. How the molecular biology of neurons relates to the development and function of neural circuits is an open question in modern neuroscience. The new Research Fellow will investigate this important problem using the latest technology in the field.

You will become a core member of the Alonso lab (https://www.sussex.ac.uk/lifesci/alonsolab/) interacting closely with other group members, and our UK and international collaborators. Together, we will apply the latest methodologies, including molecular biology, transcriptomics, neurogenetics, optogenetics, optical neuronal imaging, neurophysiology, microscopy and quantitative behavioural approaches to gain mechanistic understanding of the molecular underpinnings of neuronal development and physiology.  

Our lab is part of the Neuroscience Department (https://www.sussex.ac.uk/schools/life-sciences/research/neuroscience) which houses a cluster of leading labs investigating neural function in vertebrates and invertebrates, and an active member of Sussex Neuroscience (http://www.sussex.ac.uk/sussexneuroscience/) a university Centre of Excellence, that brings together a large, vibrant and interdisciplinary community of world-class neuroscientists providing an excellent collaborative setting for our research.

About you

The successful candidate will have a degree in Biology, Neuroscience or related disciplines, and be educated to doctoral level. They will have a solid background in Neurobiology, Neurodevelopment or Behaviour, and, familiarity with Drosophila genetics and behaviour. They will show evidence of engagement in high-quality research activity, have excellent communication and organisational skills, be able to set priorities and meet deadlines, and be capable to work independently – on own initiative, without close supervision – and as a team player supporting other colleagues. 

About our School

In the School of Life Sciences we strive to understand the mechanisms that drive biological and chemical processes and to develop innovative and diverse approaches to enhance human health, technology and the environment. We undertake multidisciplinary research, teaching and engagement across a wide range of subjects, from Chemistry through Cellular and Molecular Biosciences to Conservation Biology. 

The School comprises five Departments: Biochemistry & Biomedicine, Genome Damage and Stability Centre, Neuroscience, Ecology & Evolution and Chemistry. We also house the Sussex Drug Discovery Centre which works to deliver the bench-to-bedside translation of our discoveries. The breadth and depth of our cutting-edge research and innovative teaching practice is delivered by a diverse community who work across boundaries to deliver excellence, engage with real world problems and produce impact. 

We pride ourselves on our world-leading research and have a strong research economy, with approximately 50% of our income stemming from research and an active grant portfolio of over £50 million. We host or form part of three University Centres of Excellence: the Genome Damage and Stability Centre, Sussex Neuroscience and Sussex Sustainability Research Programme. In the 2021 Research Excellence Framework, 90.6 % of our Biological Sciences outputs and 84.8% of our Chemistry outputs were rated as world-leading or internationally excellent. We are proud that in both areas, 100% of our Impact cases were rated as world-leading or internationally excellent.

The School is committed to the University’s core values of kindness, integrity, inclusion, collaboration and courage. We believe that equality, diversity and inclusion is everyone’s responsibility and aim to provide a friendly and supportive environment for all who work, study and visit the School of Life Sciences. 

Please find further information regarding the School of Life Sciences on our website.

The School of Life Sciences is proud to hold a Silver Athena Swan Award. 

Why work here

Our university is situated off the A27, next to the beautiful South Downs where you will enjoy everything that our 150-acre campus has to offer. We are accessible by public transport; Falmer train station is a five-minute walk to campus and several bus stops are located within campus. We also have dedicated cycling paths and encourage our staff to use these with our offering of a cycle to work scheme.  

Sussex is a renowned, multi-accredited, research-led International University and this is only possible because of the people that work here. Whether you are a member of Faculty, part of a Professional Services team or a Student, it’s our people that make us great and we want you to be part of that. 

Find out more about our reward and benefits package. 

Find out about our equality, diversity and inclusion.

Please contact Professor Claudio R. Alonso at c.alonso@sussex.ac.uk for informal enquiries.

For full details and how to apply see our vacancies page.

The University is committed to equality and valuing diversity, and applications are particularly welcomed from women and black and minority ethnic candidates, who are under-represented in academic posts in Science, Technology, Engineering, Medicine and Mathematics (STEMM) at Sussex. 

Eligibility

This role may be eligible for sponsorship under the Skilled Worker route. Our Research
 
Research with us
 
Postgraduate Research 
 
Postgraduate Researcher Development 
POSTGRADUATE RESEARCHER DEVELOPMENT

We offer a comprehensive researcher development programme for postgraduate researchers (PGRs), supporting them to develop the skills, knowledge and attributes to excel in their research and future careers, whether within or beyond academia.

Our researcher development programme encompasses training workshops delivered by internal and external experts, immersive opportunities that allow PGRs to apply and reflect on their skills, as well as online resources accessed on demand, as often as you like. The programme is underpinned by the Vitae Researcher Development Framework, designed to support our PGRs' research and professional development at every stage of their studies.

PGR Researcher Development and the Vitae RDF

Our programme is now mapped to the Vitae Researcher Development Framework (RDF), revised in 2025, to help you as researchers plan, prioritise and track your own development.

The RDF sets out the knowledge, skills and behaviours of effective researchers at all career stages, recognising the contribution of researchers to society, economic and environmental change both within and beyond higher education. It is created by Vitae, a leader in researcher development, with input from researchers and practitioners across a range of career stages and sectors.

Our approach to PGR development

Development and training doesn’t begin and end with attending a workshop, or reading a particular resource. We encourage our research students to view their entire degree as a continual, holistic programme of development in which they are learning to be researchers in their chosen field, developing the skills needed to complete their research project and write their thesis, as well as developing a range of transferable professional and personal attributes that will be of use in whatever they decide to do next. Doing this means taking advantage of all the opportunities on offer, whether formal workshops and events or the informal reflections and learning that come from conversations in the lab or over coffee, and everything in between.

Current PGR student or supervisor? Find out more here.

ABOUT THE UNIVERSITY

Swansea University is a research-led university that has been making a difference since 1920. The University community thrives on exploration and discovery and offers the right balance of excellent teaching and research, matched by an enviable quality of life.

Our stunning waterfront campuses and multicultural community make us a desirable workplace for colleagues from around the world. Our reward and benefits, and ways of working enable those who join us to have enriching careers, matched by an excellent work-life balance.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Department of Physics at Swansea University is seeking to appoint a Postdoctoral Research Associate (PDRA) in Semiconductor Physics and Terahertz Science and Technology.

The successful candidate will join a thriving research effort in semiconductor science at Swansea University’s new state-of-the-art Centre for Integrative Semiconductor Materials (CISM) and will contribute significantly to the EPSRC programme grant "Terahertz frequency devices and systems for ultrahigh capacity wireless communications (TERACOM)" (teracom.uk), EP/W028921/1. This is a collaborative project involving the Universities of Swansea, Leeds, and University College London.

The successful candidate will join a team of researchers aiming to realise next-generation communication systems operating in the terahertz range and participate in inter-site collaborations as well as regular meetings of the consortium that provide networking opportunities. As a research-focused University embedded in the South Wales Compound Semiconductor Cluster, Swansea provides excellent opportunities for applied research, semiconductor technology development, and industrial collaborations.

As the selected PDRA, you will be simulating, designing and developing terahertz devices that rely on novel physical phenomena to achieve unprecedented performance in terahertz modulation and detection. You will be fabricating the samples (field-effect transistor type terahertz devices with a focus on the gallium nitride material system) in the CISM cleanroom. You will be characterising the new devices on existing setups as well as expanding and building new experimental systems for their measurements with terahertz sources. You will present the results on regular project meetings, write up the research outcomes and publish them in international peer-reviewed journals.

EQUALITY, DIVERSITY & INCLUSION

The University is committed to supporting and promoting equality and diversity in all its practices and activities. We aim to establish an inclusive environment and welcome diverse applications from the following protected characteristics: age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race (including colour, nationality, ethnic and national origin), religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation.

As an inclusive and welcoming workplace, we value people for their skills regardless of their background. Applications are welcome in Welsh and will not be treated less favourably than those submitted in English.

WELSH LANGUAGE SKILLS

The Welsh language level required for this role is Level 1 - A little. The role holder will be able to pronounce Welsh words, answer the phone in Welsh (good morning/afternoon) and use very basic everyday words and phrases (thank you, please etc.). Level 1 can be reached by completing a 1 hour course.

The University is a proud bilingual institution, our Welsh Language Strategy outlines our aspiration to promote the language and enable our staff to engage with the language as an additional workplace skill and as a gateway to new cultural and social opportunities. Applications are welcome in Welsh and will not be treated less favourably than those submitted in English. Welsh speakers have the right to an interview in Welsh. Applicants for a role where Welsh skills are essential are expected to present their application in Welsh and will be interviewed in Welsh, if shortlisted.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

Applications for this role will take the format of a CV submission and cover letter.

Appointment at research associate level (grade 8) is dependent on having a PhD and relevant experience. A candidate who has submitted but has not yet received their PhD will be appointed at research assistant level (grade 7).

ABOUT THE UNIVERSITY

Swansea University is a research-led university that has been making a difference since 1920. The University community thrives on exploration and discovery and offers the right balance of excellent teaching and research, matched by an enviable quality of life.

Our stunning waterfront campuses and multicultural community make us a desirable workplace for colleagues from around the world. Our reward and benefits, and ways of working enable those who join us to have enriching careers, matched by an excellent work-life balance.

ABOUT THE ROLE

This is a part-time post of 7 hours per week (0.2 FTE), offered on a fixed-term basis for an initial period of 12 months.

The postholder will contribute to an established research programme, recruiting participants and supporting the collection and analysis of data and samples.

Working under the direction of the Principal Investigator, you will recruit study participants and undertake data and sample collection and sample analysis.

You will be responsible for data entry, data polishing and data analysis, and will contribute to the conduct of research, gathering and preparing data, generating original ideas and presenting results.

You will prepare reports and draft papers describing research results, and will interact professionally with collaborators within the Faculty, across the University and in third-sector organisations.

Applicants must hold a degree in public health or a related subject, be fluent in Farsi, and have experience of quantitative research and working or volunteering with sanctuary-seeking communities.

EQUALITY, DIVERSITY & INCLUSION

The University is committed to supporting and promoting equality and diversity in all its practices and activities. We aim to establish an inclusive environment and welcome diverse applications from the following protected characteristics: age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race (including colour, nationality, ethnic and national origin), religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation.

As an inclusive and welcoming workplace, we value people for their skills regardless of their background. Applications are welcome in Welsh and will not be treated less favourably than those submitted in English.

WELSH LANGUAGE SKILLS

The Welsh language level required for this role is Level 1 - A little. The role holder will be able to pronounce Welsh words, answer the phone in Welsh (good morning/afternoon) and use very basic everyday words and phrases (thank you, please etc.). Level 1 can be reached by completing a 1 hour course.

The University is a proud bilingual institution, our Welsh Language Strategy outlines our aspiration to promote the language and enable our staff to engage with the language as an additional workplace skill and as a gateway to new cultural and social opportunities. Applications are welcome in Welsh and will not be treated less favourably than those submitted in English. Welsh speakers have the right to an interview in Welsh. Applicants for a role where Welsh skills are essential are expected to present their application in Welsh and will be interviewed in Welsh, if shortlisted.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

Applications for this role will take the format of a CV submission and cover letter.

A satisfactory DBS certificate must be provided before a start date can be confirmed

ABOUT THE UNIVERSITY

Swansea University is a research-led university that has been making a difference since 1920. The University community thrives on exploration and discovery and offers the right balance of excellent teaching and research, matched by an enviable quality of life.

Our stunning waterfront campuses and multicultural community make us a desirable workplace for colleagues from around the world. Our reward and benefits, and ways of working enable those who join us to have enriching careers, matched by an excellent work-life balance.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Swansea University is seeking to appoint a Postdoctoral Research Associate to contribute to the European Horizon Europe project READY-PV – Reliability Evaluation Through Analytics and Data for Emerging Technology in Photovoltaics.

READY-PV is a pan-European research infrastructure project designed to accelerate the development of reliable and durable emerging photovoltaic (PV) technologies. The project brings together research infrastructures across Europe and beyond to provide access to advanced facilities for indoor and outdoor ageing, PV performance assessment, materials characterisation, degradation analysis and data-driven modelling.

The successful candidate will contribute to Swansea University’s role within the project, with particular responsibility for supporting indoor and outdoor photovoltaic reliability testing and the provision of research infrastructure access to external users. The role will involve experimental work on emerging PV technologies, including perovskite and organic photovoltaic devices, as well as the collection, analysis and interpretation of performance and environmental data.

The postdoctoral researcher will contribute to the delivery of the READY-PV project at Swansea University, with a particular focus on providing Transnational Access to Swansea’s photovoltaic testing and reliability facilities. The role will involve supporting indoor and outdoor performance, durability and degradation testing of emerging PV devices and modules, monitoring their performance under extended exposure and assessing relationships with environmental conditions. The researcher will also contribute to encapsulation and lamination activities, the design and maintenance of outdoor testing facilities, and the implementation of harmonised experimental procedures and reliability protocols. They will support external READY-PV users in planning and conducting experiments at Swansea, including experimental setup, measurements, data collection and initial analysis, while contributing to project meetings, training, workshops and dissemination activities. The role will also involve preparing technical reports, research papers and presentations, and working collaboratively with academic, research infrastructure and industrial partners across the READY-PV consortium.

Job description

Role:  Research Associate - InflamAb Project

Department: School of Medicine

Grade: 6/7 (£33,680 per annum)

Responsible to: Principal Investigator

Campus: Derry~Londonderry

Fixed-Term until 31st August 2027 / Full-time 

Job Purpose:

The post holder will support the preclinical development of InflamAb, a novel therapeutic candidate for inflammatory disease, through the design and delivery of experimental studies to investigate its biological activity, mechanism of action and potential therapeutic efficacy.

The role will generate robust evidence to establish how InflamAb modulates inflammatory pathways and inform its progression towards further preclinical development, while supporting commercialisation activities and the translation of research into potential therapeutic applications.

The work will contribute to the University’s research objectives, scientific outputs and wider impact through the development and exploitation of innovative approaches to inflammatory disease.

This role is funded by an Invest Northern Ireland Proof of Concept Award.

Closing Date: 9th November 2026 at 23.30

Guidance regarding applications can be found here:   https://recruitment.ulster.ac.uk/information-for-applicants/what-to-expect-from-the-application-and-interview-process. If you are still having issues, please contact Suzanne McFarlane on sj.mcfarlane@ulster.ac.uk stating the vacancy reference number.

Click on the links below for any relevant documents – Please note, these documents will not be available after the job advert closes. Please ensure that you download and save these.

Candidate Briefing Document - 044226

Salary Scale

Please be advised that due to the minimum salary thresholds imposed by the UKVI, this post will not qualify for university sponsorship under the Skilled Worker visa route. Please check your options here:  https://www.gov.uk/check-uk-visa

If you have any specific queries regarding eligibility to work in the UK, the Resourcing Compliance team may be able to assist: Resourcing-compliance@ulster.ac.uk

Role:  Research Associate in Diabetes

Department: School of Biomedical Sciences

Grade: 6/7 (£33,680 - £36,341 per annum)

Responsible to: Principal Investigator

Campus: Coleraine

Fixed-Term until 1st May 2028 / Full-time 

Job Purpose:

The worldwide increase in obesity and type 2 diabetes highlights the urgent need to develop safe and effective new therapies that can improve disease management and limit the progression of long-term diabetic complications.

The post holder will contribute to research investigating the potential of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) as novel therapeutic targets for diabetes. The role will focus on advancing the scientific understanding of GPCR-based therapies and evaluating their therapeutic potential as a promising class of treatment for obesity and type 2 diabetes.

The purpose of this role is to actively advance the Diabetes Research Centre's metabolic disease research portfolio by generating new insights into the commercialisation potential of GPCR-targeted therapeutics while improving understanding of their therapeutic efficacy through precision pharmacology. The project aims to accelerate small-molecule drug discovery by identifying and validating promising lead candidates while aligning the discovery process with key value-generation milestones.

This post offers an exciting opportunity to work within a dynamic and collaborative research environment, gaining experience in one of the fastest-moving areas of biomedical research. The successful candidate will develop expertise in both cutting-edge scientific research and the commercialisation of innovative therapeutic approaches.

We are seeking a passionate researcher with an interest in improving the health and wellbeing of people living with a stoma. The postholder will conduct an observational study examining the health outcomes of people living with a stoma, contributing to the generation of high-quality evidence to inform future care and support.

About The Post
This post is part-time, 14 hours per week and fixed-term until 28  September 2028. The salary stated above is the pro-rata amount, the full-time salary would be £41,086 - £46,542 per annum (Incl. LWA).
 

The University of Westminster is seeking to appoint an innovative Research Associate to join the School of Social Sciences (0.4 FTE basis) on the Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC) funded project, Centring Mothers’ Voices in the Prevention of Gangs and Serious Youth Violence. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to a pioneering and impactful research project that places mothers at the heart of efforts to prevent gangs and serious youth violence.

The project recognises the crucial role mothers play as protectors, advocates and sources of support within their families and communities. Working closely with Dr Sally Atkinson-Sheppard, the successful candidate will contribute to a participatory and co-produced programme of research that brings together mothers, practitioners and other stakeholders to develop new knowledge and influence policy and practice.

The role will involve undertaking a literature review and policy analysis, conducting qualitative photovoice interviews with mothers and practitioners, supporting data collection and analysis, and contributing to research outputs including reports, policy briefings and academic publications. The successful candidate will also play an important role in impact and dissemination activities, including supporting and managing a steering group of mothers and contributing to the development of resources designed to influence policy and practice.

The successful candidate will have experience of conducting research with vulnerable groups, strong qualitative research skills, excellent written and verbal communication abilities, and a commitment to collaborative and inclusive research practices. They will be able to work effectively as part of a research team while managing their own workload and contributing positively to the wider academic community..

Researcher Development Concordat

The University is fully committed to meeting the principles of the Concordat to support the Career Development of Researchers and thus to supporting its researchers at all stages of their careers. This Concordat is an agreement between stakeholders to improve the employment and support for researchers and researcher careers in higher education in the UK. It sets out three clear principles of environment and culture, employment, and professional and career development. The principles are underpinned by obligations for the four key stakeholder groups, funders, institutions, researchers, and managers of researchers, to realise the aims of the concordat. The secretariat responsibility for the concordat is held by Universities UK. Further details and resources to support implementation can be found on the Research Development Concordat webpages.

 The University’s commitment to the Concordat is reflected in two ways:       

Through our formal institutional commitment to the Concordat
Through our HR Excellence in Research (HREIR) Award
Institutional Commitment

The University made its formal commitment to the Concordat on 7th February 2023. In so doing, the University has committed to: conduct a gap analysis; produce an action plan to identify the steps to meet the concordat’s obligations; publish an action plan publicly within a year of signing the concordat; and produce an annual report in each subsequent year to report on progress implementing their action plan.

Annual Report for the Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers 2024 
Annual Report for the Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers 2025

HR Excellence in Research

In June 2016, the University of Worcester was awarded the European Commission's HR Excellence in Research Award. The award recognises our progress towards providing a high-quality research environment for research staff and postgraduate researchers at the University. In order to gain the award, we engaged in an analysis of our practice against the principles set out in the Concordat to support the Career Development of Researchers and developed an action plan to address gaps that emerged in this analysis.

As part of the required review process for the Award, at the 2-year stage, the University completed a self-assessment of its original action plan (2016-18), wrote an overarching progress report, and produced a new action plan that built on and extended the initial one (2018-20):

Updated Concordat Action Plan 2016-2018
Two-Year Internal Evaluation Report for HR Excellence in Research Award – May 2018   
Concordat Action Plan 2018-2020

The award was renewed in June 2018.

Subsequently, at the 4-year stage, the University was subject to external review of its 2018-20 action plan and a new action plan for 2021-23 based on an updated Researcher Development Concordat:    

Updated Concordat Action Plan 2018-2020
Four-Year Evaluation report for HR Excellence in Research Award

The award was renewed in April 2022.

The award was renewed in March 2024.

UKRI FUTURE LEADERS’ FELLOWSHIPS (Round 11) 

UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) has announced round 11 of this scheme with a deadline for submission on 16 June 2026.

The Future Leaders Fellowship Scheme is a scheme that supports early career researchers in any subject area, with outstanding potential, to tackle challenging research questions and develop their own careers.  Funding is available for up to seven years allowing long term flexible funding to support adventurous and ambitious programmes. There are no eligibility rules based on years since PhD or whether the applicant currently holds an open-ended academic position. The Fellowship will provide salary support, allowing successful applicants protected time to concentrate fully on their research (up to six hours per week may be spent on other commitments or related activities, provided they enhance career development).

The UKRI’s Scheme Guidance for Future Leaders Fellowships can be found here. Further information can be found on the UKRI's website.

Worcester can submit two applications to this call. We will therefore be inviting Expressions of Interest from eligible internal and external researchers and will run a selection process to select the two applications to be put forward.

We welcome Expressions of Interest from current employees or from researchers outside of the University. Researchers from outside of the University who are not current employees of the University will only receive an offer of employment from the University if researcher’s application to UKRI’s Future Leaders Fellowship Scheme is successful.

If you are interested in submitting an Expression of Interest (EoI), please get in touch to explore further by contacting Charlotte Wasilewski in the Research, Innovation & Impact Office researchoffice@worc.ac.uk.

We will be running information sessions for potential applicants on the following dates:

25 February 2026 at 11.00am on MS Teams
4 March 2026 at 1.00pm on MS Teams    

These session can be booked on iTrent for existing staff. For external candidates, please contact researcherdevelopment@worc.ac.uk.

The London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) is one of the world’s leading public health universities. Our mission is to improve health and health equity in the UK and worldwide; working in partnership to achieve excellence in public and global health research, education and translation of knowledge into policy and practice.

LSHTM is seeking to appoint a Trial Manager within the Clinical Research Department. The post-holder will be responsible for the day-to-day operational management of ADVANCING-CM, a multi-site phase IIb into phase III randomised clinical trial of adjunctive interferon gamma for HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis in Botswana, Malawi, South Africa and Uganda. They will work closely with the International Lead Clinician, the experienced senior trial management team and study coordinators at the participating African study sites. The post-holder will be expected to be based full-time at the Trial Coordinating Centre in Gaborone, Botswana for the duration of study recruitment and to travel frequently to the other trial sites. The role will provide operational leadership across trial set-up, regulatory and ethics processes, site initiation and monitoring, trial documentation, data quality, safety-reporting systems and trial governance, ensuring that the study is conducted in accordance with the protocol, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), applicable regulatory requirements and trial procedures.

The successful candidate will have a postgraduate degree, ideally a doctoral degree, in a relevant topic, relevant experience of working on multicentre phase III clinical trials, including Clinical Trials of Investigational Medicinal Products (CTIMPs), experience of trial set-up and site initiation, including preparation and maintenance of essential trial documentation, experience of clinical trial monitoring, including identification and follow-up of monitoring findings and protocol deviations. Further particulars are available in the job description.

The post is full-time 35 hours per week, 1.0 FTE and fixed term until 31 December 2030. The post is funded by Coefficient Giving and is available from 01 January 2027.

The salary will be on the LSHTM salary scale, Grade 6 in the range £46,643 - £52,909 per annum pro rata (inclusive of London Weighting). The post will be subject to the LSHTM terms and conditions of service.  Annual leave entitlement is 30 working days per year, pro rata for part time staff. In addition to this there are discretionary “Wellbeing Days”. Membership of the Pension Scheme is available. This post is based in Botswana, hosted by the Botswana Harvard Health Partnership Institute in Gaborone with frequent travels to sites in Malawi, Uganda and South Africa. 

Applications should be made on-line via our jobs website. Online applications will be accepted by the automated system until 10pm of the closing date. Any queries regarding the application process may be addressed to jobs@lshtm.ac.uk. Please quote reference ITD-CRD-2026-25.

The supporting statement section should set out how your qualifications, experience and training meet each of the selection criteria. Please provide one or more paragraphs addressing each criterion. The supporting statement is an essential part of the selection process and thus a failure to provide this information will mean that the application will not be considered. An answer to any of the criteria such as "Please see attached CV" will not be considered acceptable. 

Please note that if you are shortlisted and are unable to attend on the interview date it may not be possible to offer you an alternative date.

LSTM malaria researcher Professor Feiko ter Kuile wins George Macdonald Medal
News

16 October 2026

Press Contact

LSTM malaria researcher Professor Feiko ter Kuile wins George Macdonald Medal

LSTM’s Professor Feiko ter Kuile has been named as a joint recipient for the prestigious George MacDonald Medal. Awarded every three years jointly between the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene (RSTMH) and the London School of Tropical Medicine & Hygiene (LSHTM), it recognises outstanding individuals who have conducted research leasing to significant improvements of health in the tropics.

Professor ter Kuile was presented with the award at the RSTMH’s Annual General Meeting held in London alongside his co-recipient Professor Anthony Costello

He said: “I am truly delighted and deeply honoured to receive the George Macdonald Medal, and, I admit, a little surprised. I have spent most of my working life in Africa, so it is really nice to know our work in Kenya and the region is appreciated.

“For 30 years I have been lucky to work with wonderful colleagues at the KEMRI Centre for Global Health Research in Kisumu and at CDC and LSTM. Seeing a generation of Kenyan scientists trained with us go on to lead their own studies and grants has been a real joy.

“Looking back, some of our studies changed WHO policy, but you never know in advance which will. For every study that moves the needle, several do not. For malaria chemoprevention in pregnancy, we still rely on drugs recommended over 25 years ago. Nevertheless, these are exciting times for malaria control research, with new approaches and new tools. The team in East Africa and the next generation of scientists are well placed to make a real difference in reducing the burden of malaria.”

Feiko is Professor of Tropical Epidemiology at LSTM, and his research focuses on the epidemiology of malaria and the evaluation of new interventions for the for the control of malaria in children and pregnant women.

Keyword search
Robert Allan

Composition as documentary practice

This project sets out to bring the techniques of documentary film and theatre to music composition. Robert is supervised by Dr Richard Baker, Dr Laura Bowler and Prof Andy Lavender.

Chris Allard

An investigation into the techniques and devices of contemporary jazz guitar

This project investigates  the techniques and devices of contemporary jazz guitar stylists Kurt Rosenwinkel, Wolfgang Muthspiel, Julian Lage and Jesse Van Ruller. Chris is supervised by Dr Paul Newland and Malcolm Miles.

Chris is a member of staff teaching in the Jazz department.

Andy Asante

The new sound of Jazz

This project explores the influence of African rhythm on 21st Century American jazz. Andy is supervised by Dr Richard Baker and Robert Mitchell. 

Beatrice Baumgartner-Cohen

Drawing in and on Guildhall: what happens when I take my practice of live graphic recording out of its commercial context?

Beatrice is trying to find out what happens when you move the practice of Live Graphic Recording from a commercial context into the world of collaborative theatre and back again. Beatrice is supervised by Emily Orley and Susannah Henry.

Olivia Bell

‘Making it real’: the role of the librettist in the creation of verbatim opera.

An exploration into the uses of verbatim text in operatic performance, positioning the librettist as mediator, collector and co-curator. The project also looks at the ethical implications of using verbatim material, including from marginalised communities and as trauma writing, and the ongoing relationships between writer, subject, composer and performer.

Margarida Castro

Towards fearless elite music performance training

Drawing on Psychological Safety research from fields like organisational and elite sports psychology, Margarida is studying how a climate of candor and interpersonal risk-taking is best applied and fostered within elite music performance training for optimal learning and performance. Margarida is supervised by Dr Karen Wise and Sophia Jowett.

Jo Chard

Shifting power: democracy in cultural organisations

This project will explore the practice and impact of developing community-based decision making models by researching community and activist organising methods, and transposing these approaches into cultural organisations as higher forms of governance. It will also examine the barriers that exist in creating non-hierarchical decision-making models within the UK's economic, political and funding landscape, and aim to provide frameworks and tools that could improve the establishment of more democratic approaches. Jo is supervised by Dr Simon Bayly and Dr Toby Young.
Amanda Collins

Adaptability and Transition of the Newly Qualified Music Therapist: Tools, Tea and Therapy

Amanda's research focuses on the newly qualified music therapist and their transition into professional life. Amanda is supervised by Dr Kate Jones and Donald Wetherick.
Amy Crankshaw

Earth music: exploring ways to integrate experiences of physical natural environments and their materialities with composition practices. 

Amy's research explores ways to musicalise physical experiences of naturally occurring materialities, phenomena, and environments through the practice of music composition. Amy is supervised by Prof Julian Philips, Dr Hollie Harding and Nell Catchpole.

Robert Crehan

Amateurism and Post-Disciplinary Practices in Music Composition.

This project looks at how approaches to music composition vary between 'amateur' and 'professional' composers, and what techniques, aesthetics, or concepts are gained or lost through learning and experience.

Postdoctoral Research at Guildhall

Postdoctoral Research Fellows are an increasingly important part of the research environment of the School: they receive mentoring from established staff, supervise doctoral research, contribute to research-orientated teaching, and form a vital part of large externally-funded projects hosted at the Guildhall School, including 'Texting Scarlatti: Composition, Reception, Performance' (PI Prof. Sir Barry Ife) and ‘Immersive Opera’ (PI Dr Toby Young, himself a former Postdoctoral Fellow).

 

Our Fellows have been funded from a number of sources, including the Arts and Humanities Research Council, the Barbican, and the Esmée Fairbairn Foundation, as well as directly by the School. Opportunities supported by the School are advertised on the vacancies page, as well as Jobs.ac.uk.

Postdoctoral Research Fellows
Dr Anita Datta

Anita Datta is a performer and researcher working at the intersection of the arts and inclusivity. She is a Research Associate on the Immersive Opera research project, funded by the UKRI's Future Leader Fellowship scheme.

Dr Jasper van der Klis

Jasper van der Klis is currently the Postdoctoral Research Fellow on 'Texting Scarlatti: Composition, Reception, Performance' funded by the Leverhulme Trust. He completed his PhD at the School in 2022.

Dr Malte Kobel

Malte Kobel is a musicologist and Leverhulme Early Career Research Fellow, currently looking at Ornette Coleman’s musical thought, focussing on questions of composition, sociality and music as philosophical practice.

Dr Amy Stebbins

Amy Stebbins is a writer and director, specialising in opera and new media. She is a Research Associate on the Immersive Opera research project, funded by the UKRI's Future Leader Fellowship scheme.

Former Postdoctoral Research Fellows
Dr Kate Bennett Wadsworth

Kate Bennett Wadsworth (former Leverhulme Early Career Research Fellow) is a cellist and gambist devoted to historical performance of all periods, with a special research interest in 19th-century performing practice.

Dr Jo Gibson

Jo Gibson was a Postdoctoral Research Fellow at the Guildhall School from 2022 - 2023, working on the AHRC-funded project ‘Music for social impact: Practitioners’ contexts, work and beliefs’.

Dr Matthew Harle

Former Research Fellow (2016-2019), Matthew Harle was a Barbican-Guildhall Archive Curator who was part of the team assembling and interpreting the Barbican’s archives for the Centre’s 40th anniversary in 2022.

Dr Patrick John Jones

Patrick John Jones is a composer and researcher who worked on a practice-based Leverhulme Early Career Fellowship, ‘Sounding the archive: composition as translation and adaptation’, from 2020-2023.

Dr Maia Mackney

Maia Mackney joined the School in 2019, as the Postdoctoral Research Fellow who was part of a research collaboration between Guildhall and the Barbican Centre. She is now our Postdoctoral Innovation Fellow, focussing on Evaluation.

Dr Alessandro Mazzola

Former Postdoctoral Research Fellow (2020 - 2022), Alessandro Mazzola worked primarily on the AHRC-funded project ‘Music for social impact: Practitioners’ contexts, work and beliefs’.

Dr Tom Overton

Former Research Fellow (2016-2019), Tom Overton was a Barbican-Guildhall Archive Curator who was part of the team assembling and interpreting the Barbican’s archives for the Centre’s 40th anniversary in 2022.

Dr Toby Young

Toby Young joined the School as a Leverhulme Early Career Research Fellow working primarily on ‘Transforming the operatic voice’. He is now a UKRI Future Leader Fellow, following a £1.4m award in 2023 for 'Immersive Opera'.
